_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401878758.overall: Leeds have gone five league games without a win and Daniel Farke admits his attack is 'still struggling a little bit'. Tottenham under Roberto De Zerbi arrive on three straight wins, and this is their last game before the international break. Leeds expect Joe Rodon back, but Farke has 'major doubts' over Anton Stach (foot), Noah Okafor (adductor) has only done individual work, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin had a small foot setback. Spurs get Rodrigo Bentancur back from a three-match ban and Tosin Adarabioyo back in training, but are still without Bergvall, Sávio, Xavi Simons, Odobert and Mudryk.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Leeds have scored twice in five games, and with Stach and probably Okafor missing and Calvert-Lewin not fully fit, they have little attacking threat. Spurs have conceded once in three games. Maddison is expected to start for Spurs, but they are still missing Simons, Odobert and Mudryk, so we expect a fairly tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Spurs should see more of the ball, and Leeds will rely on wing-backs Bogle and Gudmundsson for width. That matches what the model already expects.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, already raised for John Brooks's record. Bentancur's return from his red-card ban adds some bite to the Spurs midfield, but nothing else in the news moves the number either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. Farke says his attack is still struggling, and with Okafor and Stach doubtful, Leeds may not test Spurs often. Spurs are also short of wide attackers, so the total looks slightly high.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. A blunt Leeds attack facing a Spurs defence that has conceded once in three games points to fewer clear efforts than the model expects.

401882812.overall: Málaga are bottom with 5 points after five draws and six defeats, and have not won at La Rosaleda this season. Juanfran Funes calls it 'a test of persistence and resilience' and is hoping for a first win. Racing (16th, 11 points) lost 0-3 to Real Madrid and have lost all five away games. They are without Álvaro Mantilla and Andrés Martín, while Málaga have fitness doubts over Carlos Puga, Joaquín Muñoz and Pablo Martínez on top of the long-term absences.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Racing's away record (five defeats out of five) and Málaga's need to win both point to goals. Against that, Málaga have scored only six in their last six, and Racing are without Andrés Martín, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 13.2 corners, already very high. Málaga should push hard at home, with David Larrubia running at defenders, but that is already in the model, and the doubts over Puga and Joaquín Muñoz could take some width out of their play.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, raised now that Isidro Díaz de Mera has been named referee. A tense game for a winless team at the bottom fits that number, but the news gives no reason to go above it.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.9 shots. Funes expects a 'partidazo' against a Racing side that likes to play, and Racing have been open away from home. Without Andrés Martín, Racing will produce less, which balances things out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both defences have let through plenty of chances, which the model already reflects, and the team news does not clearly change the picture.

401874791.overall: Frosinone (Massimiliano Alvini) are sixth with 20 points after back-to-back wins and come in as the in-form side. Cagliari have been stuck on 13 points under Fabio Pisacane. They are missing Mina, Nzola, Fadera and suspended Obert, which leaves Mendy as the lone striker in a 4-3-2-1. Frosinone are without striker Antonio Raimondo, and Birligea is slightly favoured over Bobcek to replace him.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already lowered for Raimondo and Nzola being out. Frosinone's attack is flying and Cagliari have leaked goals, but Cagliari have few forwards to pick from, so the model's middle ground looks right.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners. Frosinone's 4-2-3-1 with Ghedjemis and Kvernadze out wide should earn corners, which the model already accounts for.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already raised a lot for referee Giovanni Ayroldi. Cagliari's winless run adds some pressure, but nothing in the news points clearly either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.8 shots, pushed up mainly by Frosinone's last six games. Cagliari play with a single striker (Mendy) and Frosinone are without Raimondo, so that total looks stretched.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both sides are missing a first-choice striker (Nzola for Cagliari, Raimondo for Frosinone), which points to a slightly lower figure.

401874811.overall: Torino (Ignazio Abate) have lost two in a row after three straight wins, and will be without Rolando Mandragora, who is aiming to return after the international break. Lecce (Eusebio Di Francesco) are fighting relegation after three straight defeats, including 5-1 at Frosinone. Pierotti, Berisha, Geubbels and Monteiro are listed as unavailable. Torino are expected to play a 3-4-1-2 with Vlasic behind Adams and Simeone.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Lecce's defence has been leaking, but their attack is weakened without Pierotti, Berisha and Geubbels. Torino are without Mandragora in midfield, so the two effects roughly cancel out.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Torino's wing-backs and Lecce's 4-3-3 are their usual shapes, and none of the team news points clearly to more or fewer corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.1 cards, which looks low for a Serie A game with this much at stake. Lecce are in a relegation scrap after three straight defeats and Torino need a reaction after two losses, so we expect a scrappy game. Ermanno Feliciani referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots. Torino should have the edge at home with Adams, Simeone and Vlasic, while Lecce's weakened attack balances that out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. The team news doesn't give a clear reason to move away from the model.

401884737.overall: Promoted Paderborn have drawn 0-0 in their last two league games and have won both home games this season. Adi Hütter calls them 'extremely unpleasant' at home, with a high press and a 5-3-2, and says Frankfurt must bring intensity and win lots of duels in a match he calls 'richtungsweisend' (one that sets the direction). Mario Götze is out with an ear infection and captain Robin Koch (knee knock) is in a race to be fit. Hütter has not said whether Ebnoutalib and Burkardt will start together.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Paderborn come in on two goalless draws and Hütter expects a grind, with high pressing and lots of duels. Frankfurt are also without Götze as a creator, so we expect a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Paderborn's 5-3-2 relies on wing-backs for width, which the model already reflects, and nothing in the team news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards, which looks low for a game like this. Paderborn press high and Hütter says Frankfurt must win the battle of duels, which tends to bring fouls and bookings. Bastian Dankert referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 30 shots. Paderborn's recent games have been low-event (two 0-0 draws), and Frankfurt are without Götze, so a stop-start, physical game should produce fewer shots than the model expects.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Two goalless draws in a row for Paderborn and Götze's absence for Frankfurt point to slightly fewer clear efforts.

401884740.overall: Bayern are still without Vincent Kompany, who is recovering from a viral inflammation of the brain membranes, so Aaron Danks leads the team again. Danks said Díaz, Gnabry, Musiala and Saibari remain out, Pavlovic is fit to start, and Alphonso Davies may be rested after a long run of midweek games. Mainz lost three games in a week. Urs Fischer wants his side to get back to basics, with 'running, duels, intensity, aggression', and he has to rebuild his back line without the suspended Posch and Mwene.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Mainz have conceded 17 in their last six, and with Posch and Mwene suspended Fischer has to bring in Stefan Bell or Rael Nakuzola at the back, which points up. Bayern are missing four attackers and Danks is managing workloads before the international break, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Bayern should have most of the ball against a Mainz side focused on defending, and nothing in the news moves the corner figure either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Fischer has asked for aggression and hard duels, and local reports say Mainz plan to be 'eklig' (nasty to play against), with a reshuffled defence chasing Bayern's attackers. That points to more fouls and bookings than usual. Robert Schröder referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots. Bayern have scored 18 in their last six and face a weakened Mainz back line. Possible rotation (Davies may be rested) and the missing attackers stop us going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 shots on target. A makeshift Mainz defence should concede chances, but Bayern's thin front line and their tired legs after Tuesday's win at Atlético balance that out.

401884744.overall: Leipzig lost 3-2 to Manchester City on Wednesday, their fourth straight midweek game. Martín Demichelis said the squad trained for only 25 minutes afterwards and he wants 'a fresh team on the pitch', so rotation is likely. Antonio Nusa, who has started every league game, came off against City with muscle problems: Demichelis said Nusa was 'at his limit' and will be assessed on matchday. Manuel Baum's Augsburg are winless in six league games but their matches are open: 3-2, 2-2, 4-3, 1-1 and 1-2 in the last five. Augsburg are without the suspended Juma Bah plus Banks and Brackelmann.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Augsburg's recent games have been high-scoring, and their defence is missing Bah, Banks and Brackelmann. A tired, rotated Leipzig possibly without Nusa pulls the other way, so we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Leipzig should still control territory at home, and the news gives no clear reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. Augsburg's reshuffled back line could lead to some tactical fouls, but there is no specific news on discipline. Daniel Schlager referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots. Demichelis described the workload as extremely high and plans to change his line-up, and Nusa, his most dangerous winger, may sit out. A tired, rotated Leipzig is likely to produce fewer attempts than usual.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target. Augsburg's weakened defence and Leipzig's fatigue roughly cancel out.

401884745.overall: Dortmund are unbeaten in the league (five wins, three draws) but are without Serhou Guirassy (muscle strain), Emre Can, Lerma and Konstantelias. Fabio Silva, who has six goals and three assists this season, is expected to lead the line, and Kovac could rotate after Tuesday's Champions League win over Betis. Promoted Elversberg are seventh, have scored and conceded 16 goals each in eight games, and are expected to use a 4-2-3-1 with Keidel and Poreba shielding the defence.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already lower than yesterday's figure. Without Guirassy, Dortmund have scored only seven league goals in their last six. But Elversberg have scored three or more in four of their eight league games and concede plenty, and Fabio Silva is in form, so we now stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.1 corners. Elversberg's double pivot is set up to deny Dortmund space through the middle, which should push the home side wide and into crosses. That fits the model's high Dortmund corner count.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. There is no specific news on discipline. Harm Osmers referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Dortmund should still pile up attempts at home, though without Guirassy the quality is likely to drop more than the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Dortmund lose their main finisher in Guirassy, and possible rotation and tiredness after the Champions League could cost them sharpness. Elversberg's compact midfield should force more efforts from distance.

401878760.overall: League leaders Arsenal (24 points, eight wins in nine) host promoted Hull, who are 11th and winless in six league games (four draws). Arteta confirmed Ezri Konsa is fine after being taken off as a precaution in Prague, Ben White is back, and Saliba is in contention, so only Saka (thigh/quad, out until after the break) and the suspended Dowman are missing. Hull have seven players injured, including goalkeeper Jack Butland, who one report says could still play, and Matt Crooks is suspended.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Arsenal control games rather than run up scores, and Saka's absence removes their main creator. Hull have scored only 11 in nine league games and draw a lot. Sergej Jakirovic admits he found no weakness in Arsenal and wants to make the game uncomfortable for them, which points to a low-scoring match.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10 corners, most of them Arsenal's. Arteta wants his side to attack from the start, and Hull, with seven players injured, are likely to sit deep. That points to Arsenal pinning them back and forcing plenty of blocked crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, mostly from Hull. Hull lose their combative midfielder Matt Crooks to suspension, and a one-sided game in which Arsenal keep the ball usually produces few flashpoints. Farai Hallam referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. A deep Hull block suits a high Arsenal shot count, and Arsenal's defence is close to full strength. Missing Saka pulls the other way, so the model's figure looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Without Saka, Arsenal lose their main source of chances from the right, and a packed Hull defence should block plenty. Hull rarely test goalkeepers away from home.

401879241.overall: Fulham (15th, 9 points) host Newcastle (13th, 11 points), who lost twice to Everton in a week, in the league and the Carabao Cup. Reports already link Matthias Jaissle's job to other names. Newcastle are without Joelinton, Livramento, Jaouen and the suspended Jacob Ramsey. Lewis Miley and Matias Fernandez-Pardo are back in training but not certain to play. Alvaro Arbeloa says Fulham must keep believing in how they play but need to improve their finishing. Fulham have scored one goal or fewer in each of their last six games, and one report says Ryan Sessegnon is suspended after a red card.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Fulham have scored only five in their last six, and Arbeloa himself names finishing as the problem. Newcastle have six in six and are missing midfielders. Two nervous sides near the bottom half point to a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say about 11 corners, split fairly evenly. Nothing in the team news clearly moves this figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Robert Jones referees a tense game, and Newcastle had Ramsey sent off last time out. Without Ramsey and Joelinton, though, Newcastle lose two of their most combative midfielders, so we stay close to the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Newcastle's makeshift midfield, likely Willock and the 18-year-old Sean Steur, should create less. Jaissle says he will accept more long balls to avoid losing possession, which usually means fewer shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Both sides' finishing has been poor: Newcastle are well below their expected goals and Fulham's attack has stalled. That points to fewer efforts on target than the model expects.

401882813.overall: This is Eder Sarabia's first game in charge of Espanyol, who are 14th on 11 points after sacking Manolo González following a cup exit to Sestao River. Sarabia is serving the last game of a touchline ban carried over from Elche, so the site's 'Eder Sarabia suspended' entry is a coaching ban, not a player absence. Sarabia says he will change things gradually and wants a brave, proactive team that keeps the solidity of the previous regime. Antonio Hidalgo's Deportivo are eighth on 14 points. The round goes ahead despite the players' union asking for it to be postponed after the death of Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Espanyol are without striker Kike García (torn hamstring tendon) and winger Jofre Carreras, who is listed out with an adductor problem. They have scored only five in their last six. Deportivo lose centre-back Bright Ede but also forward Zakaria Eddahchouri (hand fracture), and Hidalgo is being careful with Aubameyang. With a new coach whose first priority is not to lose, we expect a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10.7 corners, split almost evenly. Sarabia wants Espanyol on the front foot, but he says he will make changes gradually rather than overhaul the side in his first week. Nothing in the news moves the total clearly.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, about normal for LaLiga, with Alejandro Quintero González refereeing. A new coach and a nervous home crowd near the bottom could add intensity. Against that, Espanyol lose Roger Hinojo to a yellow-card suspension and the weekend's sombre mood may calm things, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Sarabia's proactive approach could raise Espanyol's attempts, but they are missing Kike García and Carreras, and Deportivo are short in attack too. The two effects roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9 shots on target. Both sides are missing a first-choice forward: Kike García for Espanyol and Eddahchouri for Deportivo, while Aubameyang is being managed. Espanyol's finishing has been poor, so we expect slightly fewer efforts on target than the model.

401875555.overall: Danny Buijs's Fortuna Sittard are sixth and unbeaten in six league games after a 1-1 draw at Feyenoord last weekend. A win would lift them above AZ into fifth, but they have taken only seven points from 15 at home. Henk Brugge's Telstar are near the bottom. They beat Utrecht 4-2 but then went out of the KNVB Beker to Almere City in midweek, and they are without Patrick Brouwer, Rui Mendes and Gerald Alders.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. Fortuna have the lowest possession in the league and play a compact, counter-attacking game. Their unbeaten run includes several draws and narrow wins, including last week's 1-1 at Feyenoord. Telstar's away form is poor, and they are missing midfielder Patrick Brouwer and forward Rui Mendes, although Tyrone Owusu has been scoring.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10.7 corners. Fortuna's low-possession style may give Telstar more of the ball and a few extra corners, but nothing in the news moves the total clearly.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards, with Dennis Higler refereeing. We found no news of discipline problems or bad blood between these sides, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Fortuna rarely have the ball and rely on a few clear chances rather than lots of attempts. Telstar played a cup tie in midweek and are short of attacking options without Mendes and Brouwer.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, which is high. Fortuna are efficient but take relatively few shots, and Telstar have struggled to create away from home. A total just under 10 looks more realistic.

401885398.overall: The match was postponed on Saturday after dense fog at the Choupana, and it is now set for 15:30 on Sunday after Académico de Viseu insisted on the league's 30-hour rule. Storm Bruna is forecast to bring heavy rain, thunderstorms and gusts of up to 90 km/h to Madeira on Sunday, and Nacional president Rui Alves said forecasts were worse than for Saturday. Only players registered for the original date can play. Saturday's announced line-ups had Nacional in a back three under João Henriques. Viseu are on a six-match league winning streak and are unbeaten away.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. João Henriques has set Nacional up to defend first, and Bruno Pinheiro admits they have 'closed the doors' to their goal. Heavy rain and strong wind from storm Bruna should also disrupt Viseu's short-passing game, which points to a low-scoring match even though Viseu are in strong form.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Viseu may have most of the ball against Nacional's deep block, and a wet pitch can lead to scrambled clearances. On the other hand, the model gives Nacional the larger share, which seems unlikely if they sit deep. These factors roughly cancel out.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, with Pedro Ramalho refereeing. A heavy pitch can bring mistimed tackles, and there is some ill feeling between the clubs over the rescheduling, but a patient game against a deep defence doesn't usually produce many bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.8 shots, which looks high. Nacional's back three and wing-backs are set up to limit openings, and Pinheiro expects a slow, patient build-up. Storm conditions with gusts of up to 90 km/h make clean shooting chances harder to create.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Viseu's coach expects it to be hard to create clear chances against Nacional's new set-up, and Nacional's attack has been weak. Heavy rain and wind should further reduce accurate shooting.

401874974.overall: An Emilia derby between two sides in good spirits: Parma won 3-0 at Atalanta on Monday in Alberto Gilardino's first game, and Raffaele Palladino's Bologna have won three in a row. Neither side played in Europe this week, and the absentees match the site's list (Bernabé and Drobnic for Parma; Holm, De Silvestri and Enem for Bologna).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Parma are expected in a 3-5-2 that defends deep, which fits a low total, but both sides arrive scoring freely, so nothing pushes us either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Nothing in the team news changes how either side builds attacks, so we stay with the numbers.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. It's a local derby between two teams with momentum, and Palladino expects a physical Parma that presses high at times, so we lean a little higher. We found no recent record for referee Luca Zufferli, so this rests on the occasion alone.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.6 shots. Bologna's front three (Bernardeschi, Odgaard, Cambiaghi) should see most of the ball, as the numbers already expect, and we found nothing to move it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.1 shots on target. No news points either way.

401884743.overall: Stuttgart lost a heated 2-0 game at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday, though they created plenty (Leweling hit the post twice), and Hoeneß says some rotation is possible. Bremen are 5th, unbeaten in seven and six points ahead of Stuttgart, with Füllkrug the league's top scorer. Bremen are missing eight senior players, but Niklas Stark (listed as out on the site) is not on their absentee list and may return. Karazor is a doubt after a knock in Istanbul.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Bremen arrive with a depleted squad but in form behind Füllkrug, and Stuttgart's midfield is thin without Stiller and possibly Karazor, which tends to open games up. We lean slightly higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners. Stuttgart should have most of the ball at home, which the numbers already reflect, so we stay level.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already a high figure. We found nothing on referee Sören Storks or on bad blood between the clubs that would push it further.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.9 shots. Stuttgart created a lot even in defeat in Istanbul and won 4-2 at Leverkusen last time out in the league, and Bremen like to counter through Füllkrug, so we lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target. Possible rotation after the midweek game cuts against the higher shot count, so we stay level.

401882811.overall: Osasuna, back under Jagoba Arrasate, are 15th and rely heavily on Budimir (8 goals). Aimar Oroz and Jorge Herrando are out rather than doubtful, as several reports confirm. Edin Terzić's Athletic have won three league games in a row but have only Iñaki Williams as a fit senior striker, since Guruzeta and Sannadi are injured. Nico Williams and Yuri are back in training.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Both coaches expect a tight game, Terzić pointing out that Osasuna's games have had few goals. Osasuna lose Oroz, their main creator, and Athletic have no striker depth, so we lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Athletic's direct, transition style and Arrasate's plan to go long at times balance out, so we stay with the numbers.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Terzić expects a game of many duels in a 'hot' El Sadar, and Athletic will hold a very high line, which tends to bring tactical fouls on the break. We lean slightly higher, though we found no recent record for referee Sesma Espinosa.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots. Nothing in the news moves the volume either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. With Oroz out for Osasuna and Athletic's forward line thin, we lean a little lower on quality chances.

401878757.overall: Forest are 19th under Oliver Glasner and have not scored in any of their four home league games, despite taking the second most shots in the league. City won 3-2 at RB Leipzig in midweek after losing their last two league games (at Villa, home to Brighton), and Dias and Gvardiol may return. Reports disagree on whether Forest's Igor Jesus is back from a calf injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Forest have failed to score in every home league game this season and convert about 4% of their shots, so the home side's share looks generous. City's chances keep us from leaning far, so this lean is mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Forest shoot often from range, and City should dominate the ball, two habits that tend to produce blocked shots and corners. We lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. One profile describes Samuel Barrott as a low-key referee who lets play flow, so we lean slightly lower. That comes from a single source.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots. Forest have the second-highest shot count in the league even while losing, and City carry the league's best xG, so we lean higher on volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Forest's high volume comes with poor accuracy, which offsets the higher shot count, so we stay level.

401875552.overall: ADO Den Haag sacked coach Robin Peter this week, and assistant Levi Schwiebbe takes charge for this one. Maurice Steijn is reported as the likely successor but was not confirmed as of Friday. ADO are 17th and have lost three in a row. Sparta, near the drop zone, won 3-2 at Groningen and are expected to set up with a back five. Toornstra went off early at Groningen and one report lists him only as a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Sparta's expected back five and the caution of a relegation six-pointer, with a stand-in coach on ADO's bench, point to a tighter game than the attacking ratings suggest. We lean slightly lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Nothing in the news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. It's a South Holland derby with relegation at stake and a caretaker coach for ADO, so we lean higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots. ADO at home should push, but Sparta's back five will limit space, so we stay with the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. A packed Sparta defence and two struggling attacks suggest fewer clean chances, so we lean a little lower.

401876411.overall: Liam Rosenior's Paris FC are 4th after a 3-1 win over Monaco, in which they outshot them 19 to 9 with a high press. Will Still's Auxerre are 14th, lost 5-1 at Strasbourg and have conceded in five straight games, though they are unbeaten in three at home. Dioubaté is suspended after his red card there. L'Équipe reports Labeau-Lascary is back, while Tuanzebe is a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Auxerre's defence has leaked in every recent game and Paris FC arrive attacking with confidence, so we lean higher. Both previous league meetings were draws, the last 0-0, which keeps the lean mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Nothing in the news changes either side's approach to wide play.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already above average. Auxerre's red card last week hints at frustration, but we found nothing on referee Marc Bollengier, so we stay level.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. Paris FC took 19 shots against Monaco with a high press, and Auxerre have been giving up chances, so we lean higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. Paris FC put 10 on target against Monaco, and Auxerre's defence is short of bodies without Okoh and possibly Tuanzebe, so we lean higher.

401885402.overall: Alverca (10th) have lost three in a row without scoring, including a cup exit at Tondela. Casa Pia are 17th with the joint-lowest goal tally in the league (5), and all seven of their points came away from home. Alverca coach Sérgio Ferreira wants a compact low block, and Casa Pia's Filipe Coelho admits finishing is their main problem. Alverca keeper Jhonatan Luiz is a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Alverca have not scored in three games, Casa Pia have scored only five all season, and Alverca plan to sit in a compact block. We lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners. Estoril at home should push for a first win, but nothing specific in the news moves the corner count.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, with Barcelona taking most. That fits the expected shape: Barcelona dominate the ball, Atlético counter through Julián Álvarez. We stay with the site.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. Atlético rarely give up clear chances (8 conceded in 11), and Barcelona are without Olmo and Rodri, so we lean slightly below the site.

401885397.overall: Rio Ave are 16th with two league wins and the most goals conceded (23), having conceded at least twice in each of their five home games; Vasco Seabra took over in October. Braga (8th, 14 points) beat Famalicão 3-0 under new coach Franclim Carvalho but have not scored in their last five away games, and drew 0-0 at Aarhus on Thursday despite 26 shots. Rio Ave's André Ntoi is suspended; Braga have Barcia and Gabriel Silva back, with only Niakaté out.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, with Braga expected to score twice. Rio Ave's home defence is the worst in the league, but Braga haven't scored away in five games. These pull in opposite directions, so we stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Braga had 26 shots against Aarhus without scoring, and Carvalho wants pace, intensity and attacking play; a side dominating without finishing tends to win plenty of corners. We lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Rio Ave are fighting relegation and have had a red card recently (Ntoi), but we found nothing specific on referee Cláudio Pereira, so we keep the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, already raised by Braga's recent volume. Braga had 26 shots in Denmark on Thursday and face the league's leakiest defence, and Carvalho says Braga must be the favourites and attack. We lean slightly higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Braga create a lot but their finishing away from home has been poor, so we stay with the site.

401885401.overall: Benfica, five points off the top and the league's top scorers (27), have won seven straight and beat Lech Poznań 3-1 in the Europa League on Thursday. Estrela (12th) have lost four league games in a row and have not kept a clean sheet in 12 matches. Marco Silva said Benfica play three games in seven days and he is rotating within positions; he also named Lenglet in the squad, though the site lists him as missing.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with Benfica expected to score most of them. Benfica score freely and Estrela haven't kept a clean sheet in 12, but Silva plans some rotation after Thursday and admitted clean sheets have been a weakness, which keeps Estrela in it. We stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, mostly Benfica's. Silva expects Estrela to drop into a back five in a mid-low block, which usually means Benfica corners, and that's what the site already shows.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. Silva called Estrela combative and their ground hard to play at, but we found nothing on referee António Nobre's style this season, so we keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. Rotation could take a little off Benfica's intensity, but Vangelis Pavlidis (10 league goals) is expected to start after resting on Thursday. These roughly balance.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Benfica have scored 20 goals in their last seven games and Estrela concede in every match, so we lean slightly higher on Benfica's accuracy against a struggling defence.

401883136.overall: Early view: Leganés are 17th with one point from their last seven league games, and Luis Carrión is still without a win since replacing Rubén Albés, the latest a 1-3 home defeat by Albacete in which Álvaro Morata missed an 86th-minute penalty. Burgos arrive third after Álex Forés's late winner against Celta Fortuna, but without Jon Karrikaburu (hamstring tear) and David González. Team news and the referee will be added the day before the Friday-night kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leganés have conceded seven in their last two league games (4-3 at Valladolid, 1-3 at home to Albacete) and have to chase this one at Butarque. Burgos have scored twice in three of their last four league games, even if Sergio Francisco says he does not want an end-to-end match.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean a little higher: Leganés had roughly two-thirds of the ball and 17 shots against Albacete, and Burgos used a back five against Castellón, a shape that invites crosses and blocked shots. Most of the extra should come at the Burgos end.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already a high figure, and I lean higher still. Leganés have just had Rubén Pulido and Yassine Kechta suspended at the same time, the site lists Francisco Montero as banned after a red card, and a side one point above the drop zone meets a Burgos team its coach calls the hardest-running in the league. No referee has been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots. I lean lower: Sergio Francisco wants Burgos to have the ball and has ruled out an open game, so 12.5 away shots for them looks generous. Leganés should take most of the attempts, as they did with 17 against Albacete.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target and I see no strong reason to move it. Leganés create volume but finish poorly (no league win since 20 September, Morata's missed penalty last week), while Burgos are efficient rather than prolific, with Forés and Curro on four goals each.

401883114.overall: Early view: Castellón, second with the best defence in the division (five goals conceded in 12 games), have not played a league match since 1 November after asking to postpone their game with Eibar following the death of their former striker Jesús de Miguel. Valladolid have won two in a row, including their first away win of the season at Sporting, but Fran Escribá is without the injured Juanmi Latasa, Guille Bueno, De Rooij and Dani Pérez, and Iván Alejo is suspended after also limping off in Gijón.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Pablo Hernández's Castellón defend by keeping the ball and have let in five goals in 12 games, and Valladolid are without their striker Latasa and the suspended Alejo. Valladolid's last two games had seven and three goals, but against Leganés's weak defence and a Sporting side that had to chase the game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I stay close to that. Castellón use the full width of the pitch and should have most of the ball, which adds corners at one end, but Valladolid are unlikely to win many at the other with their attack depleted. The two effects roughly cancel out.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. I lean a little higher: LaLiga's own figures show Valladolid with 34 yellows and four reds against Castellón's 22 and two, and a home side chasing a possession team usually commits the fouls. The site also lists Castellón's Matías Orozco as banned after a red card, so the visitors are not spotless either.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. I lean lower: Castellón's possession game limits what opponents get, and 12.6 home shots for Valladolid looks high with Latasa and Alejo missing. Castellón themselves were held to one goal and few clear chances at Burgos last time out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: a Castellón defence that has conceded five league goals all season, and a Valladolid attack missing its main striker. Castellón may also be short of sharpness after two weeks without a league game.

401883134.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad II (Sanse) are 19th but won their last home game 1-0 against Girona with an 86th-minute goal from Lander Astiazaran; they also had a Monday-night game at Sabadell this week that is not yet in these numbers. Sporting are seventh but lost 1-2 at home to Valladolid despite 20 shots, and will be without Juan Otero (sent off for a second yellow in added time) on top of what one report called seven absences, with Alejo Sarco a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean higher: Sanse's home games at Zubieta have gone 2-4 against Almería, 2-3 against Granada and 1-0 against Girona, and Sporting's last four league games had three, two, four and three goals. Losing Otero hurts Sporting's attack, but Sanse's defence concedes plenty.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I stay there. Both sides like the ball (Sanse had 59 per cent possession against Girona, Sporting 63 per cent against Valladolid), so neither should sit back and concede a flood of corners. Expect a fairly even split.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Sanse committed 27 fouls and took six yellows in their win over Girona, and Sporting finished their last game with Otero sent off for a second booking. Both sides have shown they collect cards when games get stretched.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and that looks about right. Sporting took 20 shots against Valladolid and Sanse 14 against Girona, so both can generate volume, but Sporting's thin attack without Otero and possibly Sarco stops me going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Sporting's 20 shots against Valladolid brought one goal, and losing Otero and perhaps Sarco removes two of their forwards. Sanse's 14 shots against ten-man Girona produced a single goal in the 86th minute.

401883118.overall: Early view: Leaders Almería won 1-0 at Girona through Miguel de la Fuente's eighth league goal and now face an Andorra side playing for the first time since the Tenerife match in which their goalkeeper Jesús Owono collided with Jesús de Miguel, who died the next day. Andorra asked for their game with Mallorca to be postponed because of the squad's emotional state; Owono faces a long ban (the disciplinary code allows four to 12 games, per one report), and the site also lists Lautaro De León and Efe Akman as suspended.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean a little lower: Almería's last three league games have been tight (1-0, 1-1, 2-2), and Andorra, without the suspended De León (three goals) and after a deeply difficult fortnight, may offer little going forward. A stand-in goalkeeper for the banned Owono is the main reason not to go lower still.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I see no reason to move it. Almería should have the ball and most of the corners, while Andorra are likely to sit deeper than usual on the road; against the site's split those two effects broadly cancel out.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, with Andorra expected to take 3.6 of them. I lean lower: after the events in Tenerife every Andorra challenge will be watched closely, and I expect a careful game from a squad one report described as deeply shaken. Almería, top of the table and at home, have little reason to make it physical.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean lower: Almería's win at Girona came from just 12 shots per side, and their recent league games have been controlled rather than wide open. Andorra's attack is weakened by the bans to De León and Akman.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, a high figure for this division. I lean lower: Almería's recent games have been tight and Andorra are missing a regular scorer. If Andorra's replacement goalkeeper looks shaky Almería may test him often, which is the main risk to this lean.

401883135.overall: Early view: Mallorca have not played since beating Cádiz 2-1 on 2 November, because their trip to Andorra was postponed, so Luis García's side arrive rested and sixth with a game in hand. Córdoba under Iván Ania have one defeat in their last five league games and beat Ceuta 3-0 last weekend, but finished the game before that, at Celta Fortuna, with nine men. Adrián Fuentes, Segunda's top scorer for much of the autumn, is Mallorca's main threat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Córdoba have scored in each of their last four league games (1-0, 2-0, 2-2, 3-0) and Mallorca's last two home games produced four and three goals. Fuentes is in form and Mallorca are fresh after a two-week gap.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I lean a little higher: Córdoba build a lot of their attacks through crosses (Fran Escribá asked Valladolid for aggression specifically to stop them), which earns corners even away, and Mallorca will have plenty of the ball at Son Moix.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. I lean a touch higher: Córdoba ended the Celta Fortuna game with nine men after Álex Martín's straight red and Isma Ruiz's second yellow, a side that can lose its discipline when under pressure. With no referee named yet, I would not go far above six.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots and I leave it there. Mallorca at home and Córdoba's cross-heavy approach both produce attempts, but Mallorca's habit of drawing games (four draws in 12) suggests they are not always dominant. Nothing in the news moves the figure clearly.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, which fits two sides with reliable finishers in Fuentes and Eder García. Mallorca's long break could mean fresh legs or a slow start, so I lean neither way.

401883115.overall: Early view: Real Oviedo changed coach on 9 November, two days after winning 2-1 at Cádiz: one report says Raúl González, the former Real Madrid striker, replaces Julián Calero in his first senior job, with Santi Cazorla possibly joining his staff, and this is his debut at the Tartiere. Girona, relegated from LaLiga last season, are eighth after two 1-0 defeats in a row (at Real Sociedad II and at home to Almería) but still have Vladyslav Vanat and Yáser Asprilla on five goals each.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean higher: Oviedo's last four league games had three, five, four and three goals, and Raúl has asked for a team that gives everything, which points to a front-foot debut. Girona have the strongest attacking names in the division and missed good chances in both recent defeats (Vanat hit the post against Almería).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean slightly higher: Girona will push to end a two-game losing run and have the wide quality (Carles Pérez, Asprilla) to lift their 3.9, while Oviedo should play with intensity in front of a new coach.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards. I lean a bit higher: Girona picked up three yellows in the first half alone at home to Almería and had David López sent off at Zubieta, and a new coach's debut in front of the Tartiere crowd should bring an intense, physical game.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots and I hold there. Girona's shot count has dipped (eight with ten men at Zubieta, 12 against Almería), but a home side playing for a new coach pushes the other way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target and I stay there. Girona's forwards are the best in the division on paper but have scored none in two games, and Oviedo's attack, without Chris Ramos (cruciate injury), has a centre-back, Carlos Domínguez, as top scorer with five.

401883113.overall: Early view: This is Tenerife's first match since striker Jesús de Miguel died on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra's goalkeeper at the Heliodoro; their game at Granada was postponed and the club held a public tribute at the stadium on 7 November, so the emotional context outweighs anything in the numbers. Álvaro Cervera's side had drawn four in a row before that, while bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) have lost five straight and, per one report, appointed Sergio Lobera on 8 November, so this is likely his first game in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I stay close to it. Ceuta concede more than two a game, which points up, but Tenerife have been a draw team (three 1-1s and a 2-2 in a row) and an emotionally heavy day is hard to read. Lobera's first aim will probably be a more organised Ceuta.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners and I leave it. Tenerife should have more of the territory against a side that has lost five in a row, but the site already gives them the larger share, and a new coach's first priority is usually to make his team compact.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I lean lower: in the first game at the Heliodoro since the club's tribute to De Miguel, I expect both teams to avoid flashpoints, and Ceuta under a brand-new coach are unlikely to start with a niggly approach. Dani Martín's suspension (listed by the site) also removes one Tenerife booking risk.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.7 shots. I lean higher: Ceuta have conceded 30 goals in 13 games, the most in the division, and lost 0-3 at Córdoba last weekend, so Tenerife's 11.9 looks low against the league's worst defence.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I lean higher, driven by Tenerife's side: Ceuta's defence has been breached 30 times and Enric Gallego has eight goals. Ceuta's share should stay modest; they have scored once in their last three league games.

401883116.overall: Early view: Granada have won five league games in a row under Pacheta but have not played in the league since 1 November because their home game with Tenerife was postponed. Las Palmas changed coach in late October; one report says Albert Sánchez won his debut 3-2 at Oviedo, and Jesé (four goals) has just renewed. Las Palmas also had a round-13 home game against Eldense that is not yet in these numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Granada's winning run has been built on narrow scores, with clean sheets in three of the five, and none of the last five meetings between these clubs produced more than three goals. Las Palmas's new coach is also still settling his side.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners and I keep it there. Granada are happy without the ball (Eldense had 59 per cent of it against them last time out), so their 5.3 may be a little high, but Las Palmas should get more than 3.9 if they have the ball. The total looks about right.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and I see no clear push either way. Las Palmas have collected cards steadily (32 yellows and two reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), which the site already reflects in their 3.2, and Granada's 1.9 fits a side that sits off the ball and wins narrowly.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots, with Granada expected to take 14.9. I lean lower: Granada were outshot 13-8 at Eldense and still won, so their results come from efficiency rather than volume. Two weeks without a league game may also blunt their sharpness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I lean lower: Rubén Alcaraz's winner at Elda was Granada's first shot on target of the second half, and recent meetings between these sides have been short of chances.

401883117.overall: Early view: Eibar are fourth but have not played since a 1-1 draw with Almería on 31 October, after their trip to Castellón was postponed, and have one league win in their last five after a club-record winning streak. Cádiz are 20th and have lost two in a row under Borja Jiménez, who replaced Albert Celades in late October, per one report; they also lost Javi Castro to injury at home to Oviedo.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar are described as the side with the least ball in the division and win by keeping games tight, and four of the last five meetings ended 1-0 to one side. Cádiz have scored only once in each of their last two league games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, with 5.4 for Eibar. I lean slightly lower: a side that plays with little of the ball rarely builds the sustained pressure that wins corners, even at home, and Cádiz under Jiménez only pushed forward after half-time changes in their last game.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean higher: Aranbarri has publicly asked his players to recover the aggressiveness they lacked, and a Cádiz side in the relegation zone, beaten twice in a row, will have to fight for every second ball. Cádiz at 3.4 looks plausible; Eibar at 1.9 looks low.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 17.5 for Eibar. That looks high for a team that plays with so little of the ball; I expect Eibar to take fewer, better chances and Cádiz to get around ten. Two weeks without a league game adds to the case for a slower match.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the goals and shots: Eibar scored one goal or none in each of their last three league games, and Cádiz have been blunt away from home (one goal at Mallorca, none at Granada).

401883137.overall: Early view: Two mid-to-low-table sides that both like the ball. Javi Calleja's Eldense lost their last two league games without scoring before a round-13 trip to Las Palmas whose result is not yet in these numbers; Ferran Costa's Sabadell are 12th, had a Monday game at home to Real Sociedad II, and will be without Óscar Sanz through a yellow-card ban.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals and I agree with a low figure. Eldense have not scored in their last two league games and Sabadell average about a goal a game for and against. Sabadell missing Sanz (two goals) takes a little away, but not enough to go lower than the site already is.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. I lean higher: Sabadell had 66 per cent of the ball and 25 shots at Albacete, the kind of pressure that piles up corners, and Calleja wants Eldense to keep the ball too (they had 59 per cent at home to Granada). Two sides pushing for territory should mean set pieces at both ends.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean lower: two possession-minded sides usually make for fewer tactical fouls, and Eldense's record (28 yellows and no reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures) is one of the cleaner ones. Sabadell's 3.1 away looks a touch high.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.0 shots. I lean higher: Sabadell took 25 shots at Albacete and Eldense 13 at home to Granada, and with both teams keen on the ball neither should sit in a low block for 90 minutes. Volume is likely; accuracy is the problem for both.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target and I leave it. Both teams create more than they convert: Sabadell's 25 shots at Albacete brought one goal, and Eldense's 13 against Granada none. More attempts than usual, but not many more on target.

401883305.overall: Early view: Albacete have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria, who replaced Alberto González in early October per one report, the latest a 3-1 win at Leganés, but they are still 21st. Celta Fortuna, Celta's reserve side, are 16th with a long absence list: one report names five injured players (Gavián, Somuah, Óscar Marcos, Anxo Rodríguez, Olmedo) and the site adds three yellow-card bans (Joel López, Enrique Ribes, Adrià Capdevila). This Monday-night game closes round 14.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, which is high but fits the context: Celta Fortuna lost 5-1 at Girona, conceded twice at Burgos and against Córdoba, and will field a patched-up defence again. Against that, Higinio Marín, who scored Albacete's penalty at Leganés, went off injured and José Corpas is still serving a three-match ban, so I hold at the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with 6.4 for Albacete. I lean lower: Etxeberria's Albacete have been winning by scoring early and defending, not by dominating, with only five shots in their win over Sabadell and 12 to Leganés's 17. Celta Fortuna will probably have more of the ball than the split suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards. I lean higher: Albacete press high under Etxeberria, which brings fouls, Corpas was sent off two games ago, and three Celta Fortuna players have already reached five yellows. A Monday-night game between 21st and 16th should be scrappy.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. I lean lower, mainly on Albacete's side: they have been outshot in their recent wins, and 16.2 home shots does not match how they play under Etxeberria. Celta Fortuna, who took 17 shots at home to Córdoba, can contribute their share.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Albacete's wins have come from few attempts (both of their goals against Sabadell went in off opponents), and Celta Fortuna's attack is short of options with Óscar Marcos, one of their top scorers, injured.

401883112.overall: Early view: A game between 18th and 17th, 11 days away. Andorra's first games after the Tenerife tragedy will shape this one; goalkeeper Jesús Owono faces a ban of four to 12 games under the disciplinary code, per one report, while Efe Akman's one-match yellow-card ban should already be served at Almería. Leganés's Francisco Montero should likewise have served his ban against Burgos, and Luis Carrión needs results quickly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leganés have conceded eight goals in Carrión's three games (1-1, 4-3, 1-3), and Andorra are likely to have a stand-in goalkeeper with Owono suspended. Both sides sit near the drop zone and need wins, which tends to open games up late.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I stay there. Leganés's possession game (about two-thirds of the ball against Albacete) should give them more than the 3.8 the site has, but that is likely to come out of Andorra's 5.6 rather than add to the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. Leganés have had several suspensions lately and the stakes are high at the bottom, but Andorra will be careful after a month under scrutiny, so I hold at about six until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots, with 17.5 for Andorra. I lean lower: that split looks lopsided against a Leganés side that keeps the ball and took 17 shots in its last game, and Andorra's attack may still be without Lautaro De León if his ban runs on. I expect a more even, lower total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target, with 6.4 for Andorra. I lean lower for the same reason: Andorra's home share looks too high for this matchup. Leganés's own accuracy has been poor (one goal from 17 shots against Albacete, plus Morata's missed penalty).

401882299.overall: Early view: Sabadell, who like to dominate the ball (66 per cent and 25 shots at Albacete), host a Granada side that has won five league games in a row with efficient, low-possession football. Granada's postponed game with Tenerife still has to be rescheduled, and Óscar Sanz should be back for Sabadell after his ban. Both teams play in round 14 first, so this view will move.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and I agree with a low total. Granada have three clean sheets in their last five league games and Sabadell average about a goal a game at both ends. Sabadell holding the ball against a Granada side happy to wait suggests a slow, low-scoring game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I lean higher: Sabadell's habit of keeping the ball and shooting often (25 attempts at Albacete) should earn more corners than their 5.1, and Granada were content to let Eldense have the ball and the pressure that came with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, with 3.2 for Sabadell. I lean lower: the side with most of the ball usually commits fewer fouls, and Sabadell will be that side. Granada may pick up a few for slowing the game, but a total near five looks more likely.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, with 17.1 for Sabadell, which matches their style. Granada were outshot 13-8 in their last game and still won, so 9.5 for them is fair. I see no reason to move the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target and I leave it. Sabadell's volume comes with modest accuracy, and Granada take few but clean chances (Alcaraz's header and Owen Emeka's late finish at Elda). Worth revisiting after both sides' round-14 games.

401883108.overall: Early view: A relegation six-pointer between 19th and 20th. Real Sociedad II (Sanse) host Sporting first; Cádiz, who have won one of their last five league games, go to Eibar in round 14. Borja Jiménez won his debut against Ceuta but has lost both games since, so the pressure on both sides should be high by kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean a little higher: Sanse's home games have been open (2-4 against Almería, 2-3 against Granada), and Cádiz have scored in all three games under Jiménez, including a late Urko Izeta header at home to Oviedo.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I keep it. Sanse should have more of the ball at home, as they did against Girona, and Cádiz push hard in second halves when behind, as they did against Oviedo. Nothing suggests a big swing either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. I lean higher: Sanse committed 27 fouls and received six yellows against Girona, and a bottom-of-the-table game where neither side can afford to lose should be tense from the start.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, with 16.9 for Sanse. I lean slightly lower: Sanse took 14 shots against ten-man Girona, so nearly 17 against Cádiz looks generous, and six-pointers between nervous sides often slow down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, which fits two teams who score a fair amount but not efficiently. I hold here until both have played in round 14.

401882301.overall: Early view: Second-placed Castellón, who visit Valladolid first, have the best defence in the division and have beaten Sporting 4-0 and Tenerife 5-0 at Castalia. Eldense under Javi Calleja host Sabadell first and had lost their last two league games without scoring before their round-13 trip to Las Palmas. Matías Orozco, listed by the site as suspended, should have served his ban at Valladolid.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, almost all of them Castellón's. I stay close to that: Castellón can run up scores at home (4-0, 5-0) but also grind out narrow results, and Eldense have gone two league games without a goal, so the total depends almost entirely on how ruthless the hosts are.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Pablo Hernández's side use the full width of the pitch from back to front and should spend long spells in Eldense's half, which pushes their 5.6 up. Eldense want the ball under Calleja, but at Castalia they are unlikely to keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, with 3.1 for Eldense. I lean lower: Eldense have one of the cleaner records in the division (28 yellows and no reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), and Castellón win the ball back through possession and quick recovery rather than by fouling.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and I agree. Castellón will take most of them; Eldense managed 13 at home to Granada but will get far fewer at Castalia. Nothing in the news moves the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Castellón's forwards (Israel Suero six goals, Ousmane Camara four) are efficient and the site already gives them the bulk; I keep the figure until the round-14 news is in.

401883107.overall: Early view: Tenerife play Ceuta first in their emotional return after the death of Jesús de Miguel, so this view will be revisited. They had drawn four in a row under Álvaro Cervera before the tragedy, and Mallorca are also draw-prone (four draws in 12), with their own postponed game at Andorra still to be given a new date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals and I lean lower still: Mallorca's last three away league games ended 1-1, 1-1 and 0-0, and Tenerife's run before the tragedy was four draws in a row, three of them 1-1. Adrián Fuentes is the one player who can break a tight game open.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners and I keep it. Neither team has been dominant in recent weeks and both have been content to take draws, so there is no sign of a lopsided game that would push the count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Mallorca's 3.5 looks a little high for the away side, but with no referee named and Tenerife's mood after the Ceuta game unknown, I hold at the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.0 shots, a low figure that fits two cautious sides. I see nothing yet to move it; Tenerife's first game back against Ceuta will say more about their attacking intent.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with the goals: Mallorca's away games have been short of clear chances (a 0-0 at Girona and two 1-1s), and Tenerife lean heavily on Enric Gallego's eight goals.

401882300.overall: Early view: Córdoba, 10th, host an Oviedo side that will be playing only its second game under Raúl González, who one report says replaced Julián Calero on 9 November. Oviedo have one of the best away records in the division (13 points), while Iván Ania's Córdoba have won three of their last four league games and score regularly at El Arcángel.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already high, and I agree. Oviedo's away games have been lively (2-1 at Cádiz, 2-2 at Almería, 2-1 at Ceuta) and Córdoba have scored in each of their last four league games, so a low-scoring game would be the surprise.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with 7.3 for Córdoba, which suits a team that attacks through crosses (Fran Escribá made stopping them his priority). I would not go higher than the site because Oviedo, strong away, will not simply sit back.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards. Córdoba ended a recent away game with nine men and Raúl has asked Oviedo for unconditional commitment, so the case for a high figure is there; I hold rather than go higher until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, very high for this division. I lean lower: Oviedo's best away results have been compact ones (they led 2-0 at Cádiz and then held on), and Raúl's first weeks in charge are likely to put structure first, which caps the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower with the shots: Córdoba's crossing game produces many attempts, but headers from crosses often miss the target, and Oviedo's attack is without Chris Ramos (cruciate injury).

401882298.overall: Early view: Sporting, seventh, return to El Molinón after losing 1-2 to Valladolid there despite 20 shots, and should have Juan Otero back once his ban is served at Real Sociedad II. Las Palmas, under Albert Sánchez since late October per one report, have Jesé and Sandro Ramírez available. Both play in round 14 first.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Sporting's last four league games averaged three goals, and Las Palmas's last four had five, one, three and four. Sporting's home attack, with Otero back, should be stronger than it was against Valladolid.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean higher: Sporting had 63 per cent of the ball and 20 shots in their last home game, the kind of dominance that piles up corners, and Nicolás Larcamón's side should take a similar approach here.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. Las Palmas collect cards steadily (32 yellows and two reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), which the site already reflects, and this is not a derby or a high-risk fixture, so I see no reason to move it.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. I lean higher: Sporting took 20 on their own against Valladolid at El Molinón, and Las Palmas under their new coach have played open games (3-2 at Oviedo). A total in the high twenties is plausible.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target and I keep it. Sporting's volume has not turned into accuracy (one goal from 20 shots last time), so I do not follow the shots lean all the way.

401883109.overall: Early view: Girona, relegated from LaLiga last season, have lost two in a row 1-0 but still have the most attacking quality in the division (Vanat, Asprilla, Stuani, Carles Pérez). Eibar are fourth and play with less of the ball than anyone, per one report; their postponed game at Castellón still has to be rescheduled and could add a midweek fixture before this one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean higher: Girona's home games have included a 5-1 against Celta Fortuna and a 2-0 against Andorra, and Eibar's last three away league games had two, four and four goals. Girona's finishing should recover after Vanat hit the post against Almería.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I lean higher: Eibar concede possession by design, so Girona should spend long spells in their half, and Girona's wide players (Carles Pérez, Asprilla) give them the crossing and shooting that earn corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Girona collected three first-half yellows against Almería and Jokin Aranbarri wants an aggressive Eibar, but Girona usually control home games, so I hold at the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, with 18.1 for Girona, which fits a home side facing a team that gives up the ball. Girona's recent shot counts were low (eight with ten men, 12 against Almería), but Eibar's style should give them more room, so I keep it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Girona's quality should turn volume into accuracy, but Eibar's deep defending forces efforts from distance, so I see no clear lean.

401883304.overall: Early view: Celta Fortuna, 16th, have a long injury list (five players named by one report) but should get Joel López, Enrique Ribes and Adrià Capdevila back once their yellow-card bans are served at Albacete. Valladolid have won two in a row under Fran Escribá but are without Juanmi Latasa, Guille Bueno, De Rooij and Dani Pérez, and Iván Alejo's fitness after limping off in Gijón is uncertain.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already high, and I stay there. Celta Fortuna's games have been open (4-1, 1-5, 2-2 and 1-2 in recent weeks) and Valladolid's last two had seven and three goals, but Valladolid's missing striker Latasa stops me going higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, with Valladolid expected to win more than the hosts. That fits a patched-up Celta Fortuna side spending time defending, and I see no news to change it.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. I lean higher: LaLiga's figures show Valladolid with 34 yellows and four reds in 13 games, one of the heavier records in the division, and three Celta Fortuna players have already reached five yellows. Two open sides tend to produce cards in transition.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots and I keep it. Celta Fortuna took 17 at home to Córdoba and Valladolid 15 at Gijón, both consistent with the site's split.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Valladolid's attack is without its main striker, and Celta Fortuna's 17 shots against Córdoba brought two goals, so their volume does not always mean accuracy.

401883111.overall: Early view: Burgos, third, are strong at El Plantío and Sergio Francisco wants control rather than an open game, though Jon Karrikaburu is out with a hamstring tear. Albacete have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria (they host Celta Fortuna first), but José Corpas should still be suspended here (a three-match ban, per one report) and Higinio Marín went off injured at Leganés.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Burgos's last three home league games ended 2-1, 1-1 and 1-0, and Francisco has said he does not want an end-to-end game. Albacete win with few chances and could be without Higinio Marín.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners and I keep it. Burgos should have more of the ball at home, but Albacete under Etxeberria press high rather than sit deep, so the territory should not be completely one-way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, low for this division. I lean higher: Albacete's high press commits fouls, Burgos describe themselves as the hardest-running team in the league, and Corpas's recent red shows Albacete's edge. Five or six looks more likely than four.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. I lean lower: Albacete took only five shots against Sabadell and 12 at Leganés, and Burgos's controlled home games are not shot-heavy. The site's 10.3 for Albacete looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the shots and goals: Burgos's home wins have been narrow, and Albacete's goals have come from few efforts (both goals against Sabadell went in off opponents).

401883110.overall: Early view: Bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) host leaders Almería in the last game of round 15. One report says Sergio Lobera returned to Ceuta as coach on 8 November, so this would be his second league game; Almería host Andorra first, and Marcos Luna, who limped off at Girona, should have served his yellow-card ban by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, with 1.4 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta have scored once in their last three league games and Almería's recent league games have been tight (1-0, 1-1, 2-2). Almería should be favourites, but a high-scoring game needs Ceuta to contribute more than they have been.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with 6.0 for Ceuta. I lean lower: the bottom side winning six corners at home to the leaders looks generous, even if Lobera wants Ceuta to keep the ball more. Almería's share should be higher and Ceuta's lower, with a slightly smaller total.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. A desperate home side against the leaders points up, but a new coach usually starts by demanding discipline, so I hold at the site's number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, with 18.9 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta have not shown that kind of volume (they failed to score at Córdoba or at home to Sporting), and Almería's games are more controlled, with 12 shots each at Girona.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Ceuta's attack has been blunt and Almería's recent wins have been narrow. Miguel de la Fuente, the league's top scorer, is the likeliest source of efforts on target.

401882297.overall: Early view: Albacete have turned a dreadful start around under Joseba Etxeberria, who replaced Alberto González in early October, with three straight wins including 3-1 at Leganés, but they are still 21st. Tenerife have drawn four in a row and are dealing with the death of striker Jesús de Miguel after the 2 November match with Andorra. Corpas should be back from his three-match ban by round 16, and Dani Martín's ban should be served against Ceuta on 15 November, so the brief's absence list will likely be out of date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly higher: Albacete have scored seven in their last three under Etxeberria's high-pressing, vertical set-up but still have the second-worst defence (24 conceded), and Tenerife's away games have averaged over three goals. Tenerife's run of 1-1 draws keeps me from going far above the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean a little lower: Álvaro Cervera's Tenerife are happy without the ball (26% possession and no corners against Andorra), and Etxeberria's Albacete attack fast in transition rather than camping in the final third, as at Leganés where they had five corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. I lean higher: Albacete picked up six yellows at Leganés with Etxeberria's aggressive pressing, and Tenerife had three yellows and Dani Martín's red against Andorra. A relegation-threatened home side chasing a fourth straight win adds to the fouling.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.8 shots. I lean lower: Tenerife produce very few shots (five against Andorra) and lean on Enric Gallego, who has scored around half their goals, while Albacete took only 12 at Leganés even in a 3-1 win.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.3 shots on target. I see nothing to move it: Albacete were efficient at Leganés (five on target from 12) and Tenerife put two of five on target against Andorra, which fits a total close to the site's number.

401883106.overall: Early view: Almería are top on 29 points after a 1-0 win at Girona and are unbeaten at home (five wins, one draw) under Xavi García Pimienta, with Miguel de la Fuente the division's top scorer. Sporting are seventh but lost 2-1 at home to Valladolid, had a long injury list before that game and saw Juan Otero sent off. Marcos Luna's yellow-card ban should be served against Andorra on 14 November, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: Sporting's away games have averaged about 2.3 goals and they have won four of six on the road by staying compact, and Almería's last two matches finished 1-1 and 1-0. Almería at home are the likelier scorers, but a big total needs Sporting to open up.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. I lean slightly lower: García Pimienta's Almería build through the middle and took only two corners at Girona and three at Eibar, and Sporting's nine corners against Valladolid came with 62% of the ball, which they are unlikely to have at the leaders' ground.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. Sporting were booked heavily and had Otero sent off against Valladolid, but that was a high-risk home game; Almería picked up three yellows at Girona and two at Eibar. That leaves me close to the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Recent games support it: Girona-Almería had 26 shots, Eibar-Almería 30 and Sporting-Valladolid 35, so a total in the high 20s looks right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Almería had only three on target at Girona and one at Eibar, and many of the shots in these teams' games end up blocked, so I would expect fewer than ten on target.

401883105.overall: Early view: Cádiz are 20th and on their third coach of the season, Borja Jiménez, who took over in late October; they won his debut against Ceuta but then lost 2-1 at Mallorca and 2-1 at home to Oviedo despite creating more. Córdoba are tenth under Iván Ania after a 3-0 win over Ceuta, though one preview listed five injured players. This Andalusian meeting carries real pressure for Cádiz, who have only two home wins.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Córdoba's games are open (22 scored and 22 conceded, and their away games average over three goals), while Cádiz's home games have averaged just over two; the two pull in different directions, so I stay near the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners. That looks right: Córdoba won 11 corners against Ceuta and attack wide, and Cádiz under Borja Jiménez pushed hard enough against Oviedo to win six, so both sides should contribute.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Cádiz-Oviedo produced nine yellows, Córdoba had Isma Ruiz sent off for two yellows and Alex banned for violent play after their trip to Celta Fortuna, and a regional game with Cádiz fighting relegation should be tense.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Cádiz took 15 against Oviedo and Córdoba 14 against Ceuta, and both teams commit players forward, so a total close to the site's number fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Cádiz got only four of their 15 shots on target against Oviedo, with six blocked, and their finishing has been the main problem all season.

401883104.overall: Early view: a top-four meeting, with Eibar fourth on 23 points from 12 games and Burgos third on 24 after a late 2-1 win over Celta Fortuna. One report (4 November) says Eibar lost both left-backs, Juan Bernat (torn hamstring) and Imanol García de Albéniz (torn calf), and have Unai Elgezabal out with an ankle sprain. Eibar also have a postponed league game at Castellón and a Copa tie to fit in, so the schedule could be tight by late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. I lean higher: Eibar's home games have averaged nearly three goals, Burgos keep scoring late (Álex Forés in the 86th minute last time), and Eibar's patched-up back line without Bernat and García de Albéniz is a weakness.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I lean higher: Burgos won 10 corners against Celta Fortuna under Sergio Francisco, and Eibar's makeshift full-backs could invite pressure down the flanks, while Eibar themselves had 20 shots and five corners against Almería.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Eibar had three yellows against Almería and Burgos only one against Celta Fortuna; it is a big game at a tight ground, but neither side has been especially card-prone lately, so I stay with the number.
