Angers (16th) have scored only nine goals in 10 games and have one point from their last five league games, while Monaco's league form has been flat despite their European wins.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean lower: Monaco have scored 13 and conceded 11 in 10 league games, and Angers' attack is the second-weakest in the league. A 1-0 or 2-0 Monaco win looks most likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. That looks about right: Monaco average 4.1 corners but should get more at home against a team that sits deep, and Angers win plenty when they get forward (6.0 a game per Statz). No strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. That fits two sides that do not foul much: Angers are 15th for fouls (10.4 a game) and Monaco 8th. I would wait for the referee before changing it.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots, with 16.5 for Monaco. I lean lower: Monaco average only 11.7 shots a game (14th) and had five at Le Mans. Even at home against a weak side, 14 or 15 Monaco shots is more realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. I lean lower: Monaco average 4.2 on target and Angers 3.1 (17th). Seven or eight looks more likely.

401876385.overall: Early view: Lens host the bottom side four days before a Champions League home game with Bodo/Glimt, so Yannick Cahuzac may rest a few players but should still field a strong side at Bollaert. Le Havre (18th, 2 points, 22 conceded) were in turmoil after Didier Digard's suspension and the chairman's resignation, and their bench may look different by December.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean higher: Lens score most of their league goals at home and Le Havre concede 2.2 a game, including three or more in three straight league games in October. Le Havre's Josh Maja had scored in back-to-back games before the Lorient defeat, so a 3-1 type score is plausible.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Lens win 5.8 corners a game (2nd) and Le Havre 5.3 (7th). Lens should have long spells of pressure at home.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Le Havre foul a fair amount (14 a game) but Lens are mid-table, so I stay near the site. It depends on whether Le Havre's coach sets them up to sit deep.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots. Season figures (Lens 12.9, Le Havre 16.1) back that up, so I stay put. If Lens dominate as expected, their share will be larger than the site's 14.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Lens are 4th for shots on target (5.4 a game) and Le Havre's defence allows plenty of clear chances. Ten or eleven is realistic.

401876381.overall: Early view: Paris FC (3rd) host Le Mans a week before their Paris derby with PSG, with no European games to manage. Le Mans (15th) are hard to beat at home but weaker away, where they lost 2-0 at Troyes; both sides commit plenty of fouls.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I stay with it: Paris FC's games average about 2.7 goals and Le Mans' about 3.1. Paris FC's main threat Lassine Sinayoko had fitness worries in early November, which is worth rechecking.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners. I lean lower: Paris FC win 3.6 corners a game (16th) and Le Mans 3.0 (17th), two of the lowest rates in the league. Seven or so looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean higher: Le Mans are 3rd for fouls (14.8 a game) and were described as over-aggressive at the back, and Paris FC are 6th (13.9). This has the makings of a stop-start game.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots. Season averages (Paris FC 13.5, Le Mans 10.7) sum to about 24, so I stay close. Le Mans shoot far less on the road than at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Paris FC average 4.9 on target and Le Mans 3.6, which fits the site's figure. No reason to move it yet.

401876379.overall: Early view: Strasbourg's form (five defeats in six league games before the break) has put coach Hugo Oliveira under pressure according to one report, so the bench could look different by December. Lorient arrive as one of the hardest teams to score against, especially away, but also the league's least threatening attack.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean lower: Lorient have conceded eight in 10 and kept clean sheets in most of their away games, and they rarely score more than once. Strasbourg's games are open, but Lorient usually drag opponents into low-scoring matches.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners. I lean lower: Strasbourg win the fewest corners in the league (2.5 a game) and Lorient are 15th (3.7). This could be one of the lowest corner counts of the weekend.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean slightly lower: Lorient commit very few fouls (9.3 a game, 17th) and Strasbourg are mid-table. Three bookings looks the most likely number.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. I lean slightly lower: Lorient average 10.3 shots a game (17th) and Strasbourg 12.6. Lorient's deep defending also tends to cut the home side's count.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. I lean lower: Lorient are last in the league for shots on target (2.8 a game), so most will come from Strasbourg (4.9). Seven or so is more realistic.

401876377.overall: Early view: Lyon visit Troyes on a Sunday lunchtime between Europa League games (Lillestrom on 26 November, Union SG on 10 December), so rotation is possible but should not be heavy. Troyes (17th) have scored only seven goals all season, while Lyon have one of the best defences (9 conceded) but were beaten 2-0 at Brest before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Troyes score 0.7 a game and Lyon concede 0.9, and Troyes have become harder to break down (two clean sheets and a 1-0 loss at PSG before the break). A narrow Lyon win is the base case.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. That looks fair: Lyon keep the ball (69% at Brest, with eight corners) and Troyes win a decent number of corners for a bottom side (5.7 a game per Statz). I see no reason to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Troyes (12.3 fouls a game) and Lyon (11.6) are both close to the league average, so I stay with the site. A Troyes side chasing a result late could add one.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.2 shots, with Troyes taking more than Lyon, which looks unlikely. I lean slightly higher overall: Lyon average 12.8 shots a game and should dominate the ball, and Troyes average 13.1. I would expect Lyon to have the larger share.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. Troyes (3.3 a game, 16th) and Lyon (4.6) sum to about eight, so I stay with it. Lyon's finishing was poor at Brest (two on target from 10 shots).

401876380.overall: Early view: a Breton derby at Roazhon Park, four days before Rennes host Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League. Rennes' games have been the most open in the league (42 goals in 10), and Brest are in good form under Julien Lachuer, with both sides in the league's top four for shots per game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, already high. I stay with it: Rennes score and concede about two a game, and Brest score 1.8, so goals are likely at both ends. Esteban Lepaul's fitness (ankle) and Brest's centre-back injuries are the things to check nearer the time.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, with 6.5 for Rennes. I lean slightly lower: Rennes average 5.7, and Brest's direct, low-possession play produces few corners (one against Lyon). Nine or ten rather than eleven.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean higher: it is a derby, and Brest are 4th in the league for fouls (14.2 a game). Derby intensity plus Brest's physical approach makes five or more bookings plausible.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots. I lean higher: Rennes average 16.2 shots a game (3rd) and Brest 16.1 (4th), which sums to over 32. Even allowing for a tighter derby, the high 20s look likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean higher: Rennes are 2nd (6.0 a game) and Brest 3rd (5.7) for shots on target. Both goalkeepers should be busy.

401876383.overall: Early view: Marseille host Nice in a rivalry fixture between two sides in the top six, with Celta Vigo to come in the Europa League four days later. Marseille went into the break on five straight league wins under Bruno Genesio and Nice had won four of five under Olivier Pantaloni, though Nice's injuries (Antoine Mendy, Laurent Abergel, Moise Bombito) need checking.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I stay close to it: Marseille score 2.2 a game, the league's best, and Nice 1.5, while both concede between 1.2 and 1.4. Amine Gouiri's form is the main reason not to go lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I lean slightly higher: Nice win 5.7 corners a game (4th) and Marseille 4.5, and both like to keep the ball. Ten looks a fair middle.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean slightly lower: despite the rivalry, these are two of the cleaner teams in the league (Marseille 11.2 fouls a game, Nice 9.9). The referee and the occasion could change that, so this is a mild lean.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. I lean lower: Marseille average 13.2 shots and Nice 12.1, which sums to about 25. With Celta four days later, Marseille may also take a more controlled approach once ahead.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. I lean lower: Marseille average 4.7 on target and Nice 4.0. Nine is a more natural figure for two possession sides.

401882805.overall: Early view: Athletic open the post-break round on Friday night with no fit centre-forward: Gorka Guruzeta is out for the season with a cruciate tear, Asier Hierro has a knee ligament injury and Maroan Sannadi is still recovering, so the Williams brothers carry the attack. Espanyol play only their second league game under Eder Sarabia, who replaced the sacked Manolo González and started with a 0-0 draw against Deportivo in which his side kept 64% of the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Athletic have no recognised No. 9 (Guruzeta, Hierro and Sannadi all injured), and Espanyol are without striker Kike García, who one injury list has out until December. Sarabia's first game ended 0-0 with keeper Ángel Fortuño unbeaten.

corners.text: The site expects 10.0 corners, 6.5 of them for Athletic. Sarabia wants Espanyol to keep the ball (they had 64% against Deportivo), which should cut into Athletic's territory, and without a target man Terzić's side cross less. Athletic took only four corners at El Sadar last time out.

cards.text: The model has 5.0 cards and I see no reason to move it yet. Espanyol picked up four yellows against Deportivo, mostly for dangerous play, while Athletic had just one at Osasuna; the referee, who will decide a lot here, is not yet known.

shots.text: The site expects 26.1 shots, 17.7 from Athletic. Athletic managed 16 at Osasuna, and with no striker more of their efforts will come from Sancet and Navarro outside the box rather than in volume. A Sarabia side that holds possession should also limit the number of Athletic attacks.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Losing Guruzeta and Hierro removes Athletic's main finishers in the box, and Espanyol landed few efforts on target against Deportivo. A total of 7 or 8 looks more likely than 9 or more.

401882806.overall: Early view: Alavés are winless in eight league games under Quique Sánchez Flores, whose job was already under scrutiny in October; they lost 6-1 at Barcelona before a deep-lying 0-0 at Sevilla. Deportivo (9th) are steadier under Antonio Hidalgo and have Aubameyang back from knee surgery, but they managed only five shots in their 0-0 at Espanyol.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Before the Sevilla draw, Alavés had scored only 5 and conceded 14 in seven games, and both teams drew 0-0 on matchday 12. Aubameyang's return gives Deportivo more threat, but he is just back from a meniscus operation and only played a half.

corners.text: The site expects 10.8 corners, 6.2 of them for Alavés. Sánchez Flores' side sat in a 3-5-2 at Sevilla and took four corners, and they have been short of attacking ideas. Neither side looks set to pin the other back for long.

cards.text: The model has 4.8 cards and I lean higher. Alavés committed 19 fouls and took three yellows at Sevilla, while Deportivo picked up four yellows at Espanyol, three of them for dangerous play. A home side short on confidence and under pressure tends to make it scrappy.

shots.text: The site expects 25.9 shots. Alavés had 9 at Sevilla and Deportivo only 5 at Espanyol, so both attacks are running cold. Deportivo's Eddahchouri (wrist) and Bright Ede are listed as doubts, which thins Hidalgo's options.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 on target. I lean lower because Alavés have struggled to create clear chances since September and Deportivo rarely tested Fortuño at Espanyol. Expect 6 or 7 rather than 9.

401882799.overall: Early view: Valencia (19th) go to Vallecas without José Luis Gayà, sent off against Real Madrid, and Jesús Vázquez, his usual stand-in at left-back, is a doubt with a muscle problem. Javier Aguirre's side took 2 of 21 points at Mestalla and ended the Madrid game with 26 fouls and a half-time tunnel scuffle. Rayo, under Beñat San José, are playing amid fan protests against president Presa that already got their home game with Athletic suspended in October.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly higher: San José's Rayo were among the league's top scorers and leakiest defences early in the season, and Valencia's left side is makeshift without Gayà and with Vázquez doubtful. Rayo's last two home games ended 3-0 one way and 0-3 the other, not tight draws.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners. Aguirre's Valencia play a deep 5-3-2 and took only two corners at the Bernabéu, so most of the play should be Rayo crossing into a packed box, which tends to produce blocks and corners. Rayo won six corners even in their defeat at Anoeta.

cards.text: The model has 5.1 cards and I lean higher. Valencia took four yellows and a red against Madrid, Aguirre himself was booked, and there was a tunnel scuffle at half-time. Add a relegation-zone visitor and a tense Vallecas crowd and six or more cards is realistic.

shots.text: The site expects 29.0 shots, 10.7 from Valencia. That looks generous for a Valencia side that managed four shots at Madrid and set up to defend. Rayo should take most of the shots, but one team doing the shooting makes a total in the high 20s a stretch.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target and I am close to that. Rayo should create decent chances against a weakened Valencia back line, but Valencia's own output on target is minimal, so the two effects roughly cancel out.

401882797.overall: Early view: a Seville derby with Betis 4th, eight points clear of Luis García Plaza's 6th-placed Sevilla, after a 2-0 win at Elche built on set pieces. Sevilla have struggled to score, drawing 0-0 with Alavés after Rubén Vargas missed a penalty, and they may be without Peque (hamstring) and Kike Salas, who went off injured. Betis then go to Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League on Tuesday, with Cucho Hernández working back from a calf injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Sevilla have been blunt (García Plaza publicly asked his strikers for more goals before the Alavés game, which still ended 0-0), and Betis are without Cucho Hernández. Derbies tend to be stop-start, so I expect two goals or fewer.

corners.text: The site expects 9.0 corners. Betis won eight corners at Elche and worked set pieces all week, with Bartra scoring from one; Antony's habit of shooting from range also brings blocks and deflections. Sevilla took five against Alavés with 60% of the ball.

cards.text: The model already has 7.0 cards, well above a normal game, because this is a derby. Sevilla had Manu Bueno sent off at Getafe two games ago, while Betis took no yellows at Elche. I'd hold at around seven until the referee is named.

shots.text: The site expects 27.4 shots. Betis had 18 at Elche, but derbies are broken up by fouls and Sevilla's attack lacks Peque's spark. I see the total in the low to mid 20s rather than above 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 on target. Betis' volume does not always reach the target (Antony went more than 30 league shots without a goal into late October), and Sevilla missed the target repeatedly against Alavés. Seven or eight is more likely.

401882798.overall: Early view: José Mourinho's Real Madrid have won eight in a row, including 3-0 at Valencia, and Vinícius has served his domestic ban, but Rodrygo, Raúl Asencio and Ferland Mendy are out and Mourinho has complained about how little rest his internationals get. Celta came into November with the league's best defence (seven conceded in ten games) but have five injured players, including Borja Iglesias. Madrid host PSV on Tuesday and Celta host Bournemouth on Thursday.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Celta under Giráldez are built on clean sheets and draws (six in their first ten games), and Madrid's international players will have little time to recover before kick-off. A 2-0 or 2-1 looks more likely than an open game.

corners.text: The site expects 8.9 corners. Mourinho's Madrid hurt teams in transition rather than through long spells of pressure, and they took only five corners while dominating at Mestalla. Celta prefer to keep the ball rather than sit in their box.

cards.text: The model has 4.0 cards. Celta are a tidy, ball-playing side (eight fouls and one yellow against Levante), and Madrid's three yellows at Valencia came from an unusually heated game. I expect three or four.

shots.text: The site expects 28.0 shots, which fits. Madrid had 19 at Valencia, and Celta still created 23 against Levante, so they will try to have some say even at the Bernabéu.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target. Celta's compact block forces opponents into lower-quality shots, and they had the league's best defensive record into late October. Madrid's front line is back to full strength with Vinícius, but I'd still expect about nine.

401882804.overall: Early view: leaders Barcelona won 2-1 at Atlético through Fermín López but are without Rodri (hamstring, several weeks) and have doubts over Dani Olmo and Christensen. Villarreal's Íñigo Pérez faced an ultimatum from the club after a 0-6 Champions League defeat to PSG; one report says the 2-0 win over Getafe saved his job. Renato Veiga is suspended. Both clubs play away in the Champions League on Wednesday (Barça at Sabah, Villarreal at Slavia Prague).

goals.text: The numbers say 4.5 goals, which is very high. Barça scored six against Alavés, but a Villarreal side fighting for its coach's job reacted to the PSG thrashing with a clean sheet against Getafe and is likely to defend deep. Without Rodri, Barça also lose some control in midfield.

corners.text: The site expects 10.7 corners. If Pérez sits deep after the PSG game, Barça will have long spells in the final third, with Lamine Yamal and Fariñas attacking the right flank. Pressure like that usually brings plenty of blocked crosses and corners.

cards.text: The model has 4.4 cards. Teams chasing Barça on the counter tend to stop it with fouls (Atlético collected four yellows to Barça's one), and Villarreal lose Renato Veiga to a ban. Five cards looks reasonable.

shots.text: The site expects 28.2 shots. Barça at home against a deep block should be near 20 on their own, and Villarreal under Pérez still try to play out. Getting to 30 needs nothing unusual.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target and I am close to that. Barça's volume points up, but Olmo is a doubt and Villarreal's packed defence should block a lot, so I stay near the site's figure.

401882800.overall: Early view: promoted Racing, coached by José Alberto, have the worst defence in the league (about 2.6 goals conceded a game) but score through Yassir Zabiri, and they just won 2-1 at Málaga for their first away points. Real Sociedad (5th) beat Rayo 1-0, but Ander Barrenetxea limped off with a hamstring problem and Mikel Oyarzabal missed the game ill. Matarazzo says his squad is tired after eight games in four weeks, and La Real play at Crystal Palace in the Europa League four days later.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which assumes both defences give a lot away. Racing do leak goals, but La Real have been conceding few chances lately and may be without Barrenetxea and Oyarzabal, their two most dangerous players. Over 2.5 still makes sense, but nearly four is too high.

corners.text: The site expects 11.4 corners. Racing average about five corners a game, and La Real took seven against Rayo in an open match. Ten or 11 is more realistic than 12.

cards.text: The model has 5.2 cards. Racing's Jorge Salinas is booked often (five yellows in ten games), and La Real took two against Rayo, so nothing points clearly either way until the referee is named.

shots.text: The site expects 31.3 shots. Racing average about 12 shots a game and La Real had 17 at home to Rayo, which adds up to the high 20s rather than over 30. A tired, rotated La Real away from home also points down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target. Racing put about 4.5 a game on target, and La Real's attack is weaker if Barrenetxea and Oyarzabal are missing. Expect about 9.

401882801.overall: Early view: bottom-half Osasuna (16th) host winless, last-placed Málaga, who lost 2-1 at home to Racing and finished with ten men. Two reports say coach Juanfran Funes's job is in danger, so a change during the break would make this a new manager's first game. Both sides have a midfielder suspended: Jon Moncayola (five yellows) for Osasuna and Adam Aznou (sent off) for Málaga, while Arrasate expects Herrando, Oroz and Del Castillo to be fit.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Málaga had scored nine in 12 league games and Osasuna are not prolific, relying on Budimir and late set pieces (Catena's header levelled with Athletic). A team at the bottom often tightens up in a new manager's first game, so I lean lower.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners. Arrasate's side attack down the wings with Moro, Rubén García and Barja crossing for Budimir, and Málaga defend in a back five. That mix usually brings a steady flow of corners for the home team.

cards.text: The model has 4.6 cards and I lean higher. Málaga collected seven yellows and a red against Racing, and Osasuna committed 19 fouls against Athletic. At the bottom of the table in a loud El Sadar, five or six cards is likely.

shots.text: The site expects 30.6 shots. Osasuna had 17 against Athletic and Málaga average about 11 a game, which adds up to the high 20s. Málaga in a low block will keep many Osasuna attempts from long range.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Málaga average only about three shots on target a game, and Osasuna's crossing game produces more headers than clean strikes. I see about eight.

401882803.overall: Early view: Getafe have taken all 12 of their points at the Coliseum, where they are unbeaten, but Bordalás says the squad is worn out by the Conference League, and Nemanja Gudelj is suspended. Atlético's run of eight straight wins ended with a 2-1 home defeat to Barcelona, and Cuti Romero has a new muscle injury. Atlético host Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday; Getafe go to Iberia Tbilisi on Thursday.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and I lean a little lower. Getafe at home shut games down, Atlético conceded only eight in their first ten league games, and the hosts lose Gudelj's experience at the back. A 1-0 or 1-1 type of game is the most likely.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. Bordalás' sides play long and slow the game down, with lots of throw-ins and free kicks, and Atlético rarely trap opponents in their box away from home. Eight or nine corners seems right.

cards.text: The model has 5.3 cards and I lean higher. Getafe against Atlético under Bordalás and Simeone is usually a scrappy, physical game, and Atlético just took four yellows against Barcelona. Six or more is realistic.

shots.text: The site expects 24.6 shots. Bordalás admitted his tired side was passing poorly at Villarreal, and Getafe have yet to score away from home, so their attack is limited. A broken-up game should keep the total in the low 20s.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 on target. With Uche and Juanmi out, Getafe's attack lacks a sharp edge, and Atlético's chances should be few in a tight game. About six on target seems right.

401882802.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between two clubs from the Valencia region, one point apart: Levante (17th) got out of the bottom three with a 0-0 at Celta thanks to seven saves from Mathew Ryan, and Elche (18th) are bottom-three after losing 2-0 at home to Betis. Elche are much stronger away (9 of their 10 points) than at home, but Martín Anselmi has a list of knocks in midfield. Luis Castro wants Levante more patient on the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. With so much at stake, neither coach wants an open game: Levante sat deep and played for the point at Celta, and Anselmi said before the Betis game that he does not want end-to-end matches. Elche's away games have included a 0-0 at Villarreal, so I lean lower.

corners.text: The site expects 8.9 corners. Elche like the ball and won nine corners even while losing to Betis, while Levante took one corner at Celta and defend deep. If Elche have most of the ball, their corner count should push the total up.

cards.text: The model has 4.4 cards. A relegation game between regional rivals usually has more fouls, and Elche took four yellows against Betis. Five cards looks closer than four.

shots.text: The site expects 29.7 shots. Levante had only six shots at Celta and Elche 13 against Betis, and nerves make games like this cautious. Mid-20s is more realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 on target. Elche failed to score from 13 shots against Betis, and with Lemar, Aguado and possibly Ali Houary missing they lack a midfielder who makes chances. Seven looks right.

401882791.overall: Early view: Levante play their second home game in five days after the Elche relegation clash, this time against a Racing side that is open at both ends: Racing concede the most in the league but have Yassir Zabiri, who has nine league goals. Racing's away form had been poor until the 2-1 win at Málaga, and Andrés Martín may be back from his hamstring injury by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, with 2.5 for Levante. Racing do give a lot away, but Levante's attack is limited (six shots at Celta) and Castro's side plays cautiously. Over 2.5 is plausible, but nearly four overrates Levante.

corners.text: The site expects 10.9 corners. Racing average about five corners a game, and Levante rarely pin teams back; they took one corner at Balaídos. I'd expect nine or ten.

cards.text: The model has 4.7 cards and I see no strong reason to move it. Levante took two yellows at Celta and Racing two at Málaga, so it may come down to whether this turns into another relegation scrap and who referees.

shots.text: The site expects 33.7 shots, which is very high. Racing average about 12 shots a game and Levante's output has been modest, so the high 20s is more realistic even in an open game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 on target. Racing put about 4.5 a game on target and Levante rarely get to double figures in shots, so I see about nine in total.

401882796.overall: Early view: Betis host Rayo at La Cartuja four days after a Champions League trip to Slovan Bratislava. Pellegrini has said his squad is deep enough to rotate, and Cucho Hernández should be close to fitness by then. Rayo under Beñat San José press hard and play open games; they come off a home match with Valencia amid continuing fan protests at Vallecas.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Betis have attackers to spare (Isco, Antony, Abde, Riquelme and possibly Cucho back), and San José's Rayo conceded heavily early in the season and still play a high-pressing, open game. I lean towards three goals.

corners.text: The site expects 10.4 corners. Betis took eight corners at Elche and shoot a lot from distance, while Rayo won six even in defeat at Anoeta. Both teams attack down the flanks, which points slightly higher.

cards.text: The model has 5.4 cards, 3.3 of them for Rayo, which looks heavy. Rayo took two yellows at Real Sociedad and Betis none at Elche. Without derby or relegation tension, four or five cards seems more likely.

shots.text: The site expects 31.1 shots, which fits. Betis had 18 at Elche and Rayo pressed well enough to take 11 at Anoeta, but some rotation after Bratislava may take a bit off Betis' output.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Many of Betis' shots are speculative (Antony had gone more than 30 league shots without a goal by late October), and a rotated side may be less sharp. Eight or nine seems right.

401882790.overall: Early view: bottom side Málaga, still without a league win this season, host Athletic, whose striker shortage (Guruzeta out for the season, Hierro and Sannadi injured) blunts their edge. Málaga's coaching situation may have changed by then, since two reports say Funes is under threat. Aznou's red card at home to Racing was a second yellow, which normally carries a one-match ban served at Osasuna, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Málaga score about 0.8 a game, and Athletic's attack without a No. 9 depends on the Williams brothers creating from wide. A 0-1 or 1-1 type of game looks most likely.

corners.text: The site expects 10.6 corners. Terzić's Athletic keep the ball (61% at El Sadar), and Málaga defend in a back five that invites crosses and blocks. Athletic's wide play should push the total to 11 or more.

cards.text: The model has 4.2 cards. Málaga's frustration showed against Racing with seven yellows and a red, and a side fighting relegation chasing the ball at home tends to foul more. Five cards looks closer than four.

shots.text: The site expects 28.7 shots. Athletic had 16 at Osasuna and Málaga average about 11 a game, so a total around 26 or 27 fits better.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 on target. Málaga average about three shots on target a game, and Athletic lack a finisher in the box. Seven or eight is more likely.

401882793.overall: Early view: Elche have the worst home record in the league (1 point from 18 at the Martínez Valero) despite good away form, and Martín Anselmi is dealing with injuries to Lemar, Aguado and others. Atlético play Viking at home in the Champions League three days earlier, so Simeone may rotate, and Cuti Romero's new muscle injury may still keep him out.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Elche have scored little at home (losing 0-1 to Valencia and 0-2 to Betis), and Atlético had one of the two best defences in the first ten rounds. A low-scoring Atlético win is the most likely result.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. Elche like to keep the ball, even at home, and won nine corners against Betis, while Atlético take their share from set-piece pressure. Ten corners looks fair.

cards.text: The model has 4.2 cards. Elche took four yellows against Betis and Atlético four against Barcelona; Simeone's team slows games down with fouls when ahead. I lean to five cards.

shots.text: The site expects 27.1 shots and I see no strong reason to move it. Elche had 13 shots against Betis and Atlético usually take a similar number away, though a rotated side after Viking could be less sharp.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 on target. None of Elche's 13 shots against Betis went in and their creative midfielders are injured, and Atlético away often take few, careful shots. About seven on target.

401882789.overall: Early view: Real Madrid host PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday before this Saturday night game, so Mourinho may rotate, but his side has won eight in a row with Vinícius back from suspension. Alavés, winless in eight under Quique Sánchez Flores, lost 6-1 at Barcelona but then defended deep for a 0-0 at Sevilla; one injury list has Facundo Garcés and Mikel Rodríguez out with cruciate injuries.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Alavés lost 6-1 at Barcelona last month, their defence is missing Garcés, and Madrid scored three at Mestalla while hardly being tested. Even with some rotation after PSV, I lean towards four goals rather than two.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. Alavés defend in a deep 3-5-2, so Madrid will spend long spells around the box, which pushes up their corner count even though Mourinho's sides prefer quick attacks. Ten looks fair.

cards.text: The model has 4.5 cards. Sánchez Flores' side committed 19 fouls and took three yellows at Sevilla, and a team defending deep against Mbappé and Vinícius usually commits fouls to stop counterattacks. Five cards is my call.

shots.text: The site expects 28.2 shots and I agree. Madrid had 19 at Valencia, and Alavés managed nine at Sevilla, so the total should be near the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 on target. Madrid were efficient at Mestalla and their front line is complete again, but some rotation after PSV keeps me at the site's figure rather than above it.

401882787.overall: Early view: second-from-bottom Valencia have taken 2 of 21 points at Mestalla under Javier Aguirre, and the mood was tense after the 0-3 defeat to Real Madrid. Gayà's red card (one match, served at Rayo) and Moncayola's five-yellow ban (served against Málaga) should both be over by this game, despite what the brief lists. Osasuna (16th) have been poor away, losing at Deportivo and Sevilla.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Valencia's home attack has hardly worked (four shots against Madrid), and Osasuna away have scored little; both sides near the bottom will be wary of losing. I lean towards one or two goals.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners and I am close. Osasuna's wide crossing game produces corners, but Aguirre's deep 5-3-2 gives Valencia few of their own, so the two roughly balance.

cards.text: The model has 4.8 cards and I lean higher. Valencia committed 26 fouls and took five cards against Madrid, Osasuna committed 19 fouls against Athletic, and with Mestalla impatient, five or six cards is likely.

shots.text: The site expects 25.9 shots. Aguirre's Valencia generate very little (four shots at home to Real Madrid), and Osasuna's away attack has been flat. Low 20s looks right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.5 on target. Neither side creates much clear-cut, and Umar Sadiq, Valencia's main target man, took a knock against Madrid. Six on target seems more likely.

401882794.overall: Early view: Barcelona top the table with 48 goals in 12 games, but this comes four days after a Champions League trip to Sabah (25 November) and three days before hosting Atlético, and Flick keeps repeating that he has to 'look after the players', so rotation is likely. Promoted Deportivo go into the break on their first clean sheet (0-0 at Espanyol) but are without Eddahchouri after wrist surgery; Barça currently have Olmo, Rodri, Koundé and Bardghji out, and Lamine Yamal is being managed for right-knee discomfort.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, driven by Barcelona scoring four a game. I lean a little lower: a rotated Barça between the Sabah trip and Atlético, against a Deportivo side that has conceded 14 in 12 and just shut out Espanyol, points to something nearer 3. Barça's own defence (13 conceded) also limits a Deportivo attack missing Eddahchouri.

corners.text: The numbers say 11 corners. Barcelona's recent games have been light on corners despite huge possession: 7 at Betis, 6 against Alavés and 6 at Atlético, with Barça themselves taking only 2-5 in three of their last four. Deportivo took 5 at Espanyol while sitting deep, so I lean lower, around 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Deportivo picked up four yellows defending at Espanyol and Amatucci is one booking from a ban, but Barça are rarely booked (one yellow at the Metropolitano). With no referee named yet, nothing moves me far from the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. Barcelona have taken 13-19 shots in each of their last four league games and allowed 6-9, which adds up to the mid-20s rather than 28. Deportivo had only 5 shots at Espanyol with 36% of the ball, and a rotated Barça may control the game rather than chase volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target. Barça put only 4 of 19 shots on target at the Metropolitano, and Deportivo's attack is thin with Eddahchouri out and Yeremay coming back from gastroenteritis. I lean lower, around 8-9.

401882795.overall: Early view: both sides come straight from Europe, with Celta hosting Bournemouth in the Europa League on Thursday 26 November and Villarreal away at Slavia Prague the night before. Celta's games are the lowest-scoring in the league (10 scored, 10 conceded in 12), Giráldez admits the team is tired and nervous in front of goal, and his injury list is long; Iñigo Pérez's Villarreal ended a poor run by beating Getafe 2-0 with 72% of the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Celta have scored and conceded 10 each in 12 games, two of their last three ended 0-0, and they had 23 shots and no goal against Levante, which Giráldez put down to nerves in the box. With both teams coming off European games, I lean lower, around 2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Villarreal's last three league games produced 13, 10 and 15 corners as Iñigo Pérez's side pin teams back, and Celta's home pressure against Levante brought 6 corners of their own. I lean higher, around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Celta are a low-foul side (8 fouls and one yellow against Levante), and Renato Veiga is one booking away from a ban rather than suspended, as is Celta's Yoel Lago, which tends to make defenders careful. I lean slightly lower, around 3-4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots. Celta took 23 at home to Levante and Villarreal 22 against Getafe, so volume is there, but both teams will be on tired legs after midweek Europe. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Celta got 8 of their 23 shots on target against Levante and Villarreal 7 of 22 against Getafe; Borja Iglesias may only just be back from his calf injury, so I see no reason to move off the number.

401882788.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad are fifth after four wins in five, but this is the middle of a heavy run (Crystal Palace away in the Europa League on 26 November, Real Madrid on 2 December), and Barrenetxea looks set to miss the rest of 2026 with a hamstring injury, according to one report. Sevilla (sixth) have stalled, 0-0 at home to Alavés after Rubén Vargas missed a penalty, and Peque may be back from his hamstring injury around this date.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, and both teams' season totals support a lively game. But Real Sociedad have scored twice in their last two league games, lose Barrenetxea (who set up the winner against Rayo) and arrive three days after a trip to Crystal Palace, while Sevilla failed to score at home to Alavés. I lean lower, nearer 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Real Sociedad's last two games both had 13 corners as Matarazzo's side keep the ball and work it wide, and Sevilla's full-backs pushed on to earn 5 corners against a deep Alavés. I lean higher, around 10-11.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Sevilla had four yellows and a red at Getafe and Real Sociedad four bookings at Athletic, so the number looks fair; Aramburu and Yangel Herrera are one yellow from bans, which could make Real Sociedad slightly more careful. I stay close to 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Real Sociedad's last two games had 28 and 27 shots and Sevilla's 22 and 23, so the number sits right in the middle. Fatigue after Thursday could trim Real Sociedad's pressing, but nothing points clearly either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Real Sociedad managed only 3 on target from 17 shots against Rayo, and Sevilla could not beat Sivera even from the penalty spot against Alavés. Patchy finishing on both sides makes me lean lower, around 7.

401882792.overall: Early view: a low-scoring pairing of two sides on 12 points. Eder Sarabia's Espanyol keep the ball (64% against Deportivo) but have only 13 goals and lack Kike García until December, while Bordalás's Getafe have 8, the fewest in the league, and play in Tbilisi in the Conference League four days earlier. Gudelj serves his yellow-card ban against Atlético on 22 November, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. Espanyol have scored twice in their last three games and Getafe have 8 goals all season, with one shot on target at Villarreal. I agree with a low total; under 2.5 looks right.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Espanyol's last three games had 14, 10 and 13 corners, and at home under Sarabia they keep the ball against deep blocks (9 corners against Deportivo); Getafe defend deep away and gave up 9 at Villarreal. I lean slightly higher, around 10-11.

cards.text: The numbers say 7 cards, which is high but fits: Espanyol had four yellows against Deportivo and five at Racing, and Getafe's games against Rayo and Sevilla each had a red card. Gudelj should be back, and Terrats and Riedel are one yellow from bans. I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots. Espanyol's possession has not turned into volume (11 shots against Deportivo, 5 at Villarreal) and Getafe managed 9 at Villarreal. A slow Monday game after Getafe's trip to Georgia, with Bordalás already worried about fatigue, points lower, around 21.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 on target. Getafe put 1 of 9 on target at Villarreal and Espanyol's best chances against Deportivo were headers, with no proper striker while Kike García is out. I lean lower, around 6.

401882698.overall: Early view: a matchday-23 game brought forward because both clubs play February's Supercopa, and it lands at the end of a brutal week for Real Sociedad (Crystal Palace on 26 November, Sevilla on the 29th). Mourinho's Madrid have won eight in a row, Mbappé has scored in seven straight games and they have conceded 10 in 12; they then go to Athletic and Arsenal within a week, and Mourinho is already complaining about the schedule.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with Madrid expected to score twice. That fits: Madrid scored three at both Racing and Valencia and Real Sociedad have conceded 20 in 12, but a tired home side without Barrenetxea may not add much at the other end. I stay around 3, most of it from Madrid.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Real Sociedad's last two games had 13 corners each, but Madrid's away wins at Racing and Valencia produced only 8 and 7 as they controlled play through the middle. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Madrid took three yellows in each of their last two big away games, and Real Sociedad's Aramburu and Yangel Herrera are one booking from bans; a tired home side chasing Madrid's counters could foul late on. I stay around 4-5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots, 15 of them Madrid's. Madrid took 22 at Racing and 19 at Valencia while allowing 10 and 4, and Real Sociedad's own games have high volume (28 against Rayo). I lean a little higher, around 28-29.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 on target. Madrid put 11 of 19 on target at Valencia with Valverde, Güler and Mbappé all scoring, but Real Sociedad managed 3 from 17 against Rayo and will be tired. I stay close to the number, with Madrid providing most of it.

401882700.overall: Early view: the return of the game Barcelona won 2-1 at the Metropolitano on 8 November, brought forward from February because of the Supercopa. It sits between Barça's trip to Deportivo and the visit of Manchester City on 8 December, while Atlético host Viking on 25 November; Simeone said his side lacked a cutting edge in the first meeting and Julián Álvarez missed clear chances.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. Atlético have conceded only 10 in 12, the first meeting finished 2-1 with just 8 shots on target between the teams, and Simeone's side defend deep away from home. I lean lower, around 3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. The first meeting produced only 6 (Atlético 4, Barça 2) and Barcelona's home win over Alavés also had 6; Barça work the ball inside rather than forcing corners. I lean lower, around 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Atlético took four yellows in the first meeting (Baena, Llorente, Pubill and Hjulmand) against Barça's one, and Baena and Pubill are one booking from bans, which may restrain them a little. The rivalry supports a busy card count, so I stay around 5-6.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, almost exactly the 19-9 split from the first meeting. Barcelona will have the ball again and Atlético will look to break, so I see no reason to move off it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 on target. The first meeting had only 8 on target (4 each) from 28 shots, Atlético block a lot in their own box, and Julián Álvarez has been off target lately. I lean lower, around 7-8.

401882786.overall: Early view: two lower-mid-table sides a point apart. Alavés steadied with a 0-0 at Sevilla after a 6-1 loss at Barcelona, with Sivera saving a penalty, but have not won in five league games and have Garcés and Mikel Rodríguez out with knee ligament injuries; Eder Sarabia's Espanyol are possession-heavy but low-scoring, and play Getafe on the Monday before this.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Alavés drew 0-0 at Sevilla and 1-1 with Málaga, and Espanyol have two goals in their last three games with Kike García out until December. I lean slightly lower, around 2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Alavés took 7 corners at home against Málaga and Espanyol's games have produced 10-14 recently; Sarabia's side will keep the ball, which should push Alavés back at times. I stay around 9-10.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. Espanyol have collected three to five yellows in each of their last three games and Alavés had three at both Sevilla and Barcelona, so a scrappy game between close rivals points a little higher, around 6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. Espanyol have been cautious away (5 shots at Villarreal, 11 at Racing) while Alavés's games at Sevilla and Barcelona had 22 and 20 shots in total. I lean lower, around 22.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Neither attack is sharp: Alavés scored once from 18 shots against Málaga, and Espanyol rely on set pieces and headers without Kike García. I lean lower, around 7.

401882785.overall: Early view: Mourinho's Madrid (eight straight wins, 10 conceded in 12) visit San Mamés four days after Real Sociedad away and three before Arsenal, so some rotation is possible. Edin Terzić's Athletic are solid (11 conceded in 11) but short of strikers, with Guruzeta out until May and Sannadi until late December, and Nico Williams went into the break after cramps at Osasuna.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Athletic's defence is tight and their attack is weakened without Guruzeta and Sannadi, while Madrid have scored three in each of their last two away games. The two pull against each other, so I stay around 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Athletic's derby with Real Sociedad had 13 corners, but Madrid's away games at Racing and Valencia had only 8 and 7. I see no strong reason to move from around 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Athletic's last two games had six and four bookings and Madrid took three at Valencia in a heated game, but Athletic are not a heavy-fouling side (10-11 fouls in recent games) and no referee is named yet. I stay around 4.

shots.text: The numbers split 25.5 shots evenly, but Madrid have taken 19-22 shots in each of their last two away games, and Athletic took 13-16 in theirs. Even allowing for rotation before Arsenal, I lean higher, around 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 on target. Madrid's accuracy has been high (11 on target at Valencia), but Athletic's injury-hit attack lowers their share; overall I stay around 9.

401882784.overall: Early view: third against fourth, with both sides squeezed between Champions League games: Atlético play at Barcelona on 2 December and at PSV on the 9th, and Betis host Como on the 9th. Atlético had won four straight before losing to Barça and concede little; Pellegrini's Betis won 0-2 at Elche with goals from a set piece and late pressure, and Cucho Hernández should be back from his calf injury by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Atlético's home games have been tight (1-0 against Deportivo, 1-2 against Barça) and Simeone's side have conceded 10 in 12, while Betis striker Troy Parrott, Pellegrini says, needs confidence. I lean slightly lower, around 2-2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Betis's win at Elche had 17 corners and Pellegrini highlighted set pieces as a growing weapon (Bartra's header from a Ceballos corner), but Atlético's home game with Barça had only 6. I stay around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4 cards. Atlético picked up four yellows in their last home game, and Betis had a red and three yellows against Barcelona at home, though none at Elche. A big game between two top-four sides points slightly higher, around 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 29 shots. That is high for Simeone's Atlético, who took 9 against Barça and 11 at Levante, and both teams will have one eye on the Champions League the following week. I lean lower, around 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 on target. Atlético managed 4 on target against Barcelona and Julián Álvarez's finishing has dipped, though Betis did put 9 on target at Elche. I lean lower, around 8.

401882783.overall: Early view: Barcelona host Celta between Atlético (2 December) and Manchester City (8 December), so Flick is likely to rotate, though they scored six against Alavés in their last home league game. Celta play at Marseille in the Europa League four days later, have the league's lowest-scoring games (10 for, 10 against) and a long injury list that Giráldez hopes to clear by late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Celta have conceded only 10 in 12 and their games average under two goals, and Barça are likely to rotate before Manchester City. I still expect Barça to win comfortably but lean lower, around 3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Barcelona's home game with Alavés had only 6 corners despite 77% possession, and Barça took just 2 at the Metropolitano; they score from inside the box rather than forcing corners. I lean lower, around 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Celta commit few fouls (8 against Levante, one yellow) and Barça's home win over Alavés had five bookings; nothing in the news moves me off about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots. Barça took only 13 shots in the 6-1 against Alavés because they scored so efficiently, and a rotated side before Manchester City may manage the game rather than chase volume. I lean lower, around 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10 on target, mostly Barça's. Barça are clinical at home (six goals from 13 shots against Alavés), so even with fewer shots the on-target count should hold up; I stay around 9-10.

401882782.overall: Early view: a scrap between two of the weakest attacks. Bordalás's Getafe (15th) have scored 8 all season and host Inter Escaldes in the Conference League four days later, while Javier Aguirre's Valencia are 19th with one win in five and Mestalla losing patience after the 0-3 against Madrid. Gudelj serves his one-match ban against Atlético on matchday 13 and should be back; Gayà's straight red at Mestalla rules him out against Rayo, and reports so far give no longer ban, so he should also return here.

goals.text: The numbers say 2 goals. These are the two lowest-scoring attacks in the division (8 goals each in 12 games), Valencia managed 4 shots against Madrid and won at Elche with 5, and Umar Sadiq took a knock at Mestalla. I lean lower, under 2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Getafe's home game with Sevilla had only 4 corners and Valencia's last two games had 7 and 8, with both sides happy to play long and defend deep. I lean lower, around 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. Getafe's home games with Rayo and Sevilla each had a red card, and Valencia have had players sent off in two of their last three games (Elliott, Gayà) plus Aguirre booked at Mestalla. I lean higher, around 7.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.2 shots. Getafe took 9 at Villarreal and 11 against Sevilla, Valencia 4 against Madrid and 5 at Elche; even against each other, neither side creates much volume. I lean lower, around 20.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7 on target. Getafe put 1 of 9 on target at Villarreal and Valencia 2 of 4 against Madrid, so this has the look of a game with few clear chances. I lean lower, around 5-6.

401882781.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between 16th and 18th. Osasuna changed coach in October, Jagoba Arrasate replacing Luis Miguel Ramis, and rescued a 1-1 against Athletic in stoppage time, with Herrando, Oroz and Del Castillo expected back after the break; Martín Anselmi's Elche have yet to win at home but did win 0-3 at Rayo, and Lemar is out until late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Osasuna have conceded 23 in 12, which argues for goals, but Elche have scored once in their last three games and Anselmi admits they are not converting chances. I stay around 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Elche are a possession side (69% at home to Valencia) and their game with Betis produced 17 corners, while Osasuna's equaliser against Athletic came from a corner. I lean higher, around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. Osasuna picked up three and four yellows in their last two games and Elche four against Betis, in a game with relegation stakes; Moncayola is one yellow away from a ban rather than suspended. I lean slightly higher, around 5-6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. Osasuna's last home game had 33 shots and Elche have taken 13-16 shots in each of their last two games despite not scoring. I lean slightly higher, around 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 on target. Elche had only one shot on target from 13 against Betis and failed to score from 16 against Valencia, so their accuracy is the weak point. I lean lower, around 7.

401882780.overall: Early view: a meeting of two promoted sides level on points. Racing have the league's worst defence (30 conceded) but play open games and just won 1-2 at Málaga for their first away points; Antonio Hidalgo's Deportivo are steadier (14 conceded) but are without Eddahchouri after wrist surgery, while Racing hope to have Andrés Martín back from a hamstring injury by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Racing's games average almost four goals because of their defence, but Deportivo's average under 2.5 and they just kept a clean sheet at Espanyol. I stay close to 3.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.7 corners, which is a lot. Racing's recent games had 13 (Espanyol), 9 (Málaga) and 8 (Madrid), and Deportivo's had 14 at Espanyol and 10 against Osasuna; that averages around 11, so I lean lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. Racing have been booked lightly (two yellows at Málaga, two against Madrid), and Zabiri and Pablo Ramón are one yellow from bans; Deportivo had four at Espanyol but none against Osasuna. I lean slightly lower, around 4-5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots. Racing's last three games had 34, 37 and 32 shots, so their open style backs the number, though Deportivo's 5 shots at Espanyol show how cautious they can be away. I stay around 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target. Racing's game at Málaga had 15 on target, but Deportivo's attack is weakened by Eddahchouri's absence and Aubameyang is still building minutes. I stay around 10.

401882779.overall: Early view: two sides in the bottom half. Beñat San José's Rayo have lost two of their last three but beat Celta 3-0 at home, and expect Valentín and Kumbulla back after the break while Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Álvaro García stay out. Luís Castro's Levante have one point from their last two and have complained to LaLiga about a congested schedule, with games on 23 and 27 November before this trip.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Both sides' season totals point a bit higher (Rayo's games average over three goals), but Levante have scored once in their last three and had no shots on target at Celta. I stay around 2.5-3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. Rayo's games swing widely (6 against Elche, 13 at Real Sociedad) and Levante's last two had 7 and 8. I stay around 9-10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. Levante are rarely booked (two yellows at Celta, none against Atlético) and Rayo have had two or three per game, while Levante's Adrián de la Fuente is one yellow from a ban. I lean slightly lower, around 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.4 shots, which is very high. Rayo took 18 at home to Elche and 11 at Real Sociedad, and Levante managed 6 at Celta, though they had 20 against Atlético. I lean lower, around 27-28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 on target. Rayo put only 3 on target at Real Sociedad and missed a penalty against Elche, and Levante had none on target at Celta. I lean lower, around 8.

401882778.overall: Early view: sixth against bottom. Málaga have 5 points and no win in 12, the club is backing Juanfran Funes for now, and full-back Rafita is out for three to four months, per Radio MARCA; Sevilla drew a blank at home to Alavés but beat Osasuna 2-0 there in October, and Peque should be back from his hamstring injury. Aznou serves his one-game ban on matchday 13, so he should be available.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, with Sevilla scoring two. Málaga concede almost two a game and have lost Rafita, but Sevilla's home attack has stalled (no goal against Alavés, Vargas missing a penalty). I stay around 2.5-3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Sevilla's home games with Alavés and Osasuna had 9 and 11 corners and Málaga's games against Racing and Alavés had 9 each, so the number looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Málaga's frustration showed against Racing (six yellows and Aznou's red), and Larrubia and Chupete are one booking from bans; a winless side chasing points away from home tends to foul. I lean slightly higher, around 5-6.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, which is high for Sevilla, who took 13 at home to Alavés and 17 against Osasuna. Málaga managed 7 at Alavés, so I lean lower, around 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 on target. Sevilla could not beat Sivera even from the spot against Alavés, and Málaga's attack is short of quality with Lobete out until April. I lean lower, around 8.

401882777.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad arrive on their fourth game in about ten days (Crystal Palace, Sevilla, Real Madrid, then this), while Iñigo Pérez's Villarreal host Sabah in the Champions League on 8 December. Real Sociedad will be without Barrenetxea, and Renato Veiga is one booking away from a suspension rather than suspended, so his availability depends on the games before this.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Villarreal's last four league games produced 0, 3, 1 and 2 goals, and Real Sociedad will be on tired legs without Barrenetxea. I lean lower, around 2.5-3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. Villarreal's last two home games had six and four yellows and Real Sociedad had four at Athletic; several players are on the edge of bans (Veiga for Villarreal, Aramburu and Yangel Herrera for Real Sociedad). I stay around 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.3 shots, 17 of them Villarreal's. Villarreal took 22 against Getafe but only 14 against Espanyol, and a tired Real Sociedad may cede the ball; I stay around 28-29.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 on target. Villarreal put 7 of 22 on target against Getafe and Real Sociedad only 3 of 17 against Rayo; patchy finishing on both sides points lower, around 8.

401888247.overall: Early view: a bottom-five meeting between Genclerbirligi (14th, 11 pts) and Gaziantep (16th, 8 pts), who have lost six league games in a row and parted with coach Orhan Ak on 7 November with no successor named yet. Bernd Storck's side lost 3-0 at Besiktas after Metehan Baltaci's early red card, and they are also without Ousmane Diabate (fifth yellow), while defender Thalisson went off injured in that game. A new coach in the Gaziantep dugout could change the picture, so this will be refreshed with team news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Gaziantep have conceded 14 goals in their last seven matches and are in the middle of a coaching change, while Genclerbirligi scored five at home to Alanyaspor two weeks before the break. Genclerbirligi's own back line is thin, with Metehan and Diabate banned and Thalisson injured, so both nets look vulnerable.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I see no reason to move off that. Genclerbirligi should have more of the ball at Eryaman, but Gaziantep did push forward in their 2-0 home loss to Kasimpasa, hitting the woodwork twice, so both sides should earn a share.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already a busy line, and I lean a little higher. This is a relegation six-pointer, Genclerbirligi's last game brought a red card and a fifth-yellow suspension, and Gaziantep will be playing for a new or interim coach with nothing to protect.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, which already allows for an open game. Tiago Gouveia, Franco Tongya and Pedro Mendes showed against Alanyaspor that Genclerbirligi can pile up chances at home, but Gaziantep have scored just twice in seven games, so I do not see the volume going much higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because both defences are giving away clear chances: Gaziantep conceded twice to Kasimpasa inside 20 minutes, and Genclerbirligi will be patching up the middle of their defence.

401888369.overall: Early view: Amed (3rd, 23 pts) have scored 28 goals, one fewer than Fenerbahce, and lost only 4-3 at leaders Galatasaray, a result that ended an eight-game unbeaten run. Recep Ucar's Rizespor won at home for the first time this season just before the break (2-1 against Erzurumspor) but have scored only 13 and are without midfielder Can Bozdogan after ankle surgery. Samuel Ballet missed the Galatasaray game through a red-card ban; whether he is back here needs checking nearer the time.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, which I think is too high. Amed's games are open, but Rizespor's eleven matches have produced 29 goals in total and they drew 0-0 at Kocaelispor two weeks ago, so 4.1 would need Besnik Hasi's side to finish at an unusually high rate even at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners and I lean higher. Amed won six corners even away at Galatasaray and are dangerous from dead balls (Dia Saba scored from a free kick there), so at home against a side likely to defend deep they should beat their 4.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean slightly higher because Amed's discipline has slipped lately: Ballet served a red-card ban and Rayan Raveloson, Gift Orban and David Bates were all booked at Galatasaray, while Rizespor will need to stop Amed's counter-attacks.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots with Amed taking most of them. That fits: Amed had 14 shots even at RAMS Park, and Rizespor captain Taylan Antalyali admitted after the Trabzonspor game that they conceded three in eight minutes, so they do give chances away.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Amed put five on target at Galatasaray and should manage more at home, while Rizespor rarely test keepers, so I keep it near the number; it is the conversion behind the 4.1-goal forecast I doubt, not the volume.

401888245.overall: Early view: Galatasaray lead by three points and are 41 league games unbeaten at home, but they will be without Victor Osimhen (knee surgery on 7 November) and Rafael Leao (severe muscle strain against Amed), and they play Aston Villa in the Champions League three days later. Samsunspor are 17th; Nenad Bjelica's side ended an eight-game losing run by beating Konyaspor 1-0 just before the break. Captain Abdulkerim Bardakci completed his ban against Amed and should be available.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. I lean a bit lower: Galatasaray still scored four against Amed without Osimhen, but losing Leao too and the Aston Villa game three days later make rotation likely, and Samsunspor kept a clean sheet in Bjelica's first win.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, mostly Galatasaray's. They won only three against an Amed side that attacked them, but Samsunspor are likely to sit deep and defend their box, which usually pushes Galatasaray's count up, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and I lean lower. Galatasaray were not booked at all against Amed, and Davinson Sanchez and Roland Sallai are one yellow away from a ban that would rule them out of the Besiktas derby, so they have reason to stay careful; most cards should come from Samsunspor's defending.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, 22.8 of them Galatasaray's. I lean lower because the two forwards who shoot most are out and Okan Buruk may rest players before Aston Villa; Galatasaray had 17 shots against Amed, and 20-plus without Osimhen is a stretch even against a weaker side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Galatasaray hit the target six times against Amed, and with Osimhen and Leao out I expect seven or eight from them plus a couple from Samsunspor, slightly under the number.

401888244.overall: Early view: Fenerbahce (6th) have a new coach in Emre Belozoglu, who replaced Ismail Kartal and started with a 5-0 win at Corum, days after the club beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League. Selcuk Inan's Kocaelispor are level on 19 points, have conceded only nine goals in eleven games and took seven points from their last three, and their chairman called them favourites for this one. Marco Asensio was injured and Archie Brown suspended for the Corum trip, so Fenerbahce's team news needs rechecking.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean lower: Kocaelispor's matches have averaged two goals, their last home game was 0-0 with Rizespor, and Inan's side defends compactly. Fenerbahce are the league's top scorers with 29, but they lost 2-1 at home to Goztepe on 2 November, so goals against an organised defence have not always come easily.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Fenerbahce will have most of the ball against a low block, which tends to produce corners, while Kocaelispor rely on counters and their own set pieces; the split may be more one-sided than 4.9 to 4.6, but the total looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and I lean higher. A big-club visit to Kocaeli usually brings tactical fouls on the break and protests, and Belozoglu was referred to the disciplinary board over remarks about referees in his last weeks at Kasimpasa, so the touchline may be lively too.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. Kocaelispor's games are low-event and they rarely open up, so I lean lower; Fenerbahce will shoot plenty, but 14 home shots for Kocaelispor look generous for a team that has scored 13 in eleven games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. With Kocaelispor packing the box and creating little, I lean slightly lower, with most efforts on target likely to come from Mason Greenwood and Irfan Can Kahveci, who shared four goals at Corum.

401888243.overall: Early view: Goztepe (10th) won four league games in a row, including 2-1 at Fenerbahce, before Basaksehir beat them 2-1 in Izmir. Promoted Erzurumspor (12th) under Serkan Ozbalta have lost their last two, 3-1 at home to Corum and 2-1 at Rizespor, and have scored only ten goals in eleven games. goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I lean slightly higher. Goztepe's eleven games have produced 41 goals, with Juan, Henrique and Armstrong all scoring recently, and Erzurumspor conceded three at home to Corum in their last home match.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners. Neither side's recent games point to a big change, and with Erzurumspor likely to sit in against an in-form visitor, I keep it close to eight.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Nothing specific moves this: no suspensions are reported on either side and there is no rivalry to speak of, so around four looks fair until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, with Goztepe taking slightly more. That suits a game where Goztepe's attack meets a home side that has been leaking chances, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. I lean a little higher in line with goals: Goztepe have scored 22 in eleven and Erzurumspor have conceded 17, so the visitors in particular should test the keeper often.

401888248.overall: Early view: Kasimpasa (5th, unbeaten in four) lost coach Emre Belozoglu to Fenerbahce and appointed Alfred Schreuder until the end of the season; this is his first home league game, after two weeks to work with the squad over the break. Alanyaspor under Joao Pereira have lost four in a row, including 5-0 at Genclerbirligi and 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, and have scored once in their last three games.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and I lean slightly lower. Alanyaspor have scored nine all season and one in their last three, so most of the goals have to come from Kasimpasa, who won 2-0 at Gaziantep with both goals in the first 20 minutes and then managed the game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Kasimpasa should have most of the ball, as Trabzonspor did in Alanya when they gave Alanyaspor almost no possession, but there is nothing specific to push the total up or down.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Kasimpasa picked up two yellows at Gaziantep and Alanyaspor are a frustrated side on a losing run, but neither has shown a recent pattern of heavy bookings, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. I lean lower because ten away shots look generous for an Alanyaspor team that has been pinned back in recent weeks, and a new coach's first home game is often a controlled one.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Alanyaspor rarely test the keeper at the moment, so I expect most of the efforts on target from Kasimpasa's Haris Hajradinovic and Adrian Benedyczak and a total slightly under the number.

401888246.overall: Early view: Besiktas (4th) went into the break on a 3-0 win over Genclerbirligi, with Dusan Vlahovic on nine league goals and Leandro Trossard creating, but captain Orkun Kokcu is suspended after his latest yellow card. Konyaspor (15th) under Ilhan Palut have scored six goals in eleven games, have not won away and lost 1-0 at Samsunspor in their last match. Fabio Miretti, hurt against Crystal Palace, is targeting a return for this game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and I lean a touch lower. Konyaspor's games have produced just 20 goals in total, and without Kokcu, whose return was credited with lifting Besiktas's passing and tempo, Vincenzo Italiano's side lose their main playmaker; a Hurriyet columnist also flagged their away attacking as the area that still needs work.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Besiktas had about 70% of the ball in the first half against Genclerbirligi and should dominate possession again, which produces corners, while Konyaspor threatened from headers at Samsunspor; I stay near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. Konyaspor are a side under pressure (Enis Destan had a red card at Samsunspor reduced to a yellow after a VAR check) and Wilfred Ndidi was booked in the second minute last time out, so around five seems right.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.8 shots and I lean higher. Besiktas keep the ball and shoot often, with Trossard and Vlahovic combining for three goals last week, and Konyaspor's low block tends to invite many attempts from outside the box rather than clear chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. More shots from distance against a packed defence do not mean many more on target, and Konyaspor rarely trouble keepers, so I keep it near eight.

401888249.overall: Early view: Trabzonspor (2nd, three points behind) have won all six league games under Thomas Reis, the latest 2-0 at Alanyaspor, though they lost 1-0 at home to Freiburg in the Conference League. Eyupspor are bottom with three points and a 3-30 goal difference, and coach Mustafa Dalci admitted after the 2-0 home loss to Kocaelispor that things are not going well. Trabzonspor's long-term absentees include Ruslan Malinovskyi and Batagov.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean slightly higher. Eyupspor have conceded 30 goals in eleven games, including five at Amed, and Trabzonspor have scored 26 while conceding only eight, so the risk is a heavy home win rather than a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Trabzonspor gave Alanyaspor almost no possession last week and should do the same here, so nearly all corners should be theirs; Eyupspor's 3.6 looks high, but Trabzonspor's own share could be bigger, so the total holds.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and I lean lower. One-sided games like this rarely produce many bookings, and Trabzonspor have little need to foul when they control the ball the way they did in Alanya.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. I expect Trabzonspor to take well over their 17.2 and Eyupspor fewer than 10.2, since Eyupspor have scored three all season, so the total ends up near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Paul Onuachu, Salah and Muci should test the keeper often against the league's weakest defence, but Eyupspor's own contribution will be small, so I stay close to ten.

401888370.overall: Early view: Basaksehir (8th) under Nuri Sahin have scored seven in their last two games, 5-2 against Samsunspor and a comeback 2-1 at Goztepe with goals from Selke and Edin Visca. Corum (9th) lost 5-0 at home to Fenerbahce before the break, but the club president publicly backed coach Burak Yilmaz, whose side had taken nine points from the previous four games. Corum's Berat Ayberk Ozdemir is out for six to eight weeks with a calf strain.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which is high but fits these sides: Corum's eleven games have produced 42 goals and Basaksehir's 36. Corum may tighten up after the 5-0, but they scored three at Erzurumspor two weeks earlier, so they will create chances too, and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Basaksehir should have more of the ball at home while Corum look to counter, which fits the 4.9 to 3.8 split, and I have nothing that moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Corum's Gokhan Sazdagi had to sit out the Fenerbahce game after a yellow-card build-up, but this is a Monday-night mid-table game with no rivalry, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and I lean a little higher. Basaksehir's attack is in form, and Corum are more likely to come out and try to answer the heavy defeat than to sit in, which tends to open up both ends.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With both sides scoring freely this season that looks about right, and I would not move it until the lineups are known.

401888241.overall: Early view: a Friday-night meeting of two sides in trouble: Alanyaspor (13th) had lost four straight under Joao Pereira by the break, and Konyaspor (15th, 8 pts) have one of the league's weakest attacks and no away win this season. Both play the weekend before (Alanyaspor at Kasimpasa, Konyaspor at home to Besiktas), so the mood here will depend on those results.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and I lean lower. These two have scored 15 goals between them in 22 league games, Konyaspor have lost four of their five away games, and Alanyaspor have one goal in their last three, so a nervy, low-scoring game looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Alanyaspor should push at home and Konyaspor can be dangerous from crosses (they hit the bar with headers at Samsunspor), so there is no strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and I lean slightly higher. With both sides near the relegation places the tackles will be fierce; Konyaspor picked up two yellows and had a red overturned at Samsunspor, and Alanyaspor's run has left them frustrated.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.5 shots. Neither side creates much at the moment, and Pereira said his team effectively did not turn up for the first half of their loss at Kocaelispor, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. With two blunt attacks I lean slightly lower; Konyaspor have scored six all season, which points to few efforts that really test a keeper.

401888240.overall: Early view: Rizespor (11th) finally won at home on 8 November, 2-1 against Erzurumspor, and coach Recep Ucar hopes it starts a better run; they are without midfielder Can Bozdogan after ankle surgery. Kasimpasa (5th) have lost only once all season and will be in their second league game under Alfred Schreuder, after hosting Alanyaspor.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean slightly lower. Kasimpasa have drawn five of eleven and their games average about 2.5 goals, Rizespor's about 2.6, and a new coach usually starts by making his team harder to beat.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners with Rizespor taking more at home. That fits a home side that has to chase results, and I have nothing that moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. No suspensions or flashpoints are reported for either side, so I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots. I lean lower: Rizespor's 16.3 looks a lot for a side that has scored 13 in eleven, and a Kasimpasa team settling under Schreuder is more likely to keep the game tight than trade chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. In line with my lower shots view I expect around eight, with Kasimpasa's Benedyczak and Hajradinovic the most likely to test the keeper.
