shots.text: The site has 26.4 shots. I lean slightly lower: Fulham's short turnaround from a Thursday game should take some energy out of their pressing, and Everton under Moyes prefer a few good chances to many. Mid-20s fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I lean lower: Fulham had most of the territory against Newcastle but finished poorly, and Everton's chances often come from headers that miss the target. Slightly fewer on target.

401878748.overall: Early view: the Tyne-Wear derby between two struggling sides. Newcastle under Matthias Jaissle were booed at home against Everton and have only 13 goals in 10 games, while Sunderland are 19th but beat Chelsea 1-0 and also have Europa League football in late November. Expect tension and fouls more than open football.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Sunderland have scored just eight goals all season and Newcastle's attack has been flat, and derbies between nervous sides are often tight. A 1-0 or 1-1 fits the form.

corners.text: The site has 9.5 corners. I agree: Newcastle will have more of the ball and work it wide, while Sunderland defend deep and break, as they did against Chelsea. Nothing points far either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, which is very high even for a derby. I lean lower: it will be a heated game with Newcastle defending man-to-man and Sunderland pressing hard, so five or six bookings is likely, but seven-plus needs a lot to go wrong.

shots.text: The site has 29.0 shots. I lean lower: Newcastle created very little against Everton (first shot on target after 85 minutes), and Sunderland are a low-volume side. Derby tension usually means more fouls and fewer shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I lean lower because both attacks are among the weakest in the league in goals scored, and Sunderland may also feel the Europa League schedule. Seven on target looks right.

401879209.overall: Early view: the north London derby with Arsenal top on 27 points, seven clean sheets and 444 league minutes without conceding, against a Spurs side that lost at Leeds and has a long attacking injury list. Spurs play Fulham on Thursday, Arsenal at Brentford on Wednesday, and Arsenal have Champions League football the following week. Arsenal's 1-0 habit and a derby edge point to a tight, physical game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean lower: Arsenal have won 34 league games 1-0 under Mikel Arteta and concede almost nothing, while Spurs are missing Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert and others and only scored 10 in 10. A low-scoring Arsenal win fits best.

corners.text: The site has 10.7 corners. I agree: Arsenal earn plenty of corners and are dangerous from them, and Spurs will push forward at home. No clear reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I agree: it is a derby, Pedro Porro and Roberto De Zerbi were both booked at Leeds, and Arsenal are happy to slow games down when ahead. Five or six bookings is in line with the figure.

shots.text: The site has 25.2 shots. I lean lower: Arsenal held Liverpool to no shots on target at Anfield and limit teams well, and Spurs' attacking injuries cut their options. Fewer shots than the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Arsenal's defence allows very few clean chances and their own attack, without Bukayo Saka, has been wasteful. Six on target looks more likely.

401875056.overall: Early view: Como come out of the break after a 2-0 defeat at Inter ended a six-game winning run, and they host AEK Athens in the Champions League three days later, so Fabregas may manage minutes. Cagliari stopped a four-game losing run by beating Frosinone 1-0 with a compact, counter-attacking display built on goalkeeper Caprile. Twelve Como players are away with national teams, including Nico Paz and Maximo Perrone with Argentina, which means a long trip back before a Saturday afternoon kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals with Como scoring most of them. I lean lower: Como have let in one goal in four home league games and their home matches average under 1.5 goals, while Cagliari under Pisacane sit deep and won their last game 1-0 with Caprile making a string of saves. With AEK Athens on the Tuesday, Como have little reason to chase a rout.

corners.text: The site expects 9.1 corners, nearly six of them Como's. I lean higher because Como average almost eight corners a game in Como and Cagliari concede about 6.5 a game, the second-worst figure in the league. Cagliari's low block against Frosinone gave away 13 corners, and Como will see a lot of the ball here.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I lean lower: Cagliari's games have averaged about 2.4 cards, among the fewest in Serie A, and Como pick up only around one booking a game. A one-sided match in which Cagliari defend in shape rarely turns bad-tempered.

shots.text: The site expects 26.4 shots, 18 of them Como's. I lean slightly higher, because Como's home games have averaged about 29 shots and Cagliari allow close to 19 shots a game. Cagliari themselves took 14 against Frosinone, so they are not entirely passive on the break.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. I lean a little lower: Como's home games have produced about seven on target, because much of their volume comes from blocked or long efforts against packed defences. Cagliari rarely test keepers away, averaging under five on target, and a rotated Como front line could be less sharp.

401874981.overall: Early view: Gattuso's Lazio are top and unbeaten after 11 games, but the 1-1 at Napoli cost them Nuno Tavares (a muscle injury that one report calls more serious than first thought) and Sutalo, who also went off with a muscle problem. Zaccagni and Gudmundsson were missing too. Lecce took a point at Torino with a physical, compact display, and with no European games for either side both should be fresh.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, mostly Lazio's. I lean slightly higher: Lazio have scored 25 in 11 and have a 13-point run from five games, while Lecce have conceded 22, a total only four teams have topped. Losing Tavares takes width away from Lazio's attack, so I would not go much past three goals.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. I lean a little lower because Lazio's home games have averaged about 8.2 corners: Gattuso's side attack through quick wide players such as Noslin and Isaksen rather than by piling crosses in. Lecce away games have also averaged under nine.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly lower: Lazio's games do carry plenty of cards, but Lecce's matches have averaged about 2.7, among the lowest in the league, and the report from Torino mentions only one Lecce booking. There is no referee yet; a strict appointment would change this.

shots.text: The site expects 25.7 shots, and that matches both sides' record: Lazio's home games have averaged about 26 and Lecce's away games about 27. Lazio press high and should shoot more, but Lecce's deep block cuts the quality and number of clear looks, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because Lecce allow about 5.6 on target a game, above the league norm, and their away games have averaged over ten. Frattesi's late runs into the box give Lazio a source of clean, close-range efforts.

401874967.overall: Early view: Roma are unbeaten and third, but they visit PSG in the Champions League four days later, so Gasperini may rotate. Svilar and Dybala are aiming to return here, Pellegrini needs longer, and Roma have five South American internationals travelling back. Parma lose Abdoulaye Ndiaye, sent off for denying a clear chance against Bologna, and Romero went off with a shoulder injury in that game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, mostly Roma's. I stay close to that: Roma score 2.8 a game away, but Parma's games are the lowest-scoring in the league at about 2.4 goals, and Parma's home matches average around two. Ndiaye's ban weakens Parma's back line, which balances out any Roma rotation.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. Both teams point that way: Parma's home games have averaged nine corners and Roma's away games just under nine. Roma win far more corners in Rome than on the road, and a changed side before the PSG game is less likely to pin Parma back for 90 minutes.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I lean lower: Parma's games have averaged only about 2.8 cards, and Roma's away matches about 3.4. Parma played 80 minutes with ten men last time and will be wary of another early red.

shots.text: The site expects 30 shots, nearly 19 of them Roma's. I lean lower because Roma's away games have averaged about 28 shots, against almost 34 at home, and some of their regular attackers may be rested for the PSG trip. Parma themselves average only ten shots a game, the fewest in the league.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Roma's away games run a little above that and Parma's home games a little below, so I see no reason to move. Malen, with eight league goals, is the player most likely to test Parma's keeper.

401875067.overall: Early view: Napoli are tenth with five points from their last five games, and one report describes tension around the club even though Allegri has been backed; Noa Lang has fallen out with the fans after the Lazio draw. They go to Manchester City three days later. Torino lost 15 players to international duty, the most in Serie A, and Abate complained about a lack of energy in the final third after the 1-1 with Lecce.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Napoli's games have often been open (3-3 with Roma, 4-1 at Monza), but they have scored only once, an own goal, in their last two, and one Italian commentator compared their slow build-up to city traffic. Torino took only nine shots at home to Lecce, so the factors cancel out and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners. I lean slightly higher: Napoli's home games average almost 11 corners, and against Lazio they relied on crosses and direct play to get back in the game. Torino's away matches have averaged under nine, so this is a small lean.

cards.text: The numbers already say only 3.0 cards, and I lean a little lower still. Torino's games average about 2.2 cards, the fewest in the league, and Napoli's about 2.7. Neither side plays a pressing, physical game that produces bookings.

shots.text: The site expects 27.8 shots. I lean slightly higher, because Napoli's home games have averaged over 31 shots, with both sides shooting a lot. Torino give up almost 18 shots a game away, and Napoli tend to shoot from distance when they cannot get through.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Napoli's home games and Torino's away games both average a little over nine, but Torino rarely hit the target themselves, so I stay with the number.

401875008.overall: Early view: Spalletti's Juventus are seventh with a long injury list: Yildiz, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez, Locatelli, Khephren Thuram and Grabara all missed the 2-2 at Fiorentina, and Kalulu has a thigh injury that one report says will keep him out for about three weeks. Omonia visit in the Europa League four days later. Venezia have become harder to beat under Davide Nicola and won their last game 2-1 against Udinese.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, mostly Juventus's. I lean lower: Juventus's home games have averaged only 2.2 goals, and their injuries leave the attack relying on Kolo Muani and Woltemade. Nicola has made Venezia tougher to break down, and they score only about 0.6 goals a game away.

corners.text: The site expects 10.9 corners, and I lean higher. Juventus win more corners than anyone in Serie A at 8.5 a game, including 12 at Fiorentina, and their home games average close to 12 in total. A deep-sitting Venezia should give them plenty more.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean slightly higher: opponents collect about 2.5 bookings a game in Turin as they chase the ball, and Venezia are fighting to stay up. Juventus picked up three bookings at Fiorentina, including Kolo Muani for dissent.

shots.text: The site expects 30.4 shots. I lean lower, because Juventus's home games have averaged only about 22 shots: they control the ball but create few chances, and opponents take only seven shots a game in Turin. Without Yildiz there is even less creativity.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean lower: Juventus's home games have averaged about 6.4 on target, the lowest home figure of any of the bigger clubs. Venezia's own finishing away from home is poor, with about three on target a game.

401875047.overall: Early view: Palladino's Bologna have won four in a row and Orsolini is back from injury, scoring the winning penalty at Parma, though Miranda went off injured in that game. Udinese are bottom with one point from five games and, according to Tuttomercatoweb, have already replaced Runjaic with Paolo Zanetti. Neither side has a European game to worry about.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Bologna are in form and had 33 shots at Parma, while Udinese have let in 2.2 goals a game away and 25 in total. Udinese's new coach has had little time to fix the defence, and striker Davis has yet to score in the league, which keeps this mostly about Bologna.

corners.text: The site expects 9.5 corners. Bologna's home games average about 10.6 and Udinese's away games about 8.6, which lands right on the number. Bologna's wide pairs such as Cambiaghi and Orsolini do produce corners, but I see no strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Bologna's home games have been among the most card-heavy in the league, at almost six on average, while Udinese's away games have been very calm. These pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The site expects 26.2 shots. I lean slightly higher: Udinese allow about 15.5 shots a game and Bologna's attack is in form, with Orsolini, Bernardeschi and Odgaard all providing shots. Udinese also take more than 13 shots a game away, so this should not be one-way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean higher because Udinese concede 6.2 shots on target a game, the second-worst figure in Serie A, and their away games have averaged nearly ten. A team in front of a new coach is often slow to fix that.

401874960.overall: Early view: Sassuolo sacked Aquilani after five straight defeats, and multiple reports say Roberto D'Aversa is taking over, though that was not official when this was written; this would be his first game. Genoa lost 2-1 to Milan but out-shot them 17-6, after three straight wins, and De Rossi had an almost full squad. Both sides are near the bottom, so the result matters to both.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Sassuolo's games have been the highest-scoring in Serie A at over four a game, but a new coach usually starts by making his side harder to beat, and Genoa's games average only about 2.5 goals. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 8.9 corners. I lean lower: Sassuolo's home games have averaged under eight corners and Genoa's away games about 7.4. Neither side builds its attack around crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean slightly higher: both sides' games have averaged a little over four cards at these venues, and this is a nervy game near the bottom with a new coach demanding effort. Genoa collected two more bookings against Milan, and Sassuolo had a red card at home to Lazio last month.

shots.text: The site expects 24.7 shots, close to what both teams produce: Sassuolo's home games have averaged about 25 shots and Genoa's away games about 24. Genoa did take 17 shots against Milan, so a small move up is possible, but not enough to lean.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because Sassuolo allow 6.8 on target a game, the most in the league, and their home games have averaged over ten. Genoa's own accuracy is poor, so the lean is small.

401874989.overall: Early view: Amorim's Milan beat Genoa before the break despite a long injury list (Pavlovic, Tomori, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and keeper Terracciano), and the squad only returns to training on 16 November. They go to Olympiacos in the Europa League four days later. Frosinone lost 1-0 at Cagliari despite 29 shots, top scorer Raimondo went off injured, and Bracaglia serves a one-match ban for five yellow cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. That fits both teams: Milan's home games have averaged four goals and Frosinone's away games about 3.4. Bracaglia's ban weakens Frosinone's defence, but Raimondo's injury (eight goals) blunts their attack, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.9 corners. Milan's games are the quietest in the league for corners, under seven a game, but Frosinone's are the busiest at over 13, with eight a game for Frosinone away. Milan let opponents have the ball and are happy to defend crosses, so Frosinone should take most of the corners here. That leaves me at the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean lower: Milan's home games have averaged only about 2.6 cards, and Frosinone's pressing has not produced many bookings, at 1.7 a game. The Genoa game, with four Milan bookings, was more heated than usual.

shots.text: The site expects 33.4 shots. I lean lower because Milan's home games have averaged only about 21 shots: they take few shots and score from them, as they did at Genoa with six shots and two goals. Frosinone will shoot a lot, but even so, 33 looks high for a game at San Siro.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Milan's home games average about 8.8, and Frosinone may be without Raimondo, the main finisher in a side that missed chance after chance at Cagliari. Calò is the other Frosinone player who regularly tests keepers.

401875001.overall: Early view: Sarri's Atalanta ended a month without a win by beating Monza 1-0, but one report says that only bought him time, and his injury list is long (Gaetano, Bellanova, Kristensen, Hien, Raspadori and Kossounou). Chivu's Inter won 2-0 against Como, but Lautaro has been out with a muscle injury since 15 October and Bonny was hurt against Como, so Thuram and Pio Esposito carry the attack. Inter host Stuttgart in the Champions League three days later, and Atalanta go to Borac Banja Luka in the Conference League.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean slightly lower: Inter's striker cover is thin with Lautaro and Bonny injured, and Atalanta lost 3-0 at home to Parma before scraping a 1-0 at Monza. Atalanta's home games still average 3.6 goals, so the lean is small.

corners.text: The site expects 9.6 corners. I lean slightly higher: Atalanta's home games have averaged about ten and Inter's away games just over ten. Inter's wide players Dimarco and Spence attack the flanks, and that produces corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean higher: this is a big game for an Atalanta side under pressure, and Inter's away games have averaged over four cards. Atalanta's home games have been unusually calm, so the referee will matter here.

shots.text: The site expects 28.8 shots. I lean higher because Atalanta's home games have averaged about 33 shots and Inter's away games about 31. Both teams shoot often, and Atalanta at home go forward even against the leaders.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, since Atalanta's home games have produced about 12 on target and Inter away about nine. Carnesecchi was busy at Monza, and Inter's counters through Thuram usually end with a shot on target.

401875009.overall: Early view: Monza have lost four in a row and Juric was sent off at the end of the 1-0 defeat to Atalanta (the length of any touchline ban was not known when this was written). Monza still had the better of the first half in that game and have Serie A's top scorer in Gustavo Varela (nine goals). Fiorentina are up to 15th after beating Sassuolo and drawing 2-2 with Juventus, but they are missing Parisi (cruciate ligament), Pongracic, Ranieri and Atta, and De Gea's form in goal is under scrutiny.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: Fiorentina's away games have averaged about 4.4 goals and Monza's home games 3.6. De Gea has the lowest save rate among regular Serie A keepers, and Monza, with Varela up front, will attack.

corners.text: The site expects 9.5 corners. I lean slightly higher because Sassuolo's away games have averaged about 11.5 corners, with Sassuolo conceding more than seven a game on the road. Venezia's wing-back Hainaut is a regular source of crosses.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean slightly higher: this is a tense game at the bottom between two sides fighting for every point. Venezia have been booked about two times a game at home.

shots.text: The site expects 29.0 shots. Venezia's home games have averaged about 30 shots and Sassuolo's away games about 33, but two new coaches setting up to avoid defeat would bring that down. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Sassuolo allow more shots on target than anyone in Serie A, but Venezia rarely hit the target. I stay with the number.

401875107.overall: Early view: Fiorentina are near the bottom under Vanoli despite three games unbeaten before the break, with Parisi out until at least January and Pongracic, Ranieri and Atta also injured, and De Gea's form in goal criticised. Cagliari under Pisacane play compact and on the counter, and they stopped a four-game losing run with a 1-0 win over Frosinone. Neither side plays in Europe.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly higher: Fiorentina's home games have averaged 3.4 goals, with Fiorentina conceding 2.2 a game at home, and De Gea has the lowest save rate of any regular Serie A keeper. Cagliari's away games average three goals.

corners.text: The site expects 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Fiorentina's home games have averaged about 12 corners, and Cagliari concede about 6.5 corners a game. Pellegrino said Fiorentina worked all week on set pieces before scoring from one against Juventus.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean lower because Cagliari's away games have averaged under two cards, among the calmest in Serie A. Fiorentina's home games are a little higher, but not enough to reach four.

shots.text: The site expects 29.8 shots. I lean slightly higher: Fiorentina's home games have averaged almost 33 shots, with Fiorentina taking 19 a game, and Cagliari allow almost 19 shots a game. Cagliari's counter-attacking style means they shoot less.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Fiorentina's home games have averaged about 11 on target, but Cagliari's compact defence forces a lot of blocked shots, as against Frosinone's 29 attempts. I stay with the number.

401875541.overall: Early view: leaders PSV go to Nijmegen straight after the break and three days before a Champions League trip to Real Madrid on 24 November, so Peter Bosz is likely to rotate again. NEC have won two league games in a row and beat Omonia in the Europa League, but they host Rennes in Europe five days later too.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals. I lean a little lower: PSV have used 21 different starters this season and the Madrid trip makes another reshuffle likely, and NEC's league run before their win at Utrecht was mostly draws. Sven Mijnans' hat-trick form keeps three or four goals well in play, but five or more needs a lot to go right.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners and I see no reason to move. NEC under Dick Schreuder have just scored three at Utrecht and will look to attack at home, which should stop this being a one-way game, while PSV's wide play through Ruben van Bommel usually earns its share of corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. Nothing in the news points to a bad-tempered game: no recent bans for either side and no derby element. NEC chasing the leader could pick up a few tactical fouls, which is already inside the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots, with 15 for NEC. I lean lower because that home figure looks high against the league leaders, and a rotated PSV side with Madrid in mind may manage the game rather than chase volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11 shots on target. I lean a little lower for the same reason as the shots: a PSV side shuffled before Madrid and an NEC team that has scored freely only in the last week. Mijnans and Tadic are the players most likely to test the keepers.

401875544.overall: Early view: FC Utrecht come out of the break in crisis after losing 4-2 at Telstar and 3-2 at home to NEC, with Anthony Correia admitting set pieces and the defence are a problem. Cambuur's Johan Plat was October's Coach of the Month, but shipped five at home to PSV and, by one report, have lost captain Amofa for the season.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, already a very high figure. Utrecht have conceded seven in two games and Cambuur let in five against PSV, so the goals case is real, but Correia has spent the break drilling his defence. I stay with the number rather than push it higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, mostly Utrecht's. A home side needing a win should push Cambuur back, which fits the split, and nothing I read points to a change in either team's approach.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean a touch higher: Utrecht are 14th and under real pressure, Correia talked of cracking the whip, and frustrated home sides that fall behind tend to collect bookings. Cambuur's crowd trouble at the PSV game also shows the club's matches can get heated.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Utrecht's 17.5 fits a home side forced to attack, and Cambuur created enough to score twice even against PSV, so I agree with the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Both defences are leaking, which supports the estimate, but neither attack has been especially sharp outside their best days, so I do not move it.

401875543.overall: Early view: Feyenoord host Excelsior in the Rotterdam derby after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen, five games without a win and top spot gone; Giovanni van Bronckhorst says this one must be won. Porto visit De Kuip in the Champions League three days later. Excelsior have lost five league games in a row, including 0-9 to Twente, though the 0-1 against Go Ahead Eagles was closer.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals. Feyenoord should score, but goalkeeper Tjark Ernst is conceding more than expected by Opta's numbers and Excelsior have not scored in two games, so the home side carries almost all of it. I agree with the total rather than move it.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I lean higher: after the 0-9 at Twente Excelsior's priority under Ruben den Uil will be a compact low block, and a Feyenoord side desperate for a win will pile on crosses and blocked shots.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. It is a derby, Excelsior will defend deep and foul to stop counters, and Feyenoord are under pressure after five games without a win, which tends to bring rash challenges and protests. I lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots with 19 for Feyenoord. That matches a one-sided game against a team defending deep, and the Porto game three days later could see some rotation that stops it climbing further.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because Excelsior's 3.1 looks generous for a team that has gone two games without scoring, and a packed defence blocks many of Feyenoord's attempts.

401875546.overall: Early view: the Derby van het Noorden comes with FC Groningen missing keeper Etienne Vaessen (second yellow at AZ) and Hans Hateboer (red card, one-match settlement accepted); both bans are one match and are served here. Heerenveen arrive on five straight wins including the 5-3 over Feyenoord, while Groningen lost their last two league games (2-3 to Sparta, 4-3 at AZ) and went out of the cup.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean higher: Groningen's last two league games finished 2-3 and 3-4, a reserve keeper replaces Vaessen, and Heerenveen just scored five against Feyenoord with Ringo Meerveld off the bench.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, split evenly. Groningen press high under Dick Lukkien and Heerenveen are confident going forward, so both should get into the final third; I see nothing to move the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean higher: it is the northern derby, Groningen finished their last game with nine men and their own director says Vaessen's temper hurts the team, and the rivalry rarely stays calm.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Two teams who both attack and a home side under pressure to respond fits this volume; I keep it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because Heerenveen's attack is in its best spell of the season and Groningen have scored through Ondrejka, Willumsson and Van Bergen in recent weeks, so both sides should test the keepers.

401875539.overall: Early view: Alex Pastoor's first match in charge of PEC Zwolle, appointed on 7 November, partly on a trial basis. Telstar are 16th but beat Utrecht 4-2 and came back from 2-0 down at Fortuna with two set-piece goals; one report says fans turned on coach Henk Brugge after their cup exit, so pressure is on both sides of this relegation-zone game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean a little lower: PEC have scored only 13 in 12 games and a new coach usually starts by tightening the team, while a 16th v 13th game tends to be cagey. Telstar's set pieces are the main route to goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Telstar's set-piece threat makes corners valuable to them, and the home side should earn more of them, but nothing suggests a big change from the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. I lean higher because this is a relegation six-pointer between two nervy sides, and Telstar's 1.1 home cards looks low for a team that needs the points as badly as they do.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, 18.5 of them Telstar's. I lean lower: that is a big home figure for a team in 16th, and PEC under a new coach are likely to sit compact rather than open up.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. With PEC's low scoring and a likely cautious first game under Pastoor, I expect fewer clean chances than the estimate.

401875545.overall: Early view: FC Twente beat Excelsior 9-0 and outplayed Ajax in a 2-2 draw, and now host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points, lost 7-0 at PSV and only drew 1-1 with PEC in Jurgen Streppel's first weeks. Twente travel to Freiburg in the Conference League four days later, so John van den Brom may rest one or two players.

goals.text: The numbers say 4 goals. I lean higher: Wout Weghorst scored four and Sondre Orjasaeter made five assists in the 9-0 two weeks ago, and Willem II have a goal difference of -29 after 12 games.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners. I lean higher: Willem II had no shots in the first half at PSV and will defend deep, and Twente produce many crosses for Weghorst; their first goal against Ajax came from a corner.

cards.text: The numbers say 3 cards. A one-sided game usually brings few home bookings and some for a chasing away side, which is what the split shows; nothing points elsewhere.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.7 shots, 28 of them Twente's. That is already huge; Twente's attack justifies it, but possible rotation before Freiburg stops me going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target. Twente's finishing has been sharp, but Willem II's 2.6 looks generous, so the total balances out at about the estimate.

401875547.overall: Early view: Ajax drew 2-2 at Twente after five straight wins and host ADO four days before Thun in the Conference League and a week before the Klassieker, so Michel may rotate (Ajax change the most starters in the league). ADO sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and won 3-1 against Sparta under interim Levi Schwiebbe; Voetbal International reports Maurice Steijn is set to return as coach, not yet confirmed by the club when I checked.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. Ajax have the league's in-form striker in Tolu Arokodare, and ADO have conceded 25 in 12, but Ajax often lack control and a new-coach lift for ADO could make them harder to break. I stay with the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. I lean higher: Ajax build much of their threat around crosses for Tolu's headers, and ADO, playing away with possibly a new coach, will likely sit deep and concede corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. No bans or rivalry issues stand out; ADO's tactical fouls against a dominant home side fit the away-heavy split.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, 23.5 for Ajax. I lean lower: Ajax were outshot for long spells at Twente and with Thun and Feyenoord coming, Michel is likely to rotate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. ADO's keeper Kilian Nikiema made key saves against Sparta but plays for Burkina Faso as late as 17 November, and five other ADO players are also away on international duty. Ajax should create enough to reach the estimate, so I keep it.

401875540.overall: Early view: AZ came back from 1-3 to beat Groningen 4-3 and visit Sparta four days before a Europa League trip to Sparta Prague. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO and were knocked out of the cup by Fortuna, and one report says goalkeeper Brouwer went off with an ankle injury at ADO.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. I lean higher: AZ's games have been open (4-3 v Groningen, 19 shots in the 0-1 loss to Ajax), Sparta conceded three at ADO and scored three at Groningen, and Sparta may be without first-choice keeper Brouwer.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners. AZ attack a lot down the flanks with Daal and Dijkstra, which supports the figure, and I see nothing to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. No bans or special tension point either way; Sparta are mid-table and AZ need points to stay near the top four.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots. I lean higher because AZ shoot often, 19 times even in defeat against Ajax, and Sparta hit the post and kept attacking at ADO.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. AZ's volume is high but their finishing has come and gone, and Kees Smit, back from injury, adds quality; overall the estimate looks right.

401875542.overall: Early view: Go Ahead Eagles' last two league wins were both 1-0, with top scorer Mats Tengstedt deciding them and Jasper Cillessen keeping clean sheets again, either side of a 4-0 defeat at Cambuur. Fortuna Sittard sit 7th after a run of draws, including 2-2 with Telstar after leading 2-0, and coach Danny Buijs says injuries are piling up.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: the win at Excelsior was described as very dull, Go Ahead's last two wins were 1-0, and Fortuna have drawn four of their last five.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Go Ahead taking most. Neither side's style points to a big change, so I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. Both sides are well disciplined by Eredivisie standards and nothing in the news, no bans or rivalry, suggests a tetchy game.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. I lean lower: Go Ahead's recent wins have been tight, low-chance games, and a Fortuna side short of fit players is unlikely to open up away from home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With Cillessen in form and two teams who have played tight games lately, I expect fewer clear chances than the estimate.

401875536.overall: Early view: Groningen host bottom side Willem II on a Friday night six days after the northern derby. Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer, listed as missing, will have served their one-match bans against Heerenveen and should be available again. Willem II have 3 points and lost 7-0 at PSV, but drew 1-1 with PEC under new coach Jurgen Streppel.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Groningen's games have been high-scoring (2-3, 3-4) and Willem II leak goals, but with Vaessen back in goal I see no reason to go above the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners. I lean a little higher: Groningen press high and Willem II will spend long spells defending deep, as they did at PSV.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. Vaessen's temper is a known risk, but against a team this far below them Groningen should rarely be under pressure; I keep the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.3 shots, mostly Groningen's. That fits a home side with Ondrejka, Willumsson and Van Bergen all scoring against a team in last place.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. Groningen's attack has been productive even in defeat, which supports the figure.

401875537.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between 15th and 16th. Excelsior have lost five league games in a row, including 0-9 to Twente, and failed to score in two games; Telstar are more lively, beating Utrecht 4-2 and coming back at Fortuna from set pieces, with Tyrone Owusu named Player of the Month for October.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean lower: Excelsior have not scored in two games and will be wary after the 0-9, and games this close to the drop zone tend to be cagey. Telstar's set pieces are the likeliest source of goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Telstar's set-piece focus makes each corner dangerous but does not obviously add more of them; I keep the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. I lean higher: two teams in the bottom four with a lot riding on the result, and Excelsior's Nesto Groen showed the side's nerves with a red card inside five minutes at Twente.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. Both teams have created little lately apart from Telstar's good week, so I agree with the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. Given Excelsior's blunt attack and a likely tight game, I lean a little lower.

401875531.overall: Early view: PSV host Go Ahead Eagles four days after visiting Real Madrid in the Champions League. PSV beat Willem II 7-0 and Cambuur 5-2 in their last two league games with Mijnans in hat-trick form, but Go Ahead's last two wins were 1-0 with Cillessen keeping clean sheets and Tengstedt scoring, even if they also lost 4-0 at Cambuur.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.4 goals. I lean lower: Go Ahead's last two wins were 1-0 with Cillessen in form, and PSV usually rotate after a midweek game, which has cost them points this season. The 4-0 loss at Cambuur shows Go Ahead can still collapse, so three or four goals remains the likely range.

corners.text: The numbers say 11 corners, mostly PSV's. Go Ahead will defend deep at the Philips Stadion and PSV's wide play fits the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards. No rivalry, no bans in the news and a probably dominant home side; I keep it.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots. PSV's attacking volume at home justifies a high figure even with rotation, and Go Ahead will mostly look to counter through Tengstedt.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target. With Cillessen in form and a rotated PSV attack, I lean slightly lower.

401875530.overall: Early view: Cambuur have been strong at home (4-0 against Go Ahead before that game was abandoned, a win over PEC) and Johan Plat was October's Coach of the Month, but they lost 5-2 to PSV and, by one report, captain Amofa is out for the season. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO, went out of the cup and may have a goalkeeper issue after Brouwer's ankle injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals. I lean lower: that is a big figure for 10th against 12th, Sparta scored only once at ADO, and Cambuur are without their captain. Over two and a half still looks the more likely side.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners split almost evenly. Nothing in the news changes how either side plays, so I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean lower: it is not a derby or a relegation game, neither side has bans or discipline issues in the news, and 2.5 cards for Sparta away looks high for a mid-table team.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. Cambuur's home attack and Sparta's habit of creating chances (they hit the post at ADO) fit the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. A possible reserve keeper for Sparta matters for goals more than shots, so I keep it.

401875538.overall: Early view: a relegation scrap between 17th and 14th. ADO sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and beat Sparta 3-1 under interim Levi Schwiebbe; Voetbal International reports Maurice Steijn is set to return as coach. Utrecht are sinking, with Anthony Correia pointing to set pieces and the defence after conceding seven in two games.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Both defences are poor (ADO conceded 25 in 12, Utrecht seven in two games), but the stakes usually make these games tense, so I keep the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I lean higher: ADO scored from a corner against Sparta and Utrecht's set-piece defending is a known weakness, so ADO have every reason to force corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean higher: two clubs near the bottom, a coach under pressure in Correia and a home crowd that will push ADO on.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots. I lean lower: two struggling teams in a must-not-lose game usually play with caution, and neither attack has been prolific.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. For the same reasons, I expect fewer clean chances than the estimate.

401875535.overall: Early view: the Klassieker at De Kuip with Feyenoord and Ajax level on 25 points. Feyenoord play Porto at home on 24 November and have gone five games without a win, while Ajax play Thun on 26 November, so they have two days less to recover; Ajax have also struggled in big games this season.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean higher: Feyenoord's keeper Tjark Ernst has been conceding more than expected, Ajax lost control in the second half at Twente after leading 2-0, and Tolu Arokodare's heading is a constant threat.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, mostly Feyenoord's at home. Both sides cross a lot, but nothing in the news shifts the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean higher: it is the biggest rivalry in the country, both teams are under pressure, and Ajax's Sofyan Amrabat is criticised for diving into too many duels.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots. Feyenoord at home should have more of the ball, and Ajax's midweek game may make them more cautious; I agree with the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both attacks have quality, and both keepers have been unconvincing at times; I keep it.

401875534.overall: Early view: Heerenveen have won five in a row, including 5-3 against Feyenoord, with a defence that eredivisie.nl credits for their rise. Fortuna sit 7th after a run of draws and Danny Buijs is worried about injuries, saying the squad is being overworked.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. Fortuna draw a lot but conceded two set-piece goals against Telstar, and Heerenveen have scored freely; these cancel out, so I keep the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Nothing in the news changes how these teams play, so I see no reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. Two disciplined mid-table sides with no rivalry; Heerenveen coach Robin Veldman's own booking at Feyenoord was a one-off.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. I lean slightly higher because Heerenveen's attack is in its best form of the season and Fortuna will need to attack at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. With Heerenveen's attack sharp and Fortuna's defence stretched by injuries, I lean slightly higher.

401875532.overall: Early view: AZ go to Zwolle on Sunday afternoon, three days after a Europa League away game at Sparta Prague. PEC will be in their third match under Alex Pastoor, appointed on 7 November, and have only 13 goals in 12 games; AZ broke a poor run by coming back from 1-3 to beat Groningen 4-3.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. AZ's recent games have been wild, but PEC rarely score and Pastoor's first job is to make them harder to beat, while AZ will have travelled back from Prague. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, 5.8 for AZ. AZ's wide players Ro-Zangelo Daal and Elijah Dijkstra create plenty of crossing positions even when the team is rotated, so I keep the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. There is no rivalry here and no bans in the news; a PEC side defending deep may commit a few fouls, which the away-light split already reflects.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, 17 of them AZ's. I lean lower: AZ will be on their third game in a week after a Thursday night in Prague, and Leeroy Echteld is likely to rotate, which usually takes the edge off their shot volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. With PEC's blunt attack (13 goals in 12) and a probably tired AZ, I expect a little less than the estimate.

401875533.overall: Early view: NEC and Twente both play European games on Thursday 26 November, NEC at home to Rennes and Twente away at Freiburg, so both arrive with three days' rest on a Sunday night. NEC won their last two league games and beat Omonia 3-1, while Twente beat Excelsior 9-0 and were the better side in the 2-2 with Ajax.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean higher: Twente's attack with Wout Weghorst and Sondre Orjasaeter is the sharpest in the league right now, NEC's last two games finished 3-2 and 3-1, and tired legs after Thursday games usually make defending harder.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, close to even. Twente cross a lot and NEC will attack at home, which already fits the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. No rivalry, no bans in the news and two teams that both want the ball; I keep it.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.5 shots. Both sides attack, but fatigue from European games could cut both ways, more space but less intensity, so I keep the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because both attacks are in form, with Dusan Tadic scoring twice at Utrecht and Twente hitting the target often against Ajax.

401875522.overall: Early view: Telstar host Groningen on a Friday night. The brief lists Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer as missing, but both bans were one match and will have been served in the northern derby on 21 November, so both should be available. Telstar are in the play-off place but beat Utrecht 4-2 and drew 2-2 at Fortuna, and one report says fans turned on coach Henk Brugge after the cup exit.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Telstar have scored six in two league games and Groningen's last two finished 2-3 and 3-4, so goals are likely; with Vaessen back I do not push it above the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Telstar lean on set pieces and Groningen press high, but neither fact changes how many corners the game should produce.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean higher: Groningen finished their AZ game with nine men and their own director says Vaessen's temper hurts the team, and Telstar are fighting to stay up.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Both sides have been creating chances lately, which fits the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.4 shots on target. I lean a little lower: Telstar's recent goals came largely from set pieces rather than open-play shooting, and 6.3 on target for Groningen away looks high.

401875521.overall: Early view: bottom side Willem II host Feyenoord, who travel to Norway to face Viking in the Champions League three days later. Willem II have 3 points and lost 7-0 at PSV but drew 1-1 with PEC under Jurgen Streppel; Feyenoord's state will depend on how they handle Excelsior, Porto and Ajax before this.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals. Feyenoord should score freely against a team with a -29 goal difference, but Van Bronckhorst may rest players before Viking and his side have been leaking goals too, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. I lean higher: Willem II had no shots in the first half at PSV and will defend deep, which typically means many blocked shots and crosses turned behind.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards. No rivalry, no bans in the news and a likely one-sided game; I keep it.

shots.text: The numbers say 30 shots. Willem II's 11.4 looks high and Feyenoord's 18.6 looks low to me, but the total is about right for this kind of mismatch.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Feyenoord's quality should supply most of these; possible rotation before Viking keeps me from going higher.

401875523.overall: Early view: Sparta host NEC, who travel to Armenia in the Europa League five days later. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO and went out of the cup, and one report says keeper Brouwer injured his ankle; NEC came into the break on two league wins and a European win.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean a little higher: Sparta conceded three at ADO and may still be without Brouwer, and NEC's attack around Dusan Tadic has scored six in two games.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners. Both teams attack down the flanks, but nothing in the news changes that; I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. No rivalry or bans stand out, and the figure is already on the high side for a mid-table game.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots, with NEC taking more. That fits an NEC side that has been on the front foot, so I agree.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. NEC's form supports it, and Sparta created enough at ADO to hit the post; I keep the estimate.

401875527.overall: Early view: AZ host leaders PSV four days before PSV face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League and five days before AZ host Sturm Graz in the Europa League. AZ outshot Ajax 19 to 5 at home and still lost 0-1, while PSV have dropped points to ADO and Twente this season.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. I lean lower: games between top-five sides have been tighter this season (AZ 0-1 Ajax), and both coaches have a European game the following week to manage.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, evenly split. AZ's wing play and PSV's possession should both produce corners; I see no reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. Big games can get tense, but neither side has bans or disciplinary trouble in the news, so I keep it.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots. I lean higher: AZ shot 19 times at home against Ajax and PSV rarely go a game without plenty of attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10 shots on target. AZ's volume has not always turned into shots on goal, which balances the higher shot count; I keep it.

401875526.overall: Early view: Fortuna host PEC, who will be about four weeks into Alex Pastoor's spell as coach. Fortuna have drawn four of their last five and Danny Buijs is worried about injuries; PEC have scored only 13 in 12 games and drew 1-1 at bottom side Willem II.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. I lean lower: PEC's attack is one of the weakest in the league, Fortuna keep drawing, and a new coach usually makes PEC more cautious away from home.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Nothing in either team's news points to a change in style, so I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. Mid-table against lower half, no rivalry and no bans; I agree with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. Fortuna should have more of the ball at home, and that is already in the split.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With PEC's low scoring and Fortuna's injury problems, I expect a little less.

401875524.overall: Early view: in-form Heerenveen host Cambuur in a Frisian derby. Heerenveen won five in a row including the 5-3 against Feyenoord, with eredivisie.nl crediting their defence for the rise; Cambuur's Johan Plat was October's Coach of the Month, but Cambuur lost 5-2 at home to PSV and, by one report, are without captain Amofa for the rest of the season.

goals.text: The numbers say 4 goals. I lean lower: Heerenveen's run has been built on defence (a 1-0 win over NEC before the Feyenoord game), and Cambuur without their captain may struggle to keep up with Heerenveen's pace.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, mostly Heerenveen's. That fits a home side in form, and I see no reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. I lean a touch higher because this is a Frisian derby, and Cambuur's game with PSV showed how heated their fans can make things.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Heerenveen's attack, with Ringo Meerveld in form, should produce most of them, which matches the split.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Heerenveen's finishing is sharp, but Cambuur's attack will be weaker without Amofa; I keep it.

401875528.overall: Early view: Ajax host Utrecht a week after the Klassieker and four days before a Conference League trip to Sint-Truiden. Utrecht went into the break after losing 4-2 at Telstar and 3-2 at home to NEC, with coach Anthony Correia naming set pieces as a big problem, which suits Ajax's aerial threat through Tolu Arokodare.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean higher: Utrecht's set-piece defending is poor by their coach's own account, Tolu scores many of Ajax's goals with his head, and Utrecht have conceded seven in two games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. I lean slightly higher: Ajax will want corners against a team that struggles to defend them, and Utrecht will likely sit deep after their recent defeats.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. No rivalry or bans in the news; Utrecht's pressure may cause some frustration, but that is already in the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots. Ajax may rotate before Sint-Truiden, but they should still dominate at home; I keep it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Ajax have finishing quality, and Utrecht scored twice even in defeat to NEC, so I agree.

401875525.overall: Early view: Go Ahead host Twente four days before Twente's Conference League trip to AGF in Denmark. Go Ahead's last two wins were both 1-0 with Mats Tengstedt scoring and Jasper Cillessen keeping clean sheets, though they also lost 4-0 at Cambuur in a game later abandoned; Twente have scored heavily all autumn.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean a little lower: Go Ahead's home games with Cillessen in goal have been tight, and Twente may rotate before AGF.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, Twente taking most. Twente's crossing game with Weghorst fits that; I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards. Both teams are fairly disciplined and there is no rivalry or ban news; I keep the low figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.5 shots, 20 of them Twente's. That is a lot for an away side, but Twente have been dominant, so I agree.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. Cillessen's form and a deep Go Ahead defence that blocks shots suggest a little less.

401875529.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between ADO (17th) and Excelsior (15th). ADO beat Sparta 3-1 under interim Levi Schwiebbe and, according to Voetbal International, are set to bring back Maurice Steijn as coach; Excelsior have lost five league games in a row and scored none in their last two.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean lower: games between two teams in the bottom four tend to be tight, and Excelsior have not scored in two games.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, evenly split. ADO's set-piece goals make their corners dangerous, but neither team's style changes the count; I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3 cards. I lean higher: two teams near the bottom with a lot at stake, and Excelsior's Nesto Groen showed how nervy they have been with a red card inside five minutes at Twente.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. ADO at home should take more of them, which is already in the split.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. ADO scored three against Sparta, but Excelsior have been blunt; I keep the estimate.

401915380.overall: Early view: Bodo/Glimt sit 25th with 4 points after a 0-0 at home to Lille on matchday 4, while LASK climbed to 16th by beating bottom side Slovan Bratislava 4-0. I found little fresh team news for either club, so this view rests mainly on the matchday 4 results and the table; a late-November night on the artificial pitch at Aspmyra is the one thing the numbers may underrate.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which looks high for this pairing. Bodo/Glimt's last home game in this competition was a 0-0 with Lille, and LASK's 4-0 came against a Slovan side that has lost every game, so I would not read too much into it. I expect something nearer three goals than four.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners and I have nothing that moves it. Bodo/Glimt kept pressing at home against Lille without scoring, which usually means corners, but LASK's win over Slovan came mostly from open play and a free kick. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and I lean slightly lower. The Bodo/Glimt v Lille game produced only two bookings, and LASK's win over Slovan had two, both for the visitors. Neither side has shown a pattern of feisty European games so far.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots. Bodo/Glimt kept attacking in the goalless draw with Lille, and LASK showed against Slovan that they will shoot from set plays and distance (Kasper Jorgensen scored a free kick). Nothing I found points away from the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, which needs both sides to be sharp. Bodo/Glimt failed to score at home to Lille, and LASK's finishing against Slovan came against the weakest defence in the competition. I expect a little fewer efforts on target than the estimate.

401915300.overall: Early view: Galatasaray (18th, 6 points) beat Stuttgart 2-0 on matchday 4 with two early goals from Alexey Batrakov, while Aston Villa lost their perfect record with a 3-0 defeat in Barcelona and then drew 4-4 at Manchester United. Villa have conceded seven goals in two games and Unai Emery stormed off the touchline at Old Trafford, so the visitors arrive less settled than their 6th place suggests; Emery is in talks over a new contract, so his position itself is not in question.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean a little higher. Villa have just conceded three at Barcelona and four at Old Trafford, plus a late Fulham equaliser from a Zion Suzuki error, while Galatasaray scored twice in 15 minutes against Stuttgart. Galatasaray started fast against Stuttgart, and Villa's defence is the weak point right now.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I have nothing that moves it much. Galatasaray scored early against Stuttgart and then sat on the lead, which limits their corner count, and Villa were outplayed in Barcelona. A fairly even split of around nine looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and I lean higher. Galatasaray's game with Stuttgart produced eight yellow cards, and Villa collected three in the first half alone in Barcelona (Ian Maatsen, Emiliano Buendia, Nicolas Jackson). A loud Istanbul crowd and a side under pressure points to a busy night for the referee.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots and I stay close to it. Galatasaray scored twice early against Stuttgart and Villa's recent games have been open, with eight goals at Old Trafford. Nothing I found argues for a big move either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Villa's leaky defence argues for more Galatasaray efforts on goal, but Villa's own attack was shut out in Barcelona, so the two effects roughly cancel. I stay with the estimate.

401915295.overall: Early view: Arsenal are 3rd with 10 points and top of the Premier League, but they are winning narrowly: 1-0 at Liverpool, 2-1 at Slavia Prague (a win Mikel Arteta called sloppy) and 1-0 against Hull. Borussia Dortmund (12th, 9 points) beat Real Betis 2-1 on matchday 4 and drew 2-2 at Bayern before that, so they are in decent form; William Saliba is building fitness again after his World Cup injury, which would strengthen Arsenal further.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and I lean lower. Arsenal's last three games ended 1-0, 2-1 and 1-0, and Arteta himself said his side must stop chasing the perfect goal, which tells you the attack is the issue rather than the defence. With Saliba close to a return, a low-scoring home win fits the pattern better than an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I lean slightly higher. When Arsenal struggle to break teams down they keep recycling the ball wide and win corners, and their set pieces are a big part of how they create. Dortmund are likely to defend deep for long spells at the Emirates.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and I lean higher. Dortmund picked up five yellow cards against Betis (Julian Ryerson, Ramy Bensebaini, Joey Veerman and Jobe Bellingham among them), and Arsenal had two booked at Slavia. Arsenal's edge in big games, the 'dark arts' debate around them, tends to draw fouls and bookings from opponents.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and I stay with it. Arsenal will have most of the ball and plenty of attempts, but their recent games have been tight rather than shot-heavy, and Dortmund are good enough to keep it to a measured total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Arsenal's attack has lacked a focal point (Viktor Gyokeres only found form at Slavia), and Arteta has spoken about his side being too careful in the final third. Dortmund's own threat away from home should be limited.

401915296.overall: Early view: Como are the story of the competition, 4th with 9 points after a record 9-1 win at Lens in which Tasos Douvikas scored a hat-trick, although they lost 2-0 at Inter in Serie A on 8 November. AEK Athens (29th, 3 points) pushed Real Madrid hard before losing 3-2, but their scorer that night, Aboubakary Koita, was sent off in stoppage time and is banned for this game (the ban has not yet been served).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean a little higher. Como scored nine at Lens with seven different scorers, and AEK conceded three to Real Madrid at home, so I expect Como to create plenty. AEK also lose Koita, who scored against Madrid, which makes their own goal harder to find but does little to slow Como.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Como will dominate the ball, which pushes their share up, but they score so much from open play (only one of the nine at Lens was a header from Marc-Oliver Kempf) that corner pressure builds less than usual. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and I lean slightly lower. Como's 9-1 at Lens produced only two bookings, both for Lens, as one-sided games tend to. AEK may foul more chasing the ball, but this looks more like a game of three or four cards than five.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and I lean higher. Cesc Fabregas's Como have attacked relentlessly in Europe, and AEK without Koita lose an outlet to relieve pressure. Most of the total should come from the home side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target and I lean higher. Como's attack (Douvikas, Nico Paz, Martin Baturina) is in form and AEK's defence leaked three to Madrid. I expect Como alone to account for most of ten or more efforts on goal.

401915294.overall: Early view: two big names in trouble. Feyenoord are 32nd with 3 points after a 3-0 home defeat by Inter, while Porto (26th, 3 points) got their campaign going by beating Napoli 4-1, with three of the goals headed in. With both near the cut-off for the play-off places, neither side can settle for a draw; I found little fresh team news, so the view leans on the matchday 4 performances.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean a little higher. Porto just scored four against Napoli, and Feyenoord conceded three at home to Inter without reply. Both teams need a win, which tends to keep the game open late.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners and I lean slightly higher. Porto's win over Napoli came largely from set pieces, with headed goals from Jan Bednarek and Jakub Kiwior, so they will try to win corners. Feyenoord at home will also push to recover from the Inter defeat.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and I stay with it. Porto's win over Napoli had seven cards, but most went to a frustrated Napoli side; Feyenoord's defeat by Inter had only two. A tense game between two needy sides fits the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots and I have nothing that moves it. Both teams will attack, but Feyenoord's home display against Inter was flat, which cancels out some of the expected openness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10 shots on target. Porto were efficient against Napoli and Feyenoord's defence was opened up by Inter, but Feyenoord's own attack failed to score. I stay with the estimate.

401915379.overall: Early view: Manchester City are 7th with 9 points but in a poor run, losing three Premier League games in a row (the latest 3-1 at Nottingham Forest) and needing an Erling Haaland winner to beat Leipzig 3-2; Enzo Maresca has defended Gianluigi Donnarumma after his errors. Napoli (27th, 3 points) are in worse shape: beaten 4-1 at Porto and 2-0 at Juventus, and centre-back Rafa Marin is banned after his red card in Porto (ban not yet served).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I stay close to it. City are leaking goals (three conceded to Forest, two to Leipzig) and Napoli have conceded six in their last two games, so both defences are fragile. City's attack leans heavily on Haaland, which is the only thing keeping me from leaning higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. City will have the ball, but pundits have called them predictable and lacking dominance lately, and much of their threat comes through Haaland in the box rather than sustained wide pressure. I see no reason to move the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and I lean higher. Napoli collected four yellows and a red in Porto and finished with ten men at Juventus too, so discipline is an issue for Massimiliano Allegri's side. City also had two late bookings in Leipzig.

shots.text: The numbers say 29 shots. City usually take a lot of shots at home, and Napoli without Rafa Marin may sit deep, but City's recent attacking play has been criticised as predictable. I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Maresca has said City cannot rely only on Haaland for goals, which hints at a lack of clear chances elsewhere. Napoli scored only once in Porto, so their share of efforts on target should be small.

401915299.overall: Early view: a game between two sides near the bottom, both on 3 points. RB Leipzig (30th) lost 3-2 at home to Manchester City on matchday 4 but scored twice, while Lens (33rd) were thrashed 9-1 at home by Como. I found little fresh team news for either club, so this view rests on the matchday 4 results and the table.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and I lean higher. Lens conceded nine at home to Como, which suggests a defence in real trouble, and Leipzig scored twice against City through Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa. Both teams need to win to stay in the hunt for the play-off places.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners and I stay with it. Leipzig should have most of the ball at home, but Lens are likely to defend deep after their heavy defeat, which balances out. I found nothing specific on either side's set-piece approach.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. Leipzig picked up four yellow cards against City (Christoph Baumgartner, Ridle Baku, Neil El Aynaoui, David Raum), but that was against a stronger side; Lens had two in their 9-1 defeat. I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots and I lean a little higher. Lens let Como shoot at will, and Leipzig at home need goals for their goal difference as well as the points. Most of the total should come from the hosts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target and I lean slightly higher. Como put nine past Lens, so their defence is allowing clear chances, and Leipzig's attack showed against City that it can finish. I expect Leipzig to test the Lens goalkeeper often.

401915298.overall: Early view: Real Madrid are 2nd with a perfect 12 points and have won eight in a row under Jose Mourinho, most recently 3-0 at Valencia; Vinicius Junior's suspension is a LaLiga one and does not apply in Europe, though Mourinho says he is not sure of a start. PSV (24th, 4 points) lost 2-1 at home to Club Brugge on matchday 4 and sit on the edge of the play-off places.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.6 goals and I lean lower. Madrid under Mourinho win with control: 3-0 at Valencia and 3-0 at Racing Santander in their last two league games. They did concede twice in Athens, but a home win by two or three goals looks more likely than a five-goal game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I stay with it. Madrid will dominate at the Bernabeu, but they score plenty from open play through Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Arda Guler. Nothing I found moves the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and I lean slightly lower. Madrid's win in Athens had only two bookings before AEK's late red card, and PSV's home defeat by Brugge had three, all for Brugge. One-sided games at the Bernabeu tend not to be card-heavy.

shots.text: The numbers say 31 shots. Madrid's attack is in form, with Bellingham passing 50 goals for the club and Federico Valverde scoring late in Athens, so a high volume is likely. PSV scored at home against Brugge and should add some shots on the break.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.6 shots on target, which is very high. Mourinho's sides tend to slow the game once ahead, and that dampens the second-half total. I lean slightly lower but still expect a busy night for PSV's goalkeeper.

401915297.overall: Early view: Slovan Bratislava are bottom with no points and, under Yaya Toure, hold an unwanted record for consecutive Champions League defeats after losing 4-0 at LASK. Real Betis (11th, 9 points) lost 2-1 at Borussia Dortmund on matchday 4 and need the win to stay in the race for the top eight; Manuel Pellegrini's side should control this game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and I lean a little higher. Slovan conceded four in the first half and early second half at LASK, and their defensive record in this competition is the worst of the 36. Betis scored in Dortmund through Aitor Ruibal and have enough creativity, with Isco and Antony, to score several.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I stay with it. Betis should have most of the ball and win most of the corners, but if they score early the game may lose its intensity. Nothing I found argues strongly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Betis picked up five yellow cards in Dortmund, but that was a tight away game against a strong side; here they should be in control. Slovan had two players booked at LASK. The two effects cancel, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, which already reflects Betis's expected dominance. Slovan created little at LASK, so almost all the volume depends on Betis, which makes a figure above 31 hard to support. I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Betis should test the Slovan goalkeeper often, but the hosts' own contribution will be small. I see no reason to move away from the estimate.

401915378.overall: Early view: Barcelona (5th, 9 points) arrive in strong form after beating Aston Villa 3-0 and Atletico Madrid 2-1 to lead LaLiga, but Lamine Yamal has a knee problem that ruled him out of Spain's next game and Rodri has a hamstring injury. Sabah (31st, 3 points) lost 4-1 at Viking and are without Aden McCarthy, sent off in that game (ban not yet served). The long trip to Baku and a busy league schedule make some Barcelona rotation likely.

goals.text: The numbers say 5.2 goals, which looks too high. Barcelona should win comfortably, but with Yamal's knee a doubt and Hansi Flick possibly resting players for the long trip east, a 3-0 or 4-0 looks more likely than a five-goal rout. Sabah did score at Viking, so a consolation goal is possible.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I lean slightly higher. Barcelona will camp in Sabah's half and the hosts will defend deep, which is how corners build up. Even a rotated Barcelona side keeps the ball for long spells.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Sabah had two players booked and one sent off at Viking, so tired defending late in the game could add bookings. Barcelona usually pick up few cards in one-sided games. I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.8 shots and I stay with it. Even without Yamal, Barcelona have Raphinha in form (two goals against Villa) and Fermin Lopez fresh from a brace at Atletico, so the shot count will be high. Sabah should manage few attempts of their own.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.5 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Rotation and Yamal's knee injury could take some sharpness out of the attack, and a comfortable lead often slows the second half. I expect a total closer to ten or eleven.

401915293.overall: Early view: two struggling sides. Slavia Prague are 34th with 1 point but pushed Arsenal late before losing 2-1, while Villarreal (28th, 3 points) were beaten 6-0 at home by PSG on matchday 4. The brief lists Santiago Mourino as banned after three yellow cards; he was booked against PSG but I could not confirm his earlier cautions. I found little fresh team news for either club, so this view rests on recent results and the table.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals and I lean lower. Slavia scored only once against Arsenal, late, and Villarreal's 6-0 defeat came against the best team in the competition. Both sides need to avoid losing ground, which may make this a more cautious game than the estimate suggests.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Slavia push hard at home, as they did late against Arsenal, while Villarreal should see more of the ball, which balances out. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and I lean slightly higher. Villarreal picked up three yellow cards even while losing 6-0 (Santi Comesana, Santiago Mourino, Sergi Cardona), and Slavia had David Moses booked against Arsenal. This is a must-win game for both, which tends to bring more fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.8 shots and I lean lower. Slavia's attack is limited (one goal against Arsenal), and Villarreal's confidence has taken a hit after the PSG defeat. I expect a total in the high twenties.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Neither side has looked sharp in front of goal recently in this competition, and I expect a tighter game than the numbers suggest.

401915291.overall: Early view: Atletico Madrid are only 23rd with 4 points after a 2-0 home defeat by Bayern, and they then lost 2-1 to Barcelona in LaLiga, with Diego Simeone saying Julian Alvarez must get back to his best. Viking (22nd, 4 points) beat Sabah 4-1 on matchday 4 and held Bayern earlier, so they arrive with confidence. Atletico need this win badly to climb back towards the play-off places.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals and I lean lower. Atletico failed to score at home to Bayern and managed one goal against Barcelona, with Alvarez missing chances. Simeone's sides rarely let games get very open, and Viking have shown they can frustrate a top side.

corners.text: The numbers say 12 corners, which already reflects Atletico pressing a deep Viking side. When Atletico struggle to break teams down they do win many corners, so I see no reason to move the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Atletico had only one player booked against Bayern (Giuliano Simeone), and Viking had two booked against Sabah. I found nothing that moves the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 31 shots. Atletico will have long spells on the ball and take many shots, but some will come from long range against a packed defence. I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Simeone has said Alvarez is not at his best yet, and Atletico's finishing against Bayern and Barcelona was poor. Viking's Erik Botheim scored twice against Sabah, so the visitors should get a few efforts on target too.

401915292.overall: Early view: a game between two teams level on 9 points around the top-eight line. Club Brugge (9th) won 2-1 at PSV on matchday 4, while Liverpool (8th) lost 3-2 at Fenerbahce after poor set-piece defending, then lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal before winning 3-1 at Crystal Palace. Andoni Iraola's side are still finding their feet; Ryan Gravenberch missed the Fenerbahce game with a heel injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Liverpool's games are rarely tight, with five goals in Istanbul and four at Palace, and their attack (Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz) has started to click. Brugge score at home and Liverpool's set-piece defending has been described as cheap and messy, so I stay with a lively game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I stay with it. Liverpool should have more of the ball, but Brugge are dangerous on the counter through Carlos Forbs and in the air through Nicolo Tresoldi. Nothing I found moves the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards and I lean slightly higher. Brugge had three players booked at PSV, and Liverpool's recent games have been heated, with Alexis Mac Allister booked in Istanbul and accused of trying to provoke Noni Madueke at Anfield. A game with top-eight places at stake should be more tense than the estimate suggests.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots, which looks high. Liverpool's expensive forward line has scored fewer league goals than Ipswich this season, and Brugge were compact enough to win at PSV. I expect a total around 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Liverpool's attack is improving, but it has not been efficient this season, and Brugge allowed PSV only one goal in Eindhoven. I expect a total closer to ten.
