401915376.overall: Early view: Inter (15th, 6 points) have won three of their last four, including 3-0 at Feyenoord and 2-0 against Como on 8 November, with only a 3-1 derby defeat to Milan in between. Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) lost 2-0 at Galatasaray but beat Werder Bremen 1-0 at the weekend. Hakan Calhanoglu is listed as banned after his third yellow card; he was booked at Feyenoord, but I could not confirm the two earlier cautions, so that needs checking nearer the game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and I lean lower. Inter have kept clean sheets in three of their last four games (Venezia, Feyenoord, Como), and Stuttgart failed to score in Istanbul. Without Calhanoglu, Inter's build-up loses some of its quality, which points to a narrower game.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Inter will have more of the ball at San Siro and use their wing-backs, and Stuttgart are capable of pushing forward. I see nothing that moves the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and I lean slightly higher. Stuttgart had five players booked in Istanbul (Atakan Karazor, Deniz Undav, Yanik Spalt, Grischa Promel, Ramon Hendriks), and Inter had two booked at Feyenoord. A side that collected five bookings in its last away game in this competition is a fair pointer.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots and I lean lower. Calhanoglu is one of Inter's main shooters from distance, and his absence takes some volume away. Inter also tend to manage games once they lead.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Lautaro Martinez and Marcus Thuram will still create chances, and Ermedin Demirovic has four goals in four games for Stuttgart in this competition. I stay with the estimate.

401915377.overall: Early view: Lille are 35th with 1 point after a 0-0 at Bodo/Glimt and need a win to keep any hope alive. Bayern (13th, 8 points) won 2-0 at Atletico Madrid and 2-1 at home to Mainz, with Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane setting up both goals, but Manuel Neuer is out with a partial foot ligament tear and Vincent Kompany is still recovering from his collapse, with assistant Aaron Danks in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Bayern's recent scores have been controlled rather than wild (2-0 at Atletico, 2-1 against Mainz, 2-2 against Dortmund), and Lille could not score at Bodo. Neuer's absence could give Lille a better chance than usual of scoring, so the factors cancel and I stay with the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I lean slightly higher. Bayern should dominate the ball even away from home, and Lille have struggled to create, so most corners should go to Bayern. Lille may also push forward late if they need goals.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Bayern picked up two yellow cards in Madrid, and Lille had one player booked at Bodo. I found nothing to move the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and I lean slightly higher. Bayern create a lot through Kane, teenager Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer's runs, and Lille's need for a win should make the game more open than their 0-0 at Bodo.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Bayern will create good chances, but Lille's own attack has been poor. I see no reason to move the figure.

401915374.overall: Early view: PSG lead the table with 12 points from 12 and won 6-0 at Villarreal on matchday 4, with Fabian Ruiz scoring twice. Roma (20th, 4 points) led 2-0 at Manchester United before losing 3-2, and drew 3-3 with Napoli before that, so they score but concede a lot. PSG have no reason to ease off given the chase for a top-eight finish.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I lean higher. PSG scored six at Villarreal with six different scorers, and Roma have conceded six in their last two big games (Napoli and Man United). Roma's attack, with Matias Soule and Donyell Malen, can also score, which supports a high total.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. PSG move the ball quickly and score from open play more than from set pieces, which keeps their corner count down. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. Roma had three players booked at Old Trafford (Soule, Emanuele Lulli, Malen), but PSG's win at Villarreal had only one PSG booking. I see nothing that moves the figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots. PSG's attack is the best in the competition, and Roma's defence has been open, so a high total is likely. The estimate already reflects that.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.9 shots on target. PSG's finishing was very sharp at Villarreal, and Roma's attack should get a few efforts on target too. I stay with the estimate.

401915375.overall: Early view: Shakhtar (21st, 4 points) lost 1-0 at home to Sporting on matchday 4, while Fenerbahce (19th, 5 points) beat Liverpool 3-2 under interim coach Dirk Kuyt, coming from behind twice. The brief lists the venue as Stamford Bridge, so Shakhtar will again play away from Ukraine without a true home crowd. I found little fresh team news for Shakhtar, so this view leans on the matchday 4 results.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean slightly higher. Fenerbahce scored three against Liverpool through Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi, and they look confident under Kuyt. Shakhtar failed to score against Sporting, but a neutral venue removes much of their home advantage.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Fenerbahce are dangerous from set pieces, with Muriqi's header and Greenwood's free kick against Liverpool, but Shakhtar should have plenty of the ball. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5 cards, which looks high. Shakhtar's home game against Sporting had only two bookings, and Fenerbahce had two players booked against Liverpool. Without a hostile Istanbul crowd, I expect fewer cards than the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. Both teams like to attack, but Shakhtar's attack was blunt against Sporting. I see nothing to move the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Fenerbahce were efficient against Liverpool, and Shakhtar's attack has struggled. I stay with the estimate.

401915373.overall: Early view: Sporting (10th, 9 points) won 1-0 at Shakhtar on matchday 4, while Manchester United (17th, 6 points) beat Roma 3-2 after being 2-0 down, then drew 4-4 with Aston Villa. United are in the Premier League relegation zone and ESPN sources say the club is weighing Michael Carrick's future, so the manager could change before this game. Matheus Cunha, who scored twice against Roma, is banned after his second yellow card in that game (ban not yet served).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean higher. United's last two games produced 13 goals (3-2 against Roma, 4-4 against Villa), and their defence is very open. Sporting kept a clean sheet in Ukraine, but United without Cunha still have Bruno Fernandes, who scored against Roma.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Sporting should have more of the ball at home, but United create most of their chances in transition rather than from sustained pressure. I stay with the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and I lean slightly higher. United picked up five yellow cards and a red against Roma, and a team under heavy pressure tends to concede fouls. Sporting had only one player booked at Shakhtar, so most of the cards may go to United.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. United's recent games have been very open, but some of that was due to their own comebacks, which may not be repeated in Lisbon. I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Sporting will create good chances against an open United defence, but Cunha's absence reduces United's threat. I see no reason to move the figure.

401915290.overall: Early view: Viking won their first ever Champions League game 4-1 against Sabah on matchday 4 and have scored in 12 European games in a row, while Feyenoord were beaten 3-0 at home by Inter and have one win from four. Both are around the play-off line (Viking 22nd, Feyenoord 32nd), so with two rounds left after this a defeat would hurt Feyenoord far more. Matchday 5 comes first, so team news is refreshed nearer the game.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, 2.4 of them Viking's. I stay close to that: Viking's last seven home games before Sabah each had three or more goals and the 4-1 made it eight, while Feyenoord have conceded 11 in four league-phase games. The doubt is Feyenoord's end of it, with four goals all campaign and none against Inter.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners and give Feyenoord the bigger share (6.3). I lean lower: Feyenoord have been second-best away from De Kuip (5-1 at Barcelona, 1-0 at Betis), and Viking, with Christiansen and Tripic driving their attack, should have more of the ball at home than this split suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean a little higher because of the stakes: Feyenoord sit 32nd on three points, so a loss in Stavanger would leave them needing a lot from their last two games, and that kind of pressure usually brings late, desperate fouls. The referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 15.6. I lean lower on Feyenoord's side: Giovanni van Bronckhorst's team managed four goals in four games and were shut out at home by Inter, and Viking at home have dictated games rather than sat back.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target. I lean a little lower, mainly because Feyenoord's attack (Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente) has rarely tested goalkeepers in this competition. Viking's own share of around six looks fair given how they finished against Sabah.

401915372.overall: Early view: Villarreal were thrashed 6-0 at home by PSG on matchday 4 and sit 28th on three points, so a home win over Sabah is close to essential, though they did steady themselves with a 2-0 league win over Getafe on Sunday. Sabah lost 4-1 at Viking, their second four-goal away defeat after 4-0 at Manchester United. The two suspensions in the brief (Santiago Mouriño's three-yellow ban, Aden McCarthy's red card at Viking) should both be served on matchday 5, so both players should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.4 goals, 3.5 of them Villarreal's. I lean a touch higher: Villarreal have now conceded in 16 Champions League games in a row, so Sabah, who scored at Viking and in the 2-1 home loss to Dortmund, can get one, and Sabah have let in four in both away games so far. Iñigo Pérez's side also need a big goal difference swing after the PSG result.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.0 corners, eight of them Villarreal's. I lean higher: Sabah spent long spells defending in both away games (4-0 at United, 4-1 at Viking), and a Villarreal side that must win will keep the ball in the final third for long spells, with wide players like Buchanan and Moleiro pushing for crosses.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, 2.7 on Sabah. I lean slightly lower: if Villarreal go ahead early, as the numbers expect, games this one-sided tend to calm down in the second half. McCarthy's red card at Viking is the warning sign on Sabah's side, and the referee is still to be named.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.6 shots, 25.3 of them Villarreal's. I see nothing to move it further: Sabah conceded heavily on shots in both away games and Villarreal must attack, but 34-35 is already a very high total for any match.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target. I stay with that: Villarreal's forwards (Mikautadze, Oluwaseyi) should get plenty of clear looks against a side that has conceded ten in four games, and Sabah should manage two or three of their own.

401915289.overall: Early view: AEK pushed Real Madrid hard before losing 3-2 to a 93rd-minute Valverde goal, but they are 29th on three points and need wins. Galatasaray are 18th on six points after beating Stuttgart 2-0 with two early Batrakov goals, and they were top of the Super Lig at the last check. Aboubakary Koita's red card (shown after full time for protesting) means at least a ban for matchday 5; whether UEFA adds more games should be checked before this one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Galatasaray conceded nine in their first three league-phase games before the clean sheet against Stuttgart, and AEK have let in 11 in four, while both sides scored freely in their last outings (AEK twice against Real Madrid, Galatasaray 4-0 at Konyaspor in the league).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, AEK slightly ahead. I see nothing that moves it: both teams attack through the middle as much as the flanks, and with the win probabilities nearly level, neither should spend the game camped in its own box.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: a Greek-Turkish game in Athens comes with an edge, AEK need points badly, and Koita's dismissal for protesting at Real Madrid shows how heated their nights can get.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean slightly higher: both defences have been open in this competition and both teams have forwards who shoot early (Osimhen and Leão for Galatasaray, Jović and Varga for AEK in their last predicted line-up).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean higher, in line with the goals: Galatasaray put two on target and in within 15 minutes against Stuttgart, and AEK got enough efforts on goal to score twice against Real Madrid.

401915288.overall: Early view: Roma are 20th on four points after losing 3-2 at Manchester United to two late Cunha goals, and they go to PSG on matchday 5, so this home game may decide whether they reach the play-offs. Sporting are 10th on nine points and won 1-0 at Shakhtar a day after sacking coach Rui Borges; who leads them in December is the main thing to check. Roma were missing Dybala, Pellegrini, Koné and goalkeeper Svilar at Old Trafford.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean a little lower: Sporting have conceded only four goals in four league-phase games and won at Shakhtar with one goal, and Gasperini's Roma are third in Serie A, so neither side is used to shipping goals. Roma's late collapses (at Real Madrid and United) are the risk.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, 5.8 of them Roma's. I lean higher: Roma's wing-backs push right up, and a team that probably needs the win after visiting PSG will pin Sporting back for long spells, which tends to produce corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean a touch higher because of what is at stake: Roma were given a target of five more points from four games, and with PSG away just before this one, a tight game at the Olimpico could get ragged. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.6 shots, 18.2 of them Roma's. That fits what I read: Roma create plenty at home, and Sporting are compact enough to keep many efforts from distance, so I would not move it either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Sporting have kept opponents to few clear chances (four goals against in four games), and Roma had Dybala and Pellegrini, two of their most creative players, injured at the last check.

401915286.overall: Early view: PSG top the table with four wins from four and 20 goals, including 6-0 at Villarreal on matchday 4. Aston Villa are sixth on nine points but were beaten 3-0 at Barcelona and then drew 4-4 at Manchester United on Sunday, conceding twice inside the first four minutes. Villa were without Onana, Ruggeri and Wan-Bissaka at Barcelona; PSG had Kvaratskhelia (cruciate ligament), Dembélé and Marquinhos (hamstrings) out earlier in the phase.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 1.8 of them Villa's. I lean higher, mainly on PSG's side: they have scored 20 in four league-phase games and broke a scoring record, while Villa conceded three at Barcelona and four at Old Trafford in their last two games. Villa have scored 12 in Europe, so they should still get chances at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, split almost evenly. I would leave it: PSG should have more of the ball, but Villa will still attack at home, as they showed by scoring four at Old Trafford through Alysson, Jackson, McGinn and Goretzka.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. I see no reason to move it: Villa had only two bookings in the chaotic 4-4 at Old Trafford, and PSG's possession game rarely forces opponents into lots of fouls. A Villa side fighting to stay in the top eight could get a little edgier late on.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.3 shots, with PSG on 16. I lean slightly higher: PSG average well over four goals a game in this phase, which only comes with heavy shot volume, and Villa at Villa Park will take their chances rather than sit in a low block.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 shots on target. That fits a game with two attacking sides and two shaky defences, so I keep it. Fabián Ruiz, João Neves and Doué all scored at Villarreal, so the threat is spread across PSG's side.

401915285.overall: Early view: two teams on nine points chasing a top-eight place. Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0 and then won 2-1 at Atlético on Sunday to stay top in La Liga, while Manchester City won 3-2 at Leipzig but lost at Nottingham Forest at the weekend and Marc Guéhi has since withdrawn from the England squad. Rodri's hamstring injury was expected to keep him out for about a month from 3 November, so he may just be back.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals. I lean a little lower: Barcelona kept a clean sheet against Villa, and a meeting of two top-eight contenders in December is often tighter than either side's results against weaker teams. Barcelona's 14 goals and Haaland's form still make three or more likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, almost evenly split. I see no reason to move it: both teams attack through wingers (Yamal and Raphinha, Doku and Foden) but prefer to work the ball into the box rather than win corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean a little higher: the top-eight places are on the line for both, and fast wide players on each side (Yamal, Raphinha, Doku) tend to draw tactical fouls when the game opens up.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, which looks low next to their 4.3 goals. I lean higher: Barcelona have scored 14 in four games and City 12, and with neither side likely to defend deep, both should get well over ten attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. That matches two very good attacks, so I keep it. If Guéhi's injury keeps him out, City's defence could give up more clear chances than expected.

401915284.overall: Early view: Bayern are unbeaten (two wins, two draws) and won 2-0 at Atlético on matchday 4, but they are only 13th, so they need wins like this to climb into the top eight. Slavia are 34th with one point after losing 2-1 to Arsenal, though they pushed them to the end. Slavia were without the suspended Tomas Chory and the injured Igoh Ogbu for that game; Chory's ban has been served. I found no recent Bayern injury news, so their team news is a gap to fill later.

goals.text: The numbers say 5.1 goals, 4.5 of them Bayern's. I lean lower: Slavia have not been thrashed this season (2-1 against Arsenal, 3-2 against Lens), and their predicted line-up has three centre-backs and wing-backs, which makes it harder to run up big scores. Bayern's 3-3 with Viking shows they will concede chances too.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.0 corners, 8.2 of them Bayern's. I lean higher: Slavia's back five will sit deep and block crosses, which turns into corners, and Bayern will need goals for goal difference in a tight race for the top eight.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean slightly lower: one-sided games like this rarely get heated, and Bayern's possession means Slavia spend more time defending in shape than chasing. Slavia's own record (Chory suspended earlier) is the one thing pushing the other way.

shots.text: The numbers say 37 shots, 28 of them Bayern's. I would leave it: Bayern will dominate, but Slavia's deep block will block many efforts. Both effects are already priced in.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 14 shots on target. I lean lower: a crowded penalty area means more blocked and off-target attempts, and Slavia showed against Arsenal that they can keep a game close. Bayern should still have nine or ten on target.

401915371.overall: Early view: Manchester United are 18th in the Premier League after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, and director of football Jason Wilcox is due to decide on Michael Carrick's future during the break, so United could have a different manager by December. Leipzig are 30th on three points after a 3-2 home defeat by Manchester City. Matheus Cunha's red card against Roma (second yellow) should be served at Sporting on matchday 5, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: United's last two games finished 3-2 and 4-4, and Leipzig have conceded 11 in four league-phase games. Both defences are leaky, and both teams need the points.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 6.2 of them United's. I see nothing to change that: United will push forward at home, but Leipzig's quick wide players (Nusa, Gruda) mean this will not be one-way traffic.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. I lean higher: both teams are under pressure (United near the relegation zone at home, Leipzig needing points to stay in the race), and Cunha's dismissal against Roma showed how tense United's European nights have become. The 4-4 with Villa had only two bookings, so this rests on the stakes rather than recent card counts.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. I lean slightly higher, given that United and Leipzig have both been open, chaotic sides in Europe this season. A change of manager at United would make this harder to read.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.4 shots on target. I keep it: both teams have enough attackers (Fernandes, Cunha, Mbeumo, and Leipzig's front three) to test the keepers, and neither defence has held firm lately.

401915287.overall: Early view: Napoli are 27th on three points after a 4-1 defeat in Porto, eighth in Serie A, and Massimiliano Allegri was already under pressure before that game. Club Brugge are ninth on nine points after winning 2-1 at PSV, where Yann Sommer made seven saves. Rafa Marín's red card in Porto should be served at Manchester City on matchday 5, but Napoli had a long injury list (Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Buongiorno, Neres, De Bruyne with an ankle sprain).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean a little higher: Brugge's games have been open (4-3 at Inter, 2-3 against Villa), and Napoli conceded three in the last 20 minutes in Porto, which suggests a team that collapses when chasing.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. I lean higher: Napoli will probably have to win this home game, and with Politano and Olivera as wing-backs in their predicted line-up they should force corners from a Brugge side that won at PSV with Sommer making seven saves.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean higher: a Napoli side under pressure, at home and near the elimination places, plus Marín's red in Porto, point to a tense game. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.2 shots. I lean lower: Napoli's injuries in midfield (Lobotka, possibly De Bruyne) take away a lot of their creativity, and Brugge are comfortable defending in a block and breaking.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: Napoli's attack has been blunt beyond McTominay, and Brugge's shooting is concentrated in Tresoldi and Forbs.

401915283.overall: Early view: two sides on nine points. Como made history with a 9-1 win at Lens (Douvikas hat-trick) and are fourth, while Real Betis lost 2-1 at Dortmund, where they were outplayed on expected goals (2.58 to 0.82), before winning 2-0 at Elche on Sunday. Betis were without Cucho Hernández and Junior Firpo; Como without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesús Rodríguez and Assane Diao.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean higher: Como have scored 19 in four league-phase games and scored first in each of their first three, and Douvikas has scored in every league-phase game. Betis conceded twice in Dortmund and should have more to do here.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners. I see no reason to change that: Como score mostly from open play rather than set pieces, and nothing I read suggests Betis will change their approach under Pellegrini.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, 2.7 of them Como's. I lean lower: 4.9 is high for two possession-minded sides, and nothing I read points to a disciplinary problem for either team. The referee is still unknown.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots. I lean slightly higher: Como's attack (Paz, Baturina, Douvikas) has been the most productive in the competition after PSG's, and Betis at home will try to match them rather than sit back.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. I lean higher, in line with the goals: Como's finishing has been clinical, and Betis's attack (Antony, Ezzalzouli, Isco) should test Butez too.

401915282.overall: Early view: Slovan Bratislava are bottom with no points and a goal difference of -16 after losing 4-0 at LASK, so this is about pride. Shakhtar are 21st on four points after a 1-0 home defeat to Sporting and need wins to stay in the play-off places. I found little recent team news for either club, so this view rests mainly on form; Marlon Gomes was one booking away from a ban before matchday 4.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, Shakhtar with 1.4. I lean slightly higher: Slovan have conceded 17 in four games, including 4-0 at LASK, and that is hard to ignore even though Shakhtar have scored only four times in four games.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. I lean higher on Shakhtar's side: they should have most of the ball against a side that has conceded 17 goals in four games and spent long spells defending.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. With no referee named and no recent disciplinary news, I leave it. Gomes's yellow-card count could matter by then.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, 16.1 of them Shakhtar's. That fits a game where Shakhtar push and Slovan look to break, so I do not move it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, because Slovan's defence has given up so many clear chances (17 goals against in four games) that Shakhtar should test the goalkeeper often.

401915367.overall: Early view: second against third, both on course for the top eight: Real Madrid have won all four league-phase games (2-3 at AEK with a 93rd-minute Valverde winner) and beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, while Arsenal won 2-1 in Prague and have the competition's meanest defence. Arsenal had Saka (quad) out and Konsa came off with a knee problem in Prague, with Saliba back from his back injury. Real were missing Rodrygo and Raúl Asencio.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: Arsenal have conceded three in four league-phase games and set a defensive record at Anfield, and both teams already have a top-eight place within reach, so neither needs to take big risks. Mbappé and Bellingham can still punish any lapse.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 5.3 of them Arsenal's. I see no reason to change that: Arsenal should have more of the ball at home, and nothing I read points either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I lean higher: both sides want a top-two finish, and Real under Mourinho came from behind twice in a fierce game in Athens on matchday 4. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. I keep it: Arsenal will create more, but Real's counter-attacks with Vinícius and Mbappé are dangerous, and the two cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because both defences are good and Arsenal in particular limit clear chances. If Saka is back, Arsenal's share could rise.

401915368.overall: Early view: Dortmund are 12th on nine points after a 2-1 win over Betis in which they were much the better side (2.58 expected goals to 0.82). Inter are 15th on six points after a 3-0 win at Feyenoord, but they lost the Milan derby 3-1 and were missing Lautaro Martínez, Pavard and others. Hakan Çalhanoglu's three-yellow ban from the brief should be served at home to Stuttgart on matchday 5, so he should be available in Dortmund.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean slightly higher: Dortmund create a lot at home under Niko Kovač, with Guirassy and Fabio Silva in form, and Inter's defence conceded four at home to Brugge and three in the derby.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I keep it: both teams use wing-backs, so corners should come at both ends, with nothing pushing the number either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I leave it: Inter's red cards earlier in the phase (Bastoni against Shakhtar) were one-offs, and Çalhanoglu is the main card-collector. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. I lean slightly higher: Dortmund's xG against Betis shows how much they can create at home, and Inter, 15th, still need points to make their play-off place safe, so they should open up too.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, in line with the shots: Guirassy shoots a lot, and Inter's front two, Thuram and Esposito, are dangerous as well.

401915281.overall: Early view: LASK are 16th on six points after back-to-back wins, the latest 4-0 over Slovan Bratislava, and Fenerbahçe are 19th on five after beating Liverpool 3-2 under interim manager Dirk Kuyt. Fenerbahçe were without Marco Asensio (knee) and Jayden Oosterwolde (hamstring); whether Kuyt is still in charge by December is worth checking. I found little recent LASK team news.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean slightly higher: Fenerbahçe have conceded 11 in four league-phase games and LASK 9, and both attacks scored three or more in their last European games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I see no reason to move it: the teams are close in quality, and neither has a clear plan of camping in the other's half.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I leave it: with the play-off places at stake for both, the game should be competitive, but I have nothing on the referee or recent bookings to move it.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots. I lean slightly lower: 30 is a lot for two mid-table sides, and Fenerbahçe, with Kanté and Guendouzi in midfield, may be happy to slow the game down away from home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. I keep it: both teams finish well, and both defences are porous.

401915370.overall: Early view: Lens are 33rd on three points after a 9-1 home defeat by Como, the worst result of the phase, and new coach Yannick Cahuzac (who replaced Dino Toppmöller) has a defence with no clean sheet in 17 Champions League games. Bodø/Glimt are 25th on four points after a 0-0 at home to Lille. Both sides probably need to win to stay in contention for the play-offs. Lens are without Odsonne Edouard, possibly until 2027.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Lens have conceded 16 in four games and Bodø scored three in their 4-3 loss to Napoli. The 0-0 with Lille is the warning that Bodø can go quiet.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.2 corners, 8.6 of them for Lens. I lean lower: Lens have been the weaker side in three of their four games, and after a 9-1 defeat their coach may be more careful than the numbers expect. Thauvin, who created the most chances in the first three matchdays, is their main source of them.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. I lean higher: with both teams fighting to stay above 25th, the game should be tense, and a home side trying to restore pride after a 9-1 defeat may play with an edge.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots, 21.2 of them for Lens. I lean lower: 21 is a lot for a Lens side that has been second-best in three of four European games and has just lost 9-1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.4 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with the shots, mainly on Lens's side, as their main striker Edouard is out.

401915369.overall: Early view: Liverpool are eighth on nine points after a 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahçe, their first in the league phase, and Andoni Iraola has a long injury list (Ekitike, Frimpong, Bradley, Leoni and Gravenberch with a heel fracture). Porto are 26th on three points but beat Napoli 4-1 on matchday 4 and had won 10 league games in a row at the last check. Both need the points: Liverpool to stay in the top eight, Porto to reach the play-offs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Liverpool's four league-phase games have produced 24 goals, and Porto have just scored four against Napoli. Porto's league defence has been tight (four goals against in ten games at the last check), which is the case for fewer goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.7 of them Liverpool's. I keep that: Liverpool will have more of the ball at Anfield, and Porto will defend and counter as they did against Napoli.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I see nothing to move it: neither team has a disciplinary problem in what I read, and the referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots. I lean lower: Liverpool are without several regulars (Ekitike up front, Gravenberch in midfield) and lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal in a frustrating game, while Porto under Farioli are hard to break down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I keep it: the lower shot count I expect is offset by two attacks that finish well (Isak and Wirtz for Liverpool, Samu Aghehowa and Veiga for Porto).

401915366.overall: Early view: PSV and Atlético are level on four points (24th and 23rd), on the edge of the play-off places. PSV lost 2-1 at home to Brugge, and Atlético managed one shot on target in a 2-0 home defeat by Bayern and then lost 2-1 to Barcelona on Sunday. Morten Hjulmand's red card against Stuttgart has been served. PSV were missing Jerdy Schouten, Alassane Pléa and Sami Ouaissa; Atlético were without Cristian Romero and Johnny Cardoso.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, which looks far too high. PSV have scored three in four league-phase games and Atlético four, and Simeone's team will not risk much with their place in the play-offs on the line.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. I keep it: PSV will have more of the ball at home, and Atlético's habit of defending deep tends to produce corners, so the figure is about right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean higher: Atlético have had red cards against Manchester United and Stuttgart in this phase, and with both sides needing a result, there should be plenty of fouls in midfield.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots. I lean lower: Atlético had only one shot on target against Bayern, and PSV have scored three goals in four league-phase games, never more than one in a game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. I lean lower, in line with the goals and shots: neither side has created much in this competition.

401915365.overall: Early view: Stuttgart are 14th on seven points after losing 2-0 at Galatasaray, their first defeat of the phase, and they were without midfielder Angelo Stiller (adductor). Lille are 35th with one point after a 0-0 at Bodø/Glimt and need a win to keep any hope; Ethan Mbappé's three-match ban is now served. Stuttgart play at Inter on matchday 5, so this home game is their best chance of points.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I keep that: Stuttgart conceded only two in their first three league-phase games and Lille have scored just four in four. Lille's need to win could open the game late on.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. I lean slightly higher on Stuttgart's side: they should dominate the ball at home against a bottom-two team, with Leweling and Führich as wing-backs in their predicted line-up.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I leave it: Lille's discipline has been an issue (Mbappé's long ban), but that was one incident, and the referee has not been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots. I lean slightly higher: Stuttgart at home against a side with one point should have long spells of pressure, and Lille will have to push forward later.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I keep it: Stuttgart should create plenty, but Stiller, who usually controls their possession, was out with an adductor injury and his return date is unknown.

401915816.overall: Early view: Kairat (27th, two points) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty, a trip of several thousand kilometres east for the Swedes. Mjällby have been tight in Europe, beating Inter Escaldes and Borac 2-0 and drawing at Iberia, while Kairat were thrashed 5-1 at home by Panathinaikos before a creditable 1-1 at Atalanta. I found no recent team news for either side, so this rests on European form and is refreshed with team news before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. I lean a little lower: all three of Mjällby's European games finished with exactly two goals and they have conceded once in three, while Kairat's draws with Riga and at Atalanta were both 1-1. Mjällby's domestic season has also been low-scoring (30 for, 43 against in 27 Allsvenskan games on the ESPN table), which does not point to an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, split almost evenly. I read nothing on either side's wide play or set-piece habits, and neither team's European results suggest one will pin the other back for long, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Both sides need points around the 24th-place cut-off for the knockout play-offs, which can add edge, but there is no referee yet and no sign of a disciplinary pattern in either side's three games, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Mjällby slightly ahead. Kairat at home should push more than they did in Bergamo, but they were picked apart by Panathinaikos at home and Mjällby have controlled their European games without dominating, so nothing points clearly away from the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Mjällby have scored five and conceded one in Europe, a sign of reasonably clean finishing and defending, and Kairat had to make the most of few chances at Atalanta; with no team news I stay close to the number.

401915815.overall: Early view: Ajax (11th, six points) are in good shape after a 6-1 win at Midtjylland, where the home side played the second half with ten men, and they sit third in the Eredivisie with 32 goals in 12 games. Thun, the Swiss champions, are 20th with three points but have been hard to break down, losing 1-0 at Twente and 1-0 at home to Hajduk before beating Hearts 3-1. Ajax are clear favourites; the question is how deep Thun sit.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, 3.3 of them for Ajax. I lean lower: Thun have conceded only three goals in three league-phase games, including a 1-0 defeat at Twente. Ajax's six at Midtjylland came largely against ten men after Kjell-Arik Wätjen's 43rd-minute dismissal, so I would not read it as their normal rate.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, 6.4 for Ajax. I lean higher: Thun's 1-0 defeats at Twente and against Hajduk point to a side that defends deep and in numbers, and that pushes the attacking team wide and into blocked crosses, which is where corners come from. Ajax have averaged 59% possession this season according to ESPN.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with more expected for Thun. That fits a deep-defending away side chasing the ball for long spells; Furkan Dursun was booked for a forearm in the Hearts game. No referee yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.1 shots, 20.3 of them for Ajax. A deep Thun block should give Ajax plenty of attempts, many from outside the box or blocked, but Thun also showed against Hearts that they can hurt teams on the break. I see no reason to move far from the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Ajax's forwards are in form (Tolu Arokodare scored twice at Midtjylland), but against a packed defence a good share of their shots will be blocked rather than on target. That roughly balances out, so I stay with the number.

401915814.overall: Early view: Brighton (5th, seven points) are the only side in the league phase yet to concede and are second in the Premier League after wins at Manchester City and against Brentford. But Fabian Hurzeler has rotated heavily in Europe (eight changes at Jablonec, five at Getafe) and those sides have scored once in two games. Craiova (8th, seven points) have been solid too, drawing with Getafe and beating Inter Escaldes 3-1 and Egnatia 2-0.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, 2.9 of them for Brighton. I lean lower: Brighton's rotated European sides drew 0-0 at Jablonec and won 1-0 at Getafe, and Hurzeler himself said the competition needs patience against a low block. Craiova have conceded only twice in three games, so a two- or three-goal Brighton win looks more likely than a rout.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, 8.3 for Brighton. Brighton keep the ball for long spells (almost 80% after the break against Brentford, per Sky Sports) and Craiova should sit deep, which supports a high home count. That is already in the number, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, more of them for Craiova. A visiting side defending for long spells tends to pick up tactical fouls on the break, but Brighton's European games have not been feisty and there is no referee yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, 22.1 for Brighton. Brighton will have the ball, but at Getafe they were caught on the break: Jaouen Hadjam hit the woodwork twice. That suggests Craiova will get a few chances too, roughly as the number already allows.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, 7.7 for Brighton. I lean lower: at Jablonec Brighton's rotated side kept shooting wide or over, and at Getafe Ibrahim Osman skewed a close-range chance wide, so their European shooting has been loose. Against a Craiova side that has conceded twice in three games, I expect fewer efforts on target than the number.

401915810.overall: Early view: two sides near the 24th-place line for the knockout play-offs: Egnatia (26th, two points) and Lincoln Red Imps (22nd, three points). Egnatia drew with Midtjylland and at AGF before losing 2-0 at Craiova, and Lincoln beat Hajduk Split 1-0 in Gibraltar after defeats by Brann and Twente. Enea Bitri's sending-off came in that Craiova game, a UEFA match, so the ban should apply here. I found no domestic news for either side, so this rests on European form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: each of Egnatia's three European games ended with two goals, and Lincoln's win over Hajduk was 1-0. With both sides close to the cut-off line and a point not useless to either, I expect a cautious game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.9 for Egnatia. Egnatia at home should have more of the ball against a Lincoln side that sat deep against Hajduk, which the split already reflects; I read nothing to move the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean a little higher: this is a direct fight for a play-off place between two sides on two and three points, and Egnatia finished their last European game with a man sent off (Enea Bitri, per the brief and ESPN's event list). Tight, high-stakes games of this kind usually draw more fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots, 18.2 of them for Egnatia. I lean lower: Egnatia have scored two goals in three European games and do not look like a side that piles up attempts, and Lincoln defended deep and well against Hajduk. A cagey game should mean fewer shots than the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. For the same reasons as the goals and shots, with two modest attacks and a lot at stake, I lean slightly lower.

401915811.overall: Early view: Hearts (32nd, one point) are in a bad patch: a 7-1 defeat at Celtic, a League Cup semi-final loss to Hibernian and a 3-1 defeat at Thun, where Wouter Vrancken was without ten players and Stephen Kingsley went off injured. Monaco (4th, nine points, one goal conceded) have won all three league-phase games but are only seventh in Ligue 1 and lost 3-1 at Paris FC on 1 November; Ansu Fati is out for about two months, while Folarin Balogun was added to their European squad. Hearts need a result at Tynecastle to stay in the race.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, 2.5 for Monaco. I lean lower: Monaco have conceded once in three European games and won 2-1, 3-0 and 2-0, so their matches have averaged under three goals. Hearts were described by Sky Sports as only sporadically threatening at Thun, so most of the scoring should come from one side.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Hearts leaned heavily on set pieces at Thun (their goal came from a Jordi Altena free-kick headed in by Stuart Findlay), and the home crowd will push them to win corners, but Monaco should have more of the ball. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean a little higher: Hearts at home, needing points and short of players, are likely to press and chase, which tends to bring fouls against a quicker, technical side. No referee is known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Hearts' home crowd should push them forward more than at Thun, while Monaco control games without huge shot volumes; I see nothing to move the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Hearts struggled to test the keeper at Thun beyond a long-range effort from Josh McPake and their set pieces, and Monaco's wins have been efficient rather than shot-heavy.

401915813.overall: Early view: two sides on one point who need a win to get back towards the play-off places. Iberia 1999 lost 2-0 at Sint-Truiden, drew with Mjällby and lost 2-1 in Copenhagen; Getafe drew at Craiova, were beaten 5-2 at home by Lugano and lost 1-0 to Brighton. Getafe are 15th in La Liga with only eight goals in 12 games, which shapes most of this view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Getafe have scored only eight goals in 12 La Liga games and Iberia have managed two in three European games. The 5-2 home defeat to Lugano was an outlier; Getafe's league games have averaged just over two goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, more for Getafe. Nothing I read changes how either team builds attacks, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already a high figure that reflects Getafe's combative style. Both sides are desperate for points, which supports a high count, but the number already allows for that and there is no referee yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.0 shots, 15.9 for Getafe. I lean lower: Getafe's attack has been among La Liga's weakest, and Iberia have been outshot in their European games. Getafe did create chances against Brighton, with Jaouen Hadjam hitting the woodwork twice, but I expect fewer attempts in total than the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. With two struggling attacks I lean slightly lower; Getafe's eight league goals in 12 games point to poor shot quality, not just bad luck.

401915812.overall: Early view: Lugano top the league phase with nine points and 11 goals, having beaten Red Star 3-2, won 5-2 at Getafe and beaten Kauno Zalgiris 3-0; they also led the Swiss league in the latest table I could read. Jablonec (23rd, two points) under Lubos Kozel are hard to beat at home, holding Brighton to 0-0 in October, and drew 1-1 at Riga last time. The site's numbers rate this as close to even; on form I would favour Lugano.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little higher: Lugano's three games have produced 5, 7 and 3 goals, and Jablonec's earlier trip to Freiburg ended 3-2. Jablonec's 0-0 with a rotated Brighton side is the warning that they can shut games down at home.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec. Jablonec were dangerous from corners against Brighton (Rusek headed one narrowly wide), but Lugano should have plenty of the ball. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. No referee is known yet and neither side has a disciplinary pattern in this competition that I could find, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.7 shots. Lugano attack in numbers, and Jablonec will also go for it at home; the high number already captures that, so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Lugano's 11 goals in three games show sharp finishing, while Jablonec's keeper Jan Hanus kept Brighton out with several saves. I see nothing to move the number.

401915739.overall: Early view: Kauno Zalgiris are bottom with no points and one goal for, 11 against, after defeats by Brighton (4-0), Brann (4-1 at home) and Lugano (3-0). Riga have drawn all three games 1-1, against Kairat, Pafos and Jablonec. I found no domestic news for either club, so this rests on European form.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Kauno Zalgiris concede a lot, but those goals came against much stronger sides, and Riga have scored only once in each of their games. The two pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. I read nothing about either side's style that moves this, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Kauno Zalgiris need a first point and Riga need a first win, but neither side's games so far have produced red cards and no referee is known yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, split fairly evenly. Kauno Zalgiris will want to attack at home after three defeats, which supports their share, but Riga have played compact, low-scoring games. Nothing clear points either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. With little news on either side, I stay close to the number.

401915809.overall: Early view: two sides on one point that need a win. Pafos lost 3-1 at Atalanta and at Twente and drew 1-1 with Riga; Midtjylland lead the Danish Superliga unbeaten but have one point in Europe after a 6-1 home defeat to Ajax. Both lose a player sent off in their last European game: Lelê for Pafos at Twente and Kjell-Arik Wätjen for Midtjylland against Ajax, so these bans apply here.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean higher: both defences have leaked seven goals in three European games, and Midtjylland's Danish league form (27 goals in 13 games) shows they can score. Pafos lose Lelê, who scored at Twente in the game he was sent off, which hurts their attack, but both sides need to win and should open up.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Pafos at home and Midtjylland both like to attack, which the number already reflects; I see nothing to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean higher: both teams had a man sent off last time out in Europe, both are near the bottom of the table and need the win, and that tends to make games more stretched and fractious.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots. Both sides will push for the win, which supports a high count, but that is already in the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Weak defending on both sides supports a decent count, while Lelê's absence takes away one of Pafos's main finishers. I stay with the number.

401915808.overall: Early view: Brann (7th, seven points) are unbeaten in Europe after beating Lincoln and Kauno Zalgiris and drawing 1-1 at Sint-Truiden, though they are only seventh in a very open Eliteserien season (45 goals for, 42 against in 25 games). AGF (24th, two points) are eighth in Denmark with six draws in 13 games and have scored once in three European games. Brann are favourites at home.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean lower: AGF's European games ended 1-0, 1-1 and 0-0, and their Danish league record (17 goals for, 21 against in 13) is low-scoring. Brann's games are much more open, but AGF set the tempo in Europe so far.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.0 corners, 7.6 for Brann. Brann at home should have a lot of the ball against a side that has kept things tight, which fits the high home split; I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Neither side has a disciplinary pattern I could find in this competition and no referee is known yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 18.5 for Brann. Brann's open style supports a high home count, while AGF's caution keeps theirs down. That matches the split, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: AGF have scored one goal in three European games, so their 3.7 looks generous, and a deep AGF block should cut down Brann's clean shooting chances.

401915806.overall: Early view: Atalanta (16th, four points) under Maurizio Sarri are short of players: Gianluca Gaetano, Raoul Bellanova, Thomas Kristensen, Isak Hien, Giacomo Raspadori and Odilon Kossounou were all missing at Monza on 8 November. The 1-0 win there, through Nikola Krstovic, ended a run of six games without a win since 15 October, including a 3-0 home defeat by Parma and a 1-1 draw with Kairat. Borac (21st, three points) beat KuPS 2-0 at home and lost narrowly at Panathinaikos.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.0 for Atalanta. Atalanta's recent games swing widely (a 4-4 with Frosinone and a 2-2 at Fiorentina, then 1-1 and 1-0), so their defence is not reliable, but their injury-hit attack has also scored only twice in the last two games. Those cancel out, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 6.0 for Atalanta. Sarri's teams keep the ball and Borac should defend deep at home for long spells, which the split already reflects.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. Atalanta picked up two bookings at Monza (Éderson and Charles De Ketelaere) in a scrappy game; there is no referee yet and nothing in Borac's games points away from the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, 18.9 for Atalanta. I lean lower: with Raspadori, Gaetano and several defenders out, Atalanta's attack has been blunt lately, and Monza had the better of the first half against them. I expect a high count, but below the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. For the same reasons as the shots, a thin, out-of-form Atalanta side, I lean slightly lower.

401915802.overall: Early view: Braga (17th, four points) are eighth in Portugal with only 13 goals in 11 league games, and their European games have been tight: a 3-0 defeat in Copenhagen, a 2-0 win over Gent and a 0-0 at AGF. KuPS (33rd, one point) lost 4-2 to Trabzonspor and 2-0 at Borac before a 0-0 with Gent. Braga are clear favourites; how much they score is the question.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 2.1 for Braga. I lean a little lower: Braga's league games have averaged just over two goals in total, they drew 0-0 at AGF last time out, and KuPS have scored once in their last two European games. A 1-0 or 2-0 home win fits this better than an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 7.1 for Braga. Braga at home should dominate the ball against a KuPS side that kept Gent out last time, which the split already reflects.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Nothing in either side's European games points to a disciplinary trend, and no referee is known, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.8 shots, 23.3 for Braga. I lean lower: Braga's low scoring at home and in the league suggests they do not produce shots in bulk, and a deep KuPS block should limit good chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. I lean slightly lower for the same reasons: Braga have scored two goals in their last two European games and KuPS rarely test keepers.

401915803.overall: Early view: CSKA Sofia (28th, one point) have lost narrowly to Monaco (2-1) and at Panathinaikos (2-1) and drew 2-2 at Nordsjælland, so they have been competitive without winning. Trabzonspor (12th, six points) are third in the Turkish Süper Lig with the league's best goal difference, though they lost 1-0 at home to Freiburg last time. CSKA need a win to stay in the hunt for the play-offs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean a little higher: every one of CSKA's three games has produced at least three goals, and they have scored in all of them. Trabzonspor score freely in Turkey (24 goals in ten league games) and won 4-2 at KuPS.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, split evenly. I read nothing on either side's wide play that moves this.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. A full Balgarska Armia against a big Turkish club will be lively, but the number already sits fairly high and there is no referee yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.5 shots. Both sides have been attacking in their games, which fits a high count; nothing pushes me off the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. With both teams scoring regularly, a healthy count fits; I stay with the number.

401915807.overall: Early view: Panathinaikos (2nd, nine points) have won all three league-phase games and lead the Greek league with 20 goals for and four against in nine games. Nordsjælland (25th, two points) are fifth in Denmark and drew at Hearts and at home to CSKA before a 2-0 defeat at Monaco. The site's numbers make Nordsjælland slight favourites at home; on form I would rate Panathinaikos at least level.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean a little lower: Panathinaikos concede very little (four goals in nine league games, three in three European games) and Nordsjælland failed to score at Monaco. Panathinaikos's 5-1 at Kairat was the exception rather than their usual pattern.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, split evenly. I read nothing about either side's style that moves this, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, a little more for Panathinaikos. No referee is known yet and neither side's European games have been notably ill-tempered, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Nordsjælland at home will want the ball, while Panathinaikos have been efficient rather than shot-heavy; the number looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Without team news I see nothing to move it; Panathinaikos's tight defence argues slightly down, Nordsjælland's need to chase the game slightly up.

401915805.overall: Early view: Hajduk Split (13th, six points) beat Ajax 2-1 and won 1-0 at Thun before a surprise 1-0 defeat in Gibraltar against Lincoln Red Imps. Sint-Truiden (10th, seven points) are unbeaten in Europe with one goal conceded, but in Belgium they are 16th and lost three league games in a row between 11 October and 1 November, all high-scoring. A full Poljud should make this a demanding trip.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Hajduk's three European games produced three, one and one goals, and Sint-Truiden's 2-0, 1-0 and 1-1 show a team that defends far better in Europe than in their league.
